title: An automatic restart no longer steals the detail window
description:
An implementer finishes its bead, reports `done`, and the fleet view ends the session and starts a
fresh one for the next bead. That much is the design working. What it also does is throw the new
session into the detail window, over whatever the navigator was reading.

It happens roughly once an hour per implementer, unprompted, and with two or three of them running
it will interrupt something the navigator chose to look at.

## Where it comes from

`cerebro--supervise` handles `restart` by calling `cerebro--end-session` and then
`cerebro--launch` (`emacs/cerebro.el`). `cerebro--launch` spawns through
`cerebro--spawn-into-detail`, which exists precisely to put a new session in the detail window —
correct for `s`, where the navigator asked for that agent and expects to see it, and wrong here,
where nobody asked for anything.

So the restart inherits an intention that belongs to a keypress.

## What "in silence" should mean

Not quite "never touch the detail window". If the navigator *was* watching that agent, its session
buffer is about to be killed by `cerebro--end-session` and the window will show something else
regardless — putting the replacement there is continuity rather than theft. The distinction worth
implementing is:

- the detail window was showing that agent's session → show its replacement;
- the detail window was showing anything else → leave it alone.

Which of those two the navigator wants is worth confirming; "simply restart in silence" could also
mean the strict reading, where a restart never changes the detail window even if the buffer under it
has just been killed.

## Watch for

`cerebro--spawn-into-detail` does more than display: it binds `display-buffer-overriding-action` so
vterm cannot take the *selected* window, and wraps the spawn in `save-selected-window`. A silent
restart still needs both — a new session must not steal focus from the agent list either. Only the
"put it in the detail window" part is unwanted.

## Validation

Manual: select one agent in the detail window, then let a different implementer finish a bead and be
replaced. The detail window still shows what it did before. Then repeat while watching the
implementer that is being replaced, and confirm whatever was decided above.
design:
## Context

When an implementer reports `done`, the fleet view ends its session and starts a fresh one — and
the fresh session is thrown into the detail window, over whatever the navigator was reading.
`cerebro--supervise`'s `restart` branch calls `cerebro--end-session` then `cerebro--launch`, and
`cerebro--launch` always routes the new vterm through `cerebro--spawn-into-detail`, a function
built for the `s` keypress, where the navigator asked to see that agent. A restart inherits an
intention that belongs to a keypress.

Chosen behaviour (settled with the navigator): **continuity** — if the detail window was showing
the finished agent's own session, the replacement appears there (the buffer under the window is
about to be killed anyway; this is continuity, not theft); if it was showing anything else, the
restart touches no window. In both cases focus never leaves wherever the navigator is.

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`).
Line numbers are against cerebro `origin/main` at `30272fa` — and **this file is hot**: ah-b8o
(window-point fix in `cerebro--tick`) and ah-lyc (list widths) are planned/in flight against the
same file, and ah-axj/ah-4xl are queued behind them. Fetch cerebro main and rebase on whatever has
merged; none of them touch these functions, so conflicts should be textual at worst.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` (cerebro repo)

- **`cerebro--launch`** (line 879) gains an optional argument:

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--launch (agent &optional quiet)
  ```

  The only change inside: the spawn call. Today (line ~897):

  ```elisp
  (buffer (cerebro--spawn-into-detail
           session-name (lambda () (vterm session-name))))
  ```

  becomes

  ```elisp
  (buffer (if quiet
              (cerebro--spawn-quietly (lambda () (vterm session-name)))
            (cerebro--spawn-into-detail
             session-name (lambda () (vterm session-name)))))
  ```

  Everything after — the query-on-exit flag, `cerebro-session-mode`, the implementer note — is
  untouched and applies to both paths.

- **`cerebro--spawn-quietly`** — new, next to `cerebro--spawn-into-detail` (line 833):

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--spawn-quietly (spawn)
    "Run SPAWN without letting the buffer it makes keep any window.

  vterm displays its buffer via `pop-to-buffer-same-window', which would
  take the selected window.  `save-window-excursion' lets it do that and
  then puts every window back, so the session exists, its process runs,
  and nothing the navigator can see has changed.  Focus never moves for
  the same reason.  Returns SPAWN's buffer."
    (save-window-excursion (funcall spawn)))
  ```

  `save-window-excursion` rather than a `display-buffer-overriding-action` that returns no
  window: the no-window route depends on `pop-to-buffer` tolerating a nil window, which is
  version-sensitive, while restoring the configuration afterwards is unconditional. (See Known
  traps for the one cost.)

- **`cerebro--detail-showing-p`** — new, next to `cerebro--show-detail` (line 808):

  ```elisp
  (defun cerebro--detail-showing-p (agent)
    "Non-nil when the detail window is live and shows AGENT's session buffer."
    (and cerebro--detail-window
         (window-live-p cerebro--detail-window)
         (let ((buffer (get-buffer (cerebro--session-buffer-name agent))))
           (and buffer (eq (window-buffer cerebro--detail-window) buffer)))))
  ```

- **`cerebro--supervise`**, the `restart` branch (line 979). Today:

  ```elisp
  ('restart (cerebro--end-session agent)
            (cerebro--launch agent))
  ```

  becomes — **the check must run before the kill**, since after `cerebro--end-session` the
  window no longer shows the session:

  ```elisp
  ('restart (let ((watching (cerebro--detail-showing-p agent)))
              (cerebro--end-session agent)
              (cerebro--launch agent (not watching))))
  ```

- **`cerebro-start` (the `s` key) is untouched** — a requested start still lands in the detail
  window via the default (non-quiet) `cerebro--launch` path. Verify no other caller of
  `cerebro--launch` exists (at `30272fa` there are exactly the two: `cerebro-start` and the
  supervise restart).

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (cerebro repo)

Tests below; run `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` from
the cerebro root. Batch Emacs has a real frame, so window functions work; vterm does **not** load
in batch — the tests stub the launch layer and never call real `vterm` (the existing suite's
stubbing style, `cl-letf` on the function cells).

## Increments

1. **The predicate.** Failing test `cerebro-test/detail-showing-p-tracks-the-window`: with
   `cerebro--detail-window` bound to a window showing a buffer named as the agent's session
   buffer (`cerebro--session-buffer-name`), the predicate is non-nil; showing another buffer →
   nil; window dead or nil → nil. Then `cerebro--detail-showing-p`.
2. **Quiet spawn.** Failing test `cerebro-test/spawn-quietly-leaves-windows-alone`: record the
   window configuration (each window's buffer), call `cerebro--spawn-quietly` with a spawn that
   creates a buffer and `pop-to-buffer-same-window`s it (a stand-in for vterm's behaviour),
   assert every window shows the same buffer as before and the returned buffer exists. Then the
   function.
3. **The restart decision.** Failing test
   `cerebro-test/restart-is-quiet-unless-the-agent-was-watched`: `cl-letf` `cerebro--end-session`
   to a no-op recorder and `cerebro--launch` to record its `quiet` argument; drive
   `cerebro--supervise` with one agent whose action derives to `restart` (the existing supervise
   tests show the arrangement); with the detail window showing the agent's session buffer →
   launch called with `quiet` nil; showing something else → `quiet` non-nil; and the
   showing-check demonstrably ran before end-session (record call order). Then the branch edit
   and the `cerebro--launch` signature change.
4. **Delivery, two PRs** — the established cerebro shape (ah-b8o's plan, increment 3, is the
   template): (a) branch from cerebro `origin/main` in a worktree/clone of the cerebro repo —
   never inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared checkout — commit
   `fix(ah-aao): an automatic restart no longer steals the detail window`, PR to
   `rmstdope/cerebro`, `@copilot` review, merge on green; (b) atlantis-hud worktree bumps the
   submodule pointer, `feat(ah-aao): bump cerebro to the quiet restart`, normal PR flow. Close
   the bead only after the bump lands in atlantis-hud main.

## The test plan

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el`: the three tests above plus the existing suite, in batch.
- No atlantis-hud suites; the bump PR runs atlantis-hud CI as usual.

## User-facing decisions

One, settled with the navigator (question tool; no mockup — the surface is window behaviour, and
the two options were described exactly):

- **Continuity over strict silence**: a restart may (only) refresh a detail window that was
  showing the restarted agent's own session; it never touches a detail window showing anything
  else, and never moves focus. Strict silence — never touching the window even when its buffer
  was just killed under it — was offered and rejected: the window would fall to an arbitrary
  buffer and the navigator would re-select by hand.

## Out of scope

- The `s` key's behaviour (requested starts still open in the detail window — that intention is
  the keypress's).
- `cerebro--spawn-into-detail` itself — unchanged; the quiet path is a sibling, not a rewrite.
- Focus/selection behaviour of `cerebro--end-session`, the stop-flag flow, and `retire`.
- Anything in atlantis-hud application code.

## Validation

- ERT suite green in batch, new tests red-then-green in order.
- Human check, real fleet view with two implementers up: select agent A's session into the detail
  window, wait for agent B to finish a bead and restart — the detail window still shows A;
  then watch B itself and let it restart — the detail window shows B's fresh session; in both
  cases point stays where it was.

## Known traps

- **Check before kill.** `cerebro--detail-showing-p` is meaningless after `cerebro--end-session`
  has killed the buffer — the window will already show a replacement buffer. The `let` ordering
  in the restart branch is the fix's load-bearing line; increment 3's call-order assertion pins
  it.
- **`save-window-excursion` restores windows, not buffer existence** — exactly what is wanted;
  but it means the selected window *briefly* shows the new session during the spawn. In an
  interactive session this can flash for a frame. Accepted: the alternative
  (`display-buffer-no-window` + `allow-no-window`) depends on `pop-to-buffer` tolerating a
  windowless display, which varies by Emacs version; do not switch to it without testing on the
  navigator's Emacs.
- **vterm does not load in batch** — `cerebro--launch` `user-error`s without it. The tests stub
  `cerebro--launch`/spawn thunks and never touch real vterm; do not try to install vterm in CI.
- **The file is hot.** ah-b8o (`cerebro--tick`) and ah-lyc (formats/widths) land in the same file
  around the same time; fetch cerebro main before branching and rebase before the PR. No shared
  functions — conflicts, if any, are textual.
- **Two-PR delivery**: the fix is invisible to the running fleet until the submodule bump merges
  in atlantis-hud; the bead closes on the bump, not on the cerebro merge.
acceptance_criteria: When the fleet view replaces a finished implementer, the detail window keeps showing whatever it was showing, unless it was showing that agent's own session. Focus does not move: the navigator stays in whichever window they were in. Starting an agent with s still shows it in the detail window as it does today.

title: The whole row of an asking agent is emphasised in the fleet list
description:
Most of this already works, and the bead exists for the part that does not.

## What the fleet list does today

An agent blocked on a question the navigator has to answer shows the state `asking`, and
`emacs/cerebro.el` already marks it three ways:

- a `?` glyph in place of the status dot, in `warning` face;
- the word `asking` in the State column;
- **bold** on the Agent, Role and State columns.

Rendered:

    col 0 "? Storm"      bold
    col 1 "implementer"  bold
    col 2 "asking"       bold
    col 3 "ah-a1b"       not bold
    col 4 "16m"          not bold

## The gap

The navigator asked for the **entire row**. The Bead and For columns are not emphasised, so the row
trails off into normal weight at exactly the point where it says which bead is stuck and how long it
has been waiting — the two facts most worth reading once the row has caught the eye.

`cerebro--entry` applies `cerebro--emphasize` to three of the five columns. Extending it is small.
Making it *read* well may not be: bold across a full row in a narrow window is a heavier mark than
bold on a name, and the reason only three columns carry it today was to keep bold meaning "this row
wants you" without shouting.

## Worth confirming before building

Whether an implementer ever actually writes `asking` to its state file in practice. The
`implement-bead` skill instructs it to, before putting a question to the navigator, but if no agent
has yet done so then this whole signal has never fired for real and the first thing to fix is that,
not the styling.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- Whole row bold, or bold plus a background (`hl-line`-style) on the row, or the row in a face of
  its own so a theme can tune it?
- Should `done` — the other transient state — get any emphasis, or does bold stay exclusive to
  "needs you"?

## Validation

Manual: with an implementer in `asking`, confirm every column of its row is emphasised, and that a
`working` row beside it plainly is not.
design:
## Context

An agent in `asking` is blocked on the navigator, and the fleet list already marks it three ways:
the `?` glyph (warning face), the word `asking`, and **bold** on the Agent, Role and State columns
(`cerebro--emphasize`, keyed on `cerebro--wants-attention-p`, which is `(eq state 'asking)` —
`emacs/cerebro.el:216`). The Bead and For columns stay plain, so the row trails off into normal
weight exactly where it says which bead is stuck and for how long. The navigator chose: **bold the
whole row, and bold stays exclusive to `asking`** — no colour change, no emphasis for `done`.

**Cerebro submodule** (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`). Line numbers
against cerebro `origin/main` at `30272fa`. **The exact lines this bead edits are also edited by
ah-lyc** (planned, likely in flight): ah-lyc rewrites `bead-col` (external `—`, ellipsis
truncation) and shrinks the column widths. Fetch cerebro main first and build on whatever has
merged — if ah-lyc landed, wrap its versions of the cells; if not, expect a rebase.

One verification the bead itself asks for, kept cheap: the `asking` protocol exists end to end —
`implement-bead`'s skill instructs writing `asking` to the state file (SKILL.md:74, 235) and
`cerebro--derive` maps the string at `cerebro.el:129` — so this is styling, not plumbing. No
plumbing work is in scope; if a live implementer is seen never to reach `asking` in practice,
that is a separate bead against the implementer skill, not this one.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `emacs/cerebro.el` (cerebro repo)

`cerebro--entry` (lines ~236–257). `attention` is already computed (line ~244); apply
`cerebro--emphasize` to the last two cells exactly as the first three do:

- `bead-col` (~251–254): wrap the *whole* resulting string —
  `(cerebro--emphasize <today's cond expression> attention)`. This composes with ah-lyc's `—` and
  truncation unchanged: emphasize takes the finished string.
- `for-col` (~255): `(cerebro--emphasize (if external "" (cerebro--elapsed ...)) attention)` —
  emphasizing `""` is a no-op, so the external case needs no special path.

Nothing else changes: `cerebro--wants-attention-p` already excludes `done` (and everything else),
which is precisely the "asking only" decision.

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` (cerebro repo)

One test beside the existing entry tests (`cerebro-test/entry-working-implementer-shows-bead-and-elapsed`
and friends). Run: `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`.

## Increments

1. **Failing test.** `cerebro-test/entry-asking-emphasises-every-column` — build an `asking`
   agent with a bead and a since-time, call `cerebro--entry`, and assert all five cells of the
   vector carry the bold face that `cerebro--emphasize` applies, while the same agent in
   `working` has it on none. Read faces with `get-text-property 0 'face` (or the property
   `cerebro--emphasize` actually sets — read that function first and assert on what it does, not
   on an assumed `'bold`).
2. **The fix** — the two `cerebro--emphasize` wraps. Suite green.
3. **Delivery, two PRs** — the established cerebro shape (see ah-b8o's plan, increment 3, for the
   exact commands): cerebro-repo PR `fix(ah-axj): the whole row of an asking agent is emphasised`,
   `@copilot` review, merge; then the atlantis-hud submodule bump
   `feat(ah-axj): bump cerebro to the full-row asking emphasis`. If ah-lyc/ah-aao/ah-b8o are
   mid-flight in the same file, coordinate: rebase, and the bump PR may name several beads' shas —
   bump to the latest cerebro main containing this fix.

## The test plan

- `emacs/cerebro-test.el`: the new test plus the untouched suite, in batch.
- No atlantis-hud suites; the bump PR runs CI as usual.

## User-facing decisions

Settled with the navigator (question tool with rendered row previews; no HTML mockup — the
surface is a terminal table and the previews showed the exact rows):

1. **Bold across the whole row** — chosen over bold + warning-face colour (rejected: colours a
   full line of the list; the `?` glyph already carries the colour) and over a dedicated
   `cerebro-asking` face (rejected: same look today, one more moving part).
2. **`asking` only** — `done` stays plain; bold keeps meaning "this row wants you". Emphasising
   `done` was offered and rejected as diluting the signal.

## Out of scope

- Any change to `cerebro--wants-attention-p`, the glyphs, faces, or the `asking` state protocol.
- The bead panel's styling.
- Fixing an implementer that never writes `asking` (separate bead if observed).

## Validation

- ERT suite green in batch; the new test red before, green after.
- Human check, real fleet view: an implementer in `asking` shows every one of its five cells
  bold, including Bead and For; the `working` row beside it is plain; a `done` row is plain.

## Known traps

- **ah-lyc edits the same two expressions.** Its plan turns `(external)` into `—` and truncates
  long ids; this bead wraps whichever version is on main. The wrap-the-finished-string shape
  survives both orders; a mid-air collision is a rebase, not a redesign.
- **Assert on what `cerebro--emphasize` actually applies** — read it before writing the test;
  asserting a guessed face name fails against propertize details. ah-lyc's plan carries the same
  warning about faces and `substring-no-properties` for content assertions.
- **Emphasizing the empty string** (external's For cell) must stay harmless — it is, since
  `cerebro--emphasize` on `""` returns `""`; do not add a conditional for it.
- **Two-PR delivery** — the bead closes when the atlantis-hud submodule bump merges, not when
  the cerebro PR does.
acceptance_criteria: In the fleet list, every column of an agent in the asking state is emphasised, including Bead and For. A row in any other state carries no emphasis, so the mark still means "this one wants you". The ? glyph keeps its own colour rather than being repainted by the row emphasis.

title: Per-agent bd actor identity so two implementers cannot claim the same bead
description:
On 2026-08-14 ~22:55Z, Cyclops claimed ah-3cs and Storm — started 42 seconds later — claimed the same bead successfully sixteen seconds after Cyclops's claim landed. Both then built in the same worktree (.claude/worktrees/ah-3cs) until the navigator noticed and Storm was stood down.

Root cause: every agent on this machine runs under the same bd actor (the local git identity, Henrik Kurelid). `bd update --claim` is documented as idempotent when the bead is already claimed by you — so the second agent's claim returns success instead of exiting 13, and both sessions heartbeat the same lease, making the duplication invisible from the outside (the assignee reads identically either way).

Wanted: each implementer session claims under a distinct actor identity — e.g. the launcher (.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer and the cmux launch path) exporting the agent name as bd's user/actor before the session starts — so a second claim on an already-claimed bead fails (exit 13) and the agent picks different work or waits. Note --if-assignee cannot combine with --claim, so identity is the mechanism, not guard flags. Also worth covering: what Cerebro's sweeps and bd reclaim see once assignees carry agent names instead of a human name.

Urgency argument: this silently doubles work and corrupts a shared worktree whenever two implementers start near-simultaneously with a short queue — exactly the normal fleet-startup case.
design:
## Context

On 2026-08-14 ~22:55Z Cyclops claimed ah-3cs and Storm, started 42 seconds later, claimed the same
bead successfully and both built in the same worktree until the navigator stood Storm down. Root
cause: every session on this machine runs bd as the same actor — bd's global `--actor` flag defaults
to `$BEADS_ACTOR`, then `git user.name` ("Henrik Kurelid"), then `$USER` — and `bd update --claim`
is idempotent when the bead is already claimed *by you*, so the second claim succeeded silently and
both sessions heartbeated one lease.

**The fix is one mechanism**: the launchers export `BEADS_ACTOR=<agent name>` before `exec claude`,
so every bd invocation inside a launched session carries that agent's identity. Both implementer
launch paths funnel through `scripts/run-implementer` (the terminal invocation, and the Emacs fleet
view — `cerebro--launch-command`, `emacs/cerebro.el:267-278`, returns that script plus the name), so
one export covers both. The bead description's mention of a "cmux launch path" is stale — nothing
named cmux exists anywhere in the repository or the submodule.

**Verified behaviour with distinct actors** (planner ran this experiment against the live bd on
2026-08-15, scratch bead ah-dzj, since closed):

- `BEADS_ACTOR=Storm bd update <id> --claim` on a bead held by Cyclops → **exit 1**, stderr
  `Error updating <id>: issue already claimed by Cyclops`. (The bead description guessed exit 13;
  that code belongs to `--if-assignee`/`--if-status` guard mismatches, not to claim contention.
  Claim contention is exit 1 — test against that.)
- Re-claim by the same actor → exit 0, idempotent, unchanged.
- `assignee` reads the actor name (`Cyclops`), and `BEADS_ACTOR=Storm bd heartbeat <id>` on
  Cyclops's bead → exit 1, `heartbeat <id>: issue already claimed by Cyclops`.
- `bd unclaim` by the holder → exit 0.

The consumer-side workflow already handles a failing claim — atlantis-hud's CLAUDE.md: "If the
claim fails, another agent won it: pick a different bead." That instruction was dead code while all
actors were one; this bead makes it live. No skill or agent-prompt change is needed for the
implementer's reaction.

All code changes live in the **cerebro submodule** (`rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at
`.claude/cerebro`), plus one submodule-bump commit in atlantis-hud.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

All paths below are inside the submodule checkout, i.e. `.claude/cerebro/` from the consumer root.

**1. `scripts/run-implementer`** — after the roster validation succeeds (the `if [[ -z "$on_roster" ]]`
block ends at the `exit 2`; the `exec claude \` sits at the bottom of the file), add immediately
before the `exec`:

```bash
# Every bd call in this session acts as this implementer, not as the machine's git identity.
# Distinct actors are what make a second claim on a held bead fail instead of aliasing into the
# first (bd's --actor default chain: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER).
export BEADS_ACTOR="$on_roster"
```

`$on_roster`, not `$name`: it is the canonical spelling from the ROSTER array, so a future
looser-matching change can never leak a miscased actor. The `--roster` early-exit branch is above
this and unaffected. `exec` preserves the environment, and every `Bash` tool subshell inside the
claude session inherits it — nothing else needs to carry the name.

**2. The four role launchers** — same one-line export, hard-coded to the session's fixed name,
immediately before each `exec claude`:

- `scripts/run-planner` (execs with `--name Xavier`) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Xavier"`
- `scripts/run-orchestrator` (`--name Cerebro`, exec at line 31) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Cerebro"`
- `scripts/run-user-feedback` (`--name Moira`, exec at line 23) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Moira"`
- `scripts/run-psylocke` (`--name Psylocke`, exec at line 24) → `export BEADS_ACTOR="Psylocke"`

These roles never claim, but their bd writes (priorities, labels, closes, reopens) enter the audit
trail, and an audit line reading `Xavier` instead of the navigator's own name is the difference
between "an agent did this" and "the human did this". A bead claimed by hand in the navigator's own
shell keeps reading `Henrik Kurelid`, which is now a meaningful signal rather than the only value.

**3. `tests/launchers.sh`** — new file, the submodule's first shell test (there is no test harness
for scripts today; the only suite is ERT for the elisp, run per `CLAUDE.md`). Plain bash, no
framework, `set -euo pipefail`, exit non-zero on first failure, runnable from the submodule root as
`bash tests/launchers.sh`. It must not start a real session: put a stub `claude` executable first on
`PATH` in a temp dir —

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# stub claude: prove what environment and args the launcher hands over
printf 'BEADS_ACTOR=%s\n' "${BEADS_ACTOR:-<unset>}"
printf 'ARG:%s\n' "$@"
```

— then assert:

- `run-implementer Cyclops` output contains `BEADS_ACTOR=Cyclops`;
- `run-implementer storm` still exits 2 and mentions `Storm` (the existing miscased-name message —
  pins that the export did not move above validation);
- `run-implementer --roster` prints exactly the fourteen names and never reaches the stub
  (unchanged behaviour);
- each of the four role launchers' output contains its fixed `BEADS_ACTOR=<Name>`;
- `run-implementer Cyclops` output does **not** contain `BEADS_ACTOR=<unset>`.

**4. `agents/orchestrator.md`** — the claims-sweep prose that this fix falsifies, lines 295-305:
"**But the assignee name is not proof of who holds a claim…** Every claim made from this machine is
stamped with the local git identity … `assignee: Henrik Kurelid` can mean the …". Rewrite that
paragraph to the new truth: a claim from a launched session is stamped with the agent's roster
name; `assignee: Henrik Kurelid` (or any non-roster name) now specifically means a claim made by
hand outside a launched session — still check the lease before touching it, since a claim from
before this change, or from a stale session started off the old launchers, predates the naming.

  claimed by Henrik Kurelid". Land the bump when no bead is `in_progress`
  (`bd list --status in_progress --json` must be empty), or have the navigator `bd unclaim` the
  stragglers first. Running sessions keep their old identity until restarted; the fleet view
  restarts implementers between beads, so one bead-cycle after the bump the fleet is clean.

  for `--name <Name>` (`emacs/cerebro.el`, `cerebro--system-args` consumers); `BEADS_ACTOR` is
  additional, not a replacement.
- **Emacs backup files (`*.el~`, `*.sh~`) are committed in the cerebro repo** — never edit them,
  and do not "clean them up" in this PR.

title: Psylocke verifies merged work with the navigator; failures reopen at P0
description:
# Summary

Nothing checks that merged work does what it was supposed to do. A bead is planned, built under TDD,
reviewed by Copilot, merged and closed — and every one of those steps is an agent judging its own
work against its own description of it. Whether the bug is actually gone, or the feature actually
does what the navigator pictured, nobody asks.

**Psylocke is a fifth role: the verification session.** Interactive, like Xavier and Moira, because
verification is something only the navigator can do — she prepares it, sets it up, launches the
application, and records the verdict.

# What Psylocke does

A pass, then a ten-minute sleep, then another — the shape Moira already uses.

1. **Find what has merged and is not yet verified.** Beads closed since the last pass, whose commit
   is on main.
2. **Decide whether it is worth verifying at all**, and this is the first judgement she makes.
   **Only changes to the application are verified.** A bead that touched `.claude/`, `docs/`, a
   skill, a script or CI has nothing a player can look at, and asking the navigator to launch the app
   for one wastes the very attention this role exists to spend carefully. A bead that touched
   `packages/`, `crates/` or `apps/` is a candidate.
3. **Prepare everything that can be prepared before asking for anything.** Read the bead — what it
   claimed to fix or add, its acceptance criteria, the plan's *User-facing decisions* — and work out
   what the navigator will have to do, which fixtures or reports they will need, and which shell to
   launch. The navigator's time starts when they say yes, not before.
4. **Ask whether they are ready.** Not "here is a bead", but a prepared session waiting on a yes.
5. **On yes: brief, then launch.** Say what is to be verified and how to tell success from failure,
   name the reports or orders to load and where they are, then launch the application — **desktop or
   web depending on what the change touches**, and both, in turn, for something that genuinely
   differs between them.
6. **Take the verdict.** The navigator says whether it holds. Two outcomes: verified, or back for
   rework.

# The verdict, and what it does to the bead

- **Verified** — label it and move on. That is the end of the bead's life.
- **Failed** — the bead is **reopened** (`bd reopen`, which exists) with what the navigator saw,
  goes back through planning or straight to an implementer depending on why it failed, and is
  verified again once it re-merges.

**A reopened bead becomes P0, automatically** — decided by the navigator. It is on main and not
working as intended, which is the most urgent thing the repository can contain: shipped, wrong, and
in front of the player. So `bd update <id> --priority=0` is part of reopening, not a separate
question.

This is a **standing exception to "never set a priority the navigator did not choose"**, and it has
to be written into `planner.md` and `beads-workflow` as such, beside the existing exception for a
split epic's children. The rule exists so that ranking stays the navigator's; here they have ranked
this class of bead once, in advance, and the agents apply it. Xavier's P0 pre-emption then does the
rest: a reopened bead is planned on the pass it appears, ahead of a full buffer.

This is the part that reaches every other role, and is most of the work in this bead: **a reopened
bead is a state the harness has never had.** Today closed is terminal. What has to be decided and
then written into the other four agent files:

- **What labels carry it.** A scheme is needed for "needs verification", "verified" and "verification
  not needed", and the exact names are a decision to take once and apply everywhere. `bd set-state`
  also exists and may be the better instrument than raw labels — that is the planner's call.
- **What an implementer does with a reopened bead.** It is closed-then-open again, may already carry
  `planned`, and its plan describes work that is partly done. Does it go back to Xavier, or straight
  to the fleet? Probably it depends on whether the failure was in the plan or in the build, and the
  agent files have to say which.
- **What Xavier does with one.** A reopened bead with a plan that turned out to be wrong is not the
  same as an unplanned bead, and it should not be re-planned from scratch.
- **What Cerebro reports.** Anything merged and unverified belongs in its status and release
  reports. **It does not block a release** — decided with the navigator: Cerebro names what is
  unverified when cutting one and the navigator decides. A hard gate would stop everything for one
  bead.
- **What Moira tells a reporter.** Her five states end at `RELEASED`. A verification step sits
  between `MERGED` and `RELEASED`, and a bead reopened after a failed verification means an issue she
  has already told "merged" is not finished — she must not report progress that has been taken back.

# Psylocke joins the roster, and leaves the other one

**`Psylocke` must come out of `IMPLEMENTER_NAMES`** (`scripts/runImplementer.ts:61-77`, currently
fifteen X-Men). The list is closed on purpose — Cerebro picks the next unused name from it and looks
for running implementers by it — so a name that is both an implementer and the verification session
would have Cerebro looking for the wrong process and two roles answering to one name.

Removing it is a one-line change plus whatever tests assert the roster's contents; check for a live
`.claude/implementers/Psylocke.*` flag file first.

She also needs **`scripts/run-psylocke`**, alongside `run-planner`, `run-orchestrator` and
`run-user-feedback` — interactive, with the same shape: `exec claude --agent verifier --name Psylocke`
with a starting prompt. And `.claude/agents/verifier.md`, written the way the other four are.

# Scope

- The `verifier` agent definition and its launcher.
- Psylocke off the implementer roster.
- The verification label scheme, applied consistently, and the reopen workflow written into
  `planner.md`, `implementer.md` / `implement-bead`, `orchestrator.md` and `user-feedback.md`, plus
  `beads-workflow` for the lifecycle and CLAUDE.md for the summary of the five roles.
- Whatever preparation Psylocke can do mechanically: identifying the shell to launch, naming the
  fixtures, and launching the application.

# Out of scope

- Automating the verification itself. The point of this role is that a person looks at the thing.
- Blocking a release on verification — decided against above.
- Verifying anything already merged before this ships. Where the backlog starts is the navigator's
  call at the first pass, not a migration.

# Known traps

- **`bd` closed is not terminal any more.** Several places assume it is — Cerebro closes a bead whose
  work is on main, Moira reads `closed` as `MERGED`, and the implementer's parent-closing walk treats
  a closed child as done. Each needs re-reading against a bead that can come back.
- **A reopened child of an epic can reopen the epic.** The parent was closed because its last child
  closed; if that child returns, the epic's closure was premature.
- **The launch is the navigator's machine, not CI.** Desktop means a Tauri dev build; web means the
  vite dev server. Both take minutes on a cold cache, which is preparation to do *before* asking
  whether they are ready, not after they have said yes.
- **The fixtures are in `tests/fixtures/reports/`** and its README names the consecutive-turn pairs
  — that is where "which report should I load" is answered from, rather than by inventing one.
- **Interactive by necessity.** Like Xavier and Moira and unlike an implementer, this session must
  put a question in front of the navigator and wait; `--print` cannot do that.

# Validation

- The five roles are consistent: every agent file describes what it does with a reopened bead and
  the verification labels, and none of them contradicts another.
- `Psylocke` is gone from the roster, its tests pass, and `scripts/run-implementer Psylocke` fails
  with the roster message.
- A real round: merge something small and user-visible, let Psylocke find it, prepare it and launch
  the app; verify it and confirm the bead is labelled; then fail one deliberately and confirm it
  reopens and reappears where the plan says it should.
- A harness-only bead merged in the same period is correctly judged not worth verifying, and the
  navigator is never asked about it.
design:
## Context

Nothing checks that merged work does what it claimed: every step from plan to merge is an agent
judging its own work. This bead adds a fifth role, **Psylocke, the verification session** —
interactive, because only the navigator can verify — plus the *reopen workflow* that a failed
verification triggers, written consistently into every other role. Closed stops being terminal.

**This work lands in two repositories, and that shapes everything below.** The fleet was migrated
into the **cerebro submodule** (atlantis-hud commit `8049f17`, PR #231; cerebro repo
`github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at `.claude/cerebro`). The bead's original description
cites `scripts/runImplementer.ts:61-77` — **that file no longer exists**: `run-implementer` was
rewritten in bash (cerebro PR #3) and the roster is now a bash array. All agent files, skills,
launchers and the Emacs fleet view live in the cerebro repo; atlantis-hud carries only symlinks
(`.claude/agents/*.md` → `.claude/cerebro/agents/*.md`), its own CLAUDE.md (a symlink to
`.github/copilot-instructions.md`), and the submodule pointer.

So the delivery is **two PRs, in order**: PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro` with almost all the work;
PR 2 to atlantis-hud bumping the submodule, updating the consumer CLAUDE.md, and committing the new
agent symlink. The recent history shows exactly this pattern (cerebro PRs #1–#5, then atlantis-hud
"Bump cerebro to the migrated launchers").

Decisions already taken by the navigator, recorded at filing (do not re-ask):
- Psylocke polls on a ten-minute cycle, like Moira.
- An unverified bead does **not** block a release; Cerebro names what is unverified when cutting
  one and the navigator decides.
- A reopened bead is **automatically P0** — a standing exception to "never set a priority the
  navigator did not choose".

Decisions taken by the navigator during planning (see *User-facing decisions*): Moira posts
VERIFIED and REOPENED comments; Psylocke offers a third verdict, *passed with follow-up*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Design decisions bound into the files

**Verification state is a `bd set-state` dimension, not raw labels.** `bd set-state <id>
verification=<value> --reason "..."` atomically swaps the `verification:<value>` label and records
an event bead — an audit trail for free. The dimension is `verification`; the values:

| value | meaning | set by |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | merged, touches the app, selected for verification, awaiting the verdict | Psylocke, when it selects a candidate |
| `passed` | the navigator verified it | Psylocke, on a passed verdict |
| `failed` | the navigator failed it; set at reopen time and **kept through the rebuild** | Psylocke, on a failed verdict |
| `not-needed` | harness/docs/CI-only — nothing a player can look at | Psylocke, silently, during a pass |

A bead re-merged after rework closes still carrying `verification:failed`, which is what makes it a
candidate again — the work-list query below treats `failed` as "verify again".

**Psylocke's work list** (steady state): closed beads with either no `verification:*` label or
`verification:failed`, whose commits are on `origin/main`:

```bash
bd list --status closed --json | jq -r '.[]
  | select(([.labels[]? | select(startswith("verification:"))] | length == 0)
           or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed")))
  | .id'
# per id — did it land, and what did it touch:
git log origin/main --grep "(<id>):" --oneline
git show --stat --format= <sha>
```

A bead is *application-touching* iff any changed path matches `^(packages|crates|apps)/`
(all three directories exist at the atlantis-hud root). Anything else —
`.claude/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `.github/`, config — gets `verification=not-needed`
without the navigator ever being asked. `labels` is a plain string array in `bd` JSON (verified).

**The first-pass backlog cutoff** is the navigator's call at Psylocke's first pass (per the bead's
out-of-scope). Mechanism: at the first pass ever (detectable: no bead anywhere carries a
`verification:*` label), ask the navigator for the cutoff, then bulk-mark every closed bead on the
far side of it in one command — `bd label add <id> <id> ... verification:not-needed` (ids first,
label last — verified syntax; there are 67 closed beads today, so this is one short command). After
that the steady-state query above is stateless and restart-safe. `verifier.md` carries this.

**The reopen procedure**, verbatim in `verifier.md` — this is the exact sequence, in this order:

```bash
bd reopen <id> --reason "<what the navigator saw, one line>"
bd update <id> --priority=0 --append-notes "Verification failed (<date>): <what the navigator saw, in full>"
bd set-state <id> verification=failed --reason "failed verification"
# only if the navigator said the PLAN was wrong (see verdict flow below):
bd update <id> --remove-label planned
# if the bead's parent (or grandparent) is closed, reopen the chain:
bd reopen <parent> --reason "child <id> reopened by failed verification"
bd dolt push
```

`bd reopen` exists and takes `--reason` (verified). P0 is set by Psylocke without asking — the
standing exception. **Build-failure vs plan-failure is the navigator's call, made at verdict time**:
Psylocke asks "is the plan wrong, or the build?" as part of taking a failed verdict. Build failure
(the default): `planned` stays, the bead goes straight back to `bd ready` as an unclaimed P0 and the
fleet picks it up. Plan failure: `planned` is removed, and Xavier's P0 pre-emption plans it on the
next pass.

**The three verdicts** (navigator decision, see *User-facing decisions*): **passed** →
`verification=passed`; **passed with follow-up** → `verification=passed` *and* Psylocke files a new
bead for the niggle at **P4** (`bd create ... -p 4`, the ordinary creation rule — it is new,
unranked work, and Xavier triages it normally; put "found during verification of <id>" in the
description); **failed** → the reopen procedure above.

**Launch commands** (verified against the repo):
- Web: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev` — vite on its default port (5173), after a wasm build.
- Desktop: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec tauri dev` — Tauri v2; its `beforeDevCommand`
  (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:9`) starts vite on 4174 `--strictPort` itself.
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/reports/README.md` names the consecutive-turn pairs and the naming
  scheme — that is where "which report to load" is answered from.
- Both `dev` scripts run `build:wasm` first, which is minutes on a cold cache — warm it **before**
  asking whether the navigator is ready (run the dev server up once, or at least
  `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core build:wasm`), never after the yes.

**Psylocke has no state file.** Interactive agents' liveness is inferred from `--name` in process
args (`cerebro.el`, "Interactive agents have no state file"). The launcher must pass
`--name Psylocke`; nothing writes to `.claude/implementers/` (no `Psylocke.*` file exists there
today — verified).

### Cerebro repo (`github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at `.claude/cerebro`) — PR 1

**New: `agents/verifier.md`.** Frontmatter matching `agents/user-feedback.md`'s shape:

```yaml
---
name: verifier
description: Psylocke, the verification session for atlantis-hud. Walks beads merged since her last pass, judges which touched the application, prepares each verification before asking for the navigator's time, launches the right shell with the right fixtures, and records the verdict — passed, passed with a follow-up bead, or failed, which reopens the bead at P0 and sends it back to the fleet. Started by `.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-psylocke`, and interactive by design.
model: sonnet
---
```

Body in the house style of the other four (open with **"You are Psylocke." Say so in your first
message**, same rationale sentence), covering, in order: (1) the pass cycle — pass, ten-minute sleep
in two five-minute halves that print each minute (copy the sleep loop from `plan-bead`'s "Sleeping
without dying"), pass again, until the navigator ends it; `bd dolt pull` at the top of each pass;
(2) the work-list query, the app-touching classification and the silent `not-needed` marking, all
as specified above; (3) the first-pass cutoff conversation and bulk backfill; (4) preparation
before asking — read the bead's description, acceptance criteria and the plan's *User-facing
decisions*, find its PR and commits, choose the shell (desktop, web, or both in turn when the change
genuinely differs between them), choose fixtures from the README, write the briefing, warm the wasm
build; (5) the readiness question — a prepared session waiting on a yes, via the question tool; if
the navigator is away or says later, the bead simply stays `verification:pending` and is re-offered
at most once per pass — **no `human` label, nothing is blocked, pending waits**; (6) briefing and
launching — say what is being verified, how to tell success from failure, which reports to load and
from where, then start the app; (7) the verdict question — passed / passed with follow-up / failed,
and on failed the plan-or-build question and the reopen procedure, both verbatim; (8) what Psylocke
never does — never claims, never touches code, never sets a priority outside the standing P0
exception, never posts to GitHub (Moira owns the inbox), never verifies anything herself: the point
of the role is that a person looks at the thing; (9) `bd dolt push` after every state change and at
the end of every pass.

**New: `scripts/run-psylocke`.** Copy the shape of `scripts/run-user-feedback` (same header
structure, same `set -euo pipefail`, same "extra arguments go to claude" comment, no `--model` —
like Moira it takes the default). Executable bit set. The exec:

```bash
exec claude \
  --agent verifier \
  --name Psylocke \
  --permission-mode auto \
  "$@" \
  "You are Psylocke, the verifier. Follow your agent definition. Start now: pull the beads, find
what has merged unverified, mark what a player could never see as not needed, and prepare the rest.
Bring me one verification at a time, ready to run — say what I am checking, how to tell success
from failure, and which reports to load — then launch the application and take my verdict. A
failure reopens the bead at P0. Then tell me what you did and sleep."
```

**`scripts/run-implementer`** — remove `Psylocke` from the `ROSTER` array (lines 36–40; 15 → 14
names), and fix the header comment `--roster    # the fifteen names, one per line` (line ~6) to say
fourteen. The miscased-name hint and roster-message behaviour need no code change — a removed name
simply falls through to "not on the roster".

**`emacs/cerebro.el`** — three point changes plus docstrings:
- `cerebro-interactive-agents` (just after the `;;; The interactive roster` header, line ~41): add
  `("Psylocke" . "verifier")` as the fourth entry; docstring "The three interactive agents" → four.
- `cerebro--role-launch-commands` (lines 259–263): add `("verifier" . "run-psylocke")`.
- File-header comment (line ~20) "the fifteen implementer names" and the `cerebro--roster`
  docstring "The fifteen implementer names" (line ~335) → fourteen.
Keep all logic in the pure core — both changes are data in existing defconsts, nothing impure moves.

**`emacs/cerebro-test.el`** — `cerebro-roster-fixture` (lines ~163–166): remove `"Psylocke"`
(15 → 14). The nearby test asserting 18 `tabulated-list-entries` **still passes by coincidence**
(3+15 = 4+14 = 18) — tighten it to assert composition, not just count. New tests per Increment 1.

**`agents/orchestrator.md`** — four edits:
- Line 169's name list (`Iceman · Beast · Jubilee · Psylocke · ...`): remove Psylocke; fix any
  "fifteen" nearby.
- *Beads that finished without being closed* (section at line ~249): add the guard — **a bead
  carrying `verification:failed` is never sweep-closed.** It is a reopened bead being rebuilt; its
  old commits are on `origin/main` by definition, so the `git log --grep "(<id>):"` test proves
  nothing about the rework. Report it instead of closing it.
- Status and release reporting: the "what shipped" reports name **merged-but-unverified** beads —
  closed, application-touching, carrying neither `verification:passed` nor `verification:not-needed`.
  When cutting a release, list them and let the navigator decide; **verification does not gate the
  release** (navigator's decision, recorded in the bead).
- The epic sweep: add one sentence of awareness — Psylocke reopens a closed parent chain when
  reopening a child, and the implementer's close-walk re-closes it; the sweep must not fight either
  (its existing "all children closed" condition already prevents that — say so).

**`agents/planner.md`** — beside "Never set a priority the navigator did not choose" (line ~109):
the standing exception — a bead reopened by a failed verification is set to P0 by Psylocke as part
of reopening; the navigator ranked this class once, in advance. Plus a short paragraph: a reopened
bead arriving unplanned (its `planned` label removed because the plan was wrong) is a P0 with an
existing design and a recorded failure — amend, don't rewrite (details in `plan-bead`).

**`skills/plan-bead/SKILL.md`** — a short subsection under *P0 pre-empts the buffer*: a reopened
bead that reaches you has `verification:failed`, notes beginning "Verification failed", and a full
existing design including the interview record. Read the failure, update the existing plan in place
(keep all eight headings and the interview record; revise the sections the failure touches; note
what the verification found under *Context*), re-add `planned`. Never re-open user-facing questions
the navigator already answered unless the failure was about exactly that answer.

**`agents/implementer.md`** — no change to the state-file contract. One paragraph in the working
rules: a reopened bead is picked up like any other (it is open, `planned`, P0, and appears in
`bd ready`).

**`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`** — a subsection near the pickup (lines ~256–271): how to
recognise a reopened bead (`verification:failed` label, notes with "Verification failed", closed
history) and what changes: read the original PR(s) (`git log origin/main --grep "(<id>):"`) and the
failure notes before the plan; the first failing test reproduces what the navigator saw, where it is
testable at all; the scope is making the plan's promise true, not rebuilding the bead; on merge,
close it again as normal — it keeps `verification:failed`, which is what re-queues it for Psylocke.
The parent-close walk is unchanged (Psylocke reopened the parent; closing the last open child
closes it again).

**`agents/user-feedback.md`** — the ladder grows and the marker rule changes:
- Frontmatter description and the state table (lines 197–201): the ladder becomes
  `CREATED, PLANNED, CLAIMED, MERGED, VERIFIED, RELEASED`, plus `REOPENED` outside the ladder.
  New rows: `VERIFIED` — the bead is closed **and** carries `verification:passed`; `REOPENED` — the
  bead is open or in_progress again **and** carries `verification:failed`, after having been told
  MERGED. For a closed bead the state is computed by precedence: RELEASED if the commit is in a
  release tag, else VERIFIED if `verification:passed`, else MERGED. A `verification:not-needed`
  bead never sees VERIFIED and goes MERGED → RELEASED as today.
- The marker rule (lines ~243–246): **"once each, ever" becomes "post when the current state
  differs from the last posted marker"** — take the *last* `beads-state:` marker in the thread
  (the existing grep, keeping only the final match), not the set of all markers. This is what lets
  a MERGED → REOPENED → MERGED cycle post each transition without ever repeating a state
  consecutively. If verification passed between passes, posting VERIFIED without a second MERGED is
  correct — VERIFIED implies merged.
- Per-state guidance (the bullets at lines ~287–303), two new entries in the same style —
  guidance, not fixed strings, since Moira writes each comment for its issue:
  **VERIFIED** — a person has run the application and confirmed the change does what this issue
  asked; still unreleased unless RELEASED has also been reached. **REOPENED** — verification found
  the change does not fully hold; say what was observed, that the earlier "merged" no longer
  stands, and that it is back in work at top priority.
- *Closing on RELEASED* (lines ~305–310) is unchanged — release is not gated on verification.

**`CLAUDE.md`** (cerebro's own) — "Four roles" (line 34) becomes five, with a Psylocke/verifier
bullet in the style of the others; "three interactive agents" and "fifteen implementers" (line ~77)
updated; the invariants list gains one line: *closed is not terminal — a failed verification reopens
a bead at P0, and the roles above describe what each does with one.*

**`docs/agent-workflow.md`** — a section for the human: starting Psylocke
(`.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-psylocke`), what a verification session asks of you and roughly what
it costs, the three verdicts, and what a failed one sets in motion.

### atlantis-hud repo — PR 2

- **Submodule bump**: `.claude/cerebro` to the merged PR-1 sha.
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`** — this is what `CLAUDE.md` symlinks to; **edit the target,
  not the symlink**. Add a Psylocke paragraph to the roles section (after Moira's, same register:
  what she does, how she is started, that a failed verification reopens the bead at P0 and what
  each role does with a reopened bead in one sentence each); change "All four roles are defined in
  `.claude/agents/`" to five.
- **`.claude/agents/verifier.md` symlink** — created by running
  `.claude/cerebro/scripts/sync-symlinks.sh` from the worktree root after the bump; the existing
  four agent symlinks are tracked in git (verified with `git ls-files`), so commit the new one.

### What to reuse

- `scripts/run-user-feedback` — the launcher template, near-verbatim.
- `agents/user-feedback.md` — the pass/sleep/report session shape and the house prose style.
- `plan-bead`'s "Sleeping without dying" loop — verbatim into `verifier.md`.
- `bd set-state` / `bd reopen` / `bd label add <ids...> <label>` — all verified to exist with these
  signatures; invent no new mechanism.

## Increments

Increments 1–6 are one branch and one PR in the **cerebro repo**; 7 is the atlantis-hud PR.
Branching for PR 1 must not touch the shared submodule checkout — use a worktree of the *submodule's*
repo, placed under the consumer's `.claude/worktrees/` (run from the atlantis-hud root):

```bash
git -C .claude/cerebro fetch origin main
git -C .claude/cerebro worktree add -b ah-7s7-verifier "$PWD/.claude/worktrees/ah-7s7-cerebro" origin/main
```

1. **Psylocke becomes an interactive agent in the fleet view** (elisp, TDD — cerebro's CLAUDE.md
   mandates it and says run to completion without per-phase approval). Opening failing tests, in
   `emacs/cerebro-test.el`:
   - `cerebro-test/interactive-roster-has-psylocke` — `(assoc "Psylocke" cerebro-interactive-agents)`
     equals `("Psylocke" . "verifier")` and the alist has four entries.
   - `cerebro-test/launch-command-verifier` — `cerebro--launch-command` on an interactive
     `cerebro-agent` with role `"verifier"` returns `".claude/cerebro/scripts/run-psylocke"`.
   - Amend `cerebro-roster-fixture` to 14 names (no Psylocke) and tighten the 18-entry test to also
     assert Psylocke appears exactly once, as an interactive row.
   GREEN: the two defconst additions and docstring updates in `cerebro.el`.
2. **Psylocke off the implementer roster** — edit `ROSTER` and the header comment in
   `scripts/run-implementer`. No unit harness for bash; the opening check is the validation pair
   run before and after: `scripts/run-implementer --roster | wc -l` (15 → 14) and
   `scripts/run-implementer Psylocke; echo $?` (starts a session → exits 2 with the roster message).
3. **`scripts/run-psylocke`** — new file as specified, `chmod +x`; `bash -n scripts/run-psylocke`
   clean.
4. **`agents/verifier.md`** — new file per the content spec above.
5. **The reopen workflow written into every role** — the edits to `orchestrator.md`, `planner.md`,
   `plan-bead/SKILL.md`, `implementer.md`, `implement-bead/SKILL.md`, `user-feedback.md`, exactly as
   specified in *Files to change*.
6. **Roll-up docs** — cerebro `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/agent-workflow.md`. Then the PR: run the full
   ert suite, push the branch to `origin` (the cerebro repo's own origin), open the PR with
   `gh pr create -R rmstdope/cerebro`, request Copilot
   (`gh pr edit <n> -R rmstdope/cerebro --add-reviewer @copilot`), answer every comment, merge.
   **The cerebro repo has no CI** (no `.github/workflows/` — verified), so paste the ert run's
   output into the PR body; the review is the only other gate. Then remove the cerebro worktree
   (`git -C .claude/cerebro worktree remove --force ...` from the atlantis-hud root, then
   `git -C .claude/cerebro worktree prune`).
7. **The consumer PR** — ordinary implement-bead worktree of atlantis-hud from `origin/main`; inside
   it `git submodule update --init .claude/cerebro`, then in the submodule fetch and check out the
   merged PR-1 sha; edit `.github/copilot-instructions.md`; run
   `.claude/cerebro/scripts/sync-symlinks.sh`; commit the pointer, the doc and the new
   `.claude/agents/verifier.md` symlink. Normal PR, Copilot review, green checks, merge, close the
   bead.

## The test plan

- **ert (cerebro repo)**: `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit`
  — the whole suite, green, with the three new/tightened tests of Increment 1. This is the only
  automated suite the cerebro repo has, and the only code in this bead that has one.
- **Script checks**: the Increment 2 pair (`--roster` count and the exit-2 on `Psylocke`), and
  `bash -n` on `run-psylocke`.
- **atlantis-hud suites**: PR 2 touches no application code, so CI's normal checks are the gate;
  nothing new to write.
- **The real round** (bead Validation, run by the navigator with Psylocke after merge, not by the
  implementer): one bead verified and labelled; one deliberately failed and observed to reopen at
  P0 and reappear in `bd ready`; one harness-only bead judged `not-needed` without the navigator
  being asked.

## User-facing decisions

No player-visible UI — no mockups. The user-facing surface is Moira's GitHub comments (read by real
reporters) and the verdict flow the navigator will live with. Asked and decided in this planning
session:

1. **"Should Moira post a VERIFIED status comment on the linked issue?"** — **Yes** (recommended
   option chosen). Rejected: staying silent until RELEASED — less noise, but the reporter never
   learns a person confirmed the fix.
2. **"Should Moira post a REOPENED comment when a merged bead fails verification?"** — **Yes**
   (recommended option chosen). Rejected: silent rework — avoids alarming the reporter, but leaves
   the thread saying "merged" while that has been taken back.
3. **"Should Psylocke offer a third verdict for a small niggle on a working feature?"** — **Yes:
   passed-with-follow-up** — the bead passes and the niggle becomes a new P4 bead triaged normally
   (recommended option chosen). Rejected: binary passed/failed, which either escalates a cosmetic
   niggle to a P0 reopen or loses it entirely.

Decided at filing by the navigator (not re-asked): ten-minute polling; release not gated on
verification; automatic P0 on reopen. The comments' exact texts are deliberately guidance-style,
not fixed strings — that is how every existing Moira state comment works, and this bead follows it.

## Out of scope

- Automating the verification itself — the point of the role is that a person looks at the thing.
- Blocking a release on verification (decided against, at filing).
- Verifying anything merged before this ships; the backlog cutoff is the navigator's call at
  Psylocke's first pass, and the bulk `not-needed` backfill happens then, not in this bead.
- Retiring or renaming any existing role, label or launcher beyond the Psylocke roster removal.
- Changes to `bd` itself — everything uses existing commands (`reopen`, `set-state`, `label add`).

## Validation

From the atlantis-hud root, after both PRs are merged:

```bash
emacs --batch -L .claude/cerebro/emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit   # all green
.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer --roster | wc -l                                 # 14
.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer --roster | grep -c Psylocke                      # 0
.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer Psylocke; echo $?                                # roster message, 2
test -x .claude/cerebro/scripts/run-psylocke && bash -n .claude/cerebro/scripts/run-psylocke
readlink .claude/agents/verifier.md    # → .claude/cerebro/agents/verifier.md (absolute or relative)
grep -l "verification:failed" .claude/cerebro/agents/orchestrator.md \
  .claude/cerebro/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md .claude/cerebro/agents/user-feedback.md
grep -c "REOPENED" .claude/cerebro/agents/user-feedback.md               # non-zero
grep -n "five roles\|Psylocke" .github/copilot-instructions.md | head    # the summary names her
```

Consistency check, by reading: every one of the five agent files and three skills describes what it
does with a reopened bead and the `verification:*` labels, and no two contradict each other — the
bead's own acceptance criteria make this the bar. Human-only checks: the "real round" in *The test
plan* — run by the navigator with a live Psylocke session after merge.

## Known traps

- **Two repos, two PRs, strict order.** PR 2's submodule bump needs PR 1's *merged* sha — never the
  branch head, which `--delete-branch` will remove. Push access to `rmstdope/cerebro` exists (PRs
  #1–#5 went this way); if it turns out not to for this session, escalate the bead
  (remove `planned`, add `human`) rather than improvising a fork.
- **Never branch in the shared submodule checkout at `.claude/cerebro`.** The navigator's session
  reads the live skills and agents through it, and it is dirty in their checkout right now. Use the
  submodule-worktree commands in *Increments*; run the ert suite inside that worktree
  (`-L emacs` from the worktree root), not against the mounted copy.
- **Cerebro's claim sweep will kill reopened beads unless taught not to** — it decides "delivered"
  by `git log origin/main --grep "(<id>):"`, and a reopened bead's *old* commits match. The
  `verification:failed` guard in `orchestrator.md` (Increment 5) is load-bearing, not documentation
  polish; without it the first reopened bead gets sweep-closed mid-rework.
- **The 18-entry ert test passes by coincidence after the roster change** (3+15 = 4+14). Tighten it
  (Increment 1) or a future roster edit silently breaks composition while the count holds.
- **`cerebro--derive-interactive` needs no change** — it is generic over the alist — but the
  role string must be `"verifier"` in *both* `cerebro-interactive-agents` and
  `cerebro--role-launch-commands`, and must match `--agent verifier` and `agents/verifier.md`'s
  `name:`. Four places, one spelling; a mismatch fails at `s` in the fleet view with
  "no launch command for role", not at review.
- **atlantis-hud's `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink** to `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — edit the
  target. An edit "to CLAUDE.md" that replaces the symlink with a regular file is a regression a
  reviewer may not catch.
- **Emacs backup files (`*.el~`, `*.md~`) exist committed in the cerebro repo** — never edit them,
  and don't let an editor drop new ones into the PR.
- **Moira's marker logic changes meaning.** Her current grep collects *all* markers; the new rule
  keys off the *last* one. Rewrite the instruction, not just the ladder — an implementer that only
  adds the new states while keeping "once ever" makes a reopen cycle unreportable.
- **`bd label propagate` exists but is not wanted here** — verification state is per-bead; a
  parent's `verification:*` must never cascade to children.
- **`zsh` note for validation commands**: a bare `===` separator in a compound command is expanded
  as a command path and errors; use `"---"` strings when echoing separators.

On a pass the bead is labelled verified; on a failure it is reopened, set to P0 and returns to the fleet. title: Emacs agent list shows the whole fleet's state at a glance
description: Second child of ah-vcf (Emacs fleet view). The list buffer: every agent by name with its state — up/dead for the interactive three, working/idle/dead plus bead and elapsed time for implementers, external ones marked — flat format, glyph column, auto-refresh every 5s, special-mode navigation. Pure state-derivation elisp with ERT tests; reads the status files ah-vcf's first child adds.
design:
## Context

Second child of epic ah-vcf (run the fleet from Emacs; P0), blocked on ah-vcf.1. This bead delivers
the **agent list buffer**: `M-x atlantis-fleet` opens a buffer listing every agent the fleet can
have — Xavier, Cerebro, Moira and the fifteen implementers — each with a state glyph, role, state,
and for an implementer the bead it is on and for how long. It refreshes itself every 5 seconds.
The live detail window, and starting/killing agents, are ah-vcf.3; this bead ships a list you can
trust and navigate, nothing more.

Decided with the navigator (interview in the epic, recorded fully below): flat list, glyphs
● working/up ◌ idle ○ dead, `up`/`dead` for the interactive three (an interactive session's
busy-ness is not readable from outside; implementers get exact working/idle/dead from their
launcher's status file), external agents shown and marked, special-mode keys, auto-refresh 5s.

Data sources (why this is buildable unattended): ah-vcf.1 gives every implementer a status file
`.claude/implementers/<name>.state.json` — `{ state: "idle"|"working", bead: string|null, since:
ISO-8601, pid }` — written by the launcher loop wherever it runs, plus `scripts/run-implementer
--roster` printing the fifteen names. **ah-vcf.1 is planned but may be unbuilt when you start —
check it merged first; if it did not, stop and hand back rather than inventing the file format.**
Interactive agents have no loop: their liveness comes from scanning system processes for the
`--name <Name>` argument their launchers pass (`scripts/run-planner` → `exec claude --agent planner
--name Xavier`, and likewise Cerebro/Moira).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

New directory `tools/emacs/` (nothing exists there today; the repo has no elisp yet):

**`tools/emacs/atlantis-fleet.el`** — the package. Emacs 28+ (`json-parse-string`,
`parse-iso8601-time-string` via `iso8601-parse`). Lexical binding. No external packages in this
bead (vterm arrives in ah-vcf.3). Public surface:

```elisp
;; Entry point: opens (or refreshes) the *atlantis-fleet* buffer in the selected window.
(defun atlantis-fleet ())                                             ; autoload, interactive

;; The interactive roster: fixed, mirrors the three launchers.
(defconst atlantis-fleet-interactive-agents
  '(("Xavier"  . "planner")
    ("Cerebro" . "orchestrator")
    ("Moira"   . "feedback")))

;; Impure readers, each trivially small so everything downstream is pure and testable:
(defun atlantis-fleet--repo-root ())            ; locate-dominating-file for .claude/implementers,
                                                ; from default-directory
(defun atlantis-fleet--roster (repo-root))      ; runs scripts/run-implementer --roster, splits
                                                ; lines; cached in a buffer-local after first call
(defun atlantis-fleet--read-state-file (path))  ; json-parse-string of the file, nil on any error
(defun atlantis-fleet--pid-alive-p (pid))       ; (process-attributes pid) non-nil
(defun atlantis-fleet--system-args ())          ; list of args strings for all system processes,
                                                ; via list-system-processes + process-attributes

;; The pure core — every input passed in, nothing read inside:
(cl-defstruct atlantis-fleet-agent
  name role kind      ; kind: 'interactive | 'implementer
  state               ; 'up | 'working | 'idle | 'dead
  bead since external)

(defun atlantis-fleet--derive (roster interactive-agents states pid-alive-p args owned)
  "STATES is an alist of (name . parsed-state-json-or-nil); ARGS the system process args;
OWNED the set of agent names whose sessions Emacs owns (always empty until ah-vcf.3).
Returns a list of atlantis-fleet-agent, interactive three first, then roster order.")

(defun atlantis-fleet--entry (agent now)
  "AGENT as a tabulated-list entry: [glyph+name role state bead for], propertized.")

(defun atlantis-fleet--elapsed (since now))     ; "12m", "1h03", "2d" — nil-safe
```

Derivation rules `atlantis-fleet--derive` implements (the state machine the epic's validation
cares about):

- **Implementer** with a state file whose `pid` is alive → `working` or `idle` straight from the
  file, `bead`/`since` carried along. File absent, unreadable, or pid dead → `dead`. An
  implementer whose name is not in OWNED but whose pid is alive is `external` (t) — same states,
  marked `(external)` in the line and un-viewable until ah-vcf.3's placeholder.
- **Interactive** agent in OWNED → `up` (ah-vcf.3 supplies that; unreachable in this bead).
  Otherwise `up`+external if any system-process args contain `--name <Name>` (whole-word), else
  `dead`. Between-beads implementers must read `idle`, never `dead` — that is exactly what the
  status file distinguishes.

**The buffer** is `tabulated-list-mode` derived — the Emacs convention for exactly this kind of
list (`list-processes`, `package-menu`), and it supplies `g` (revert), `q` (quit-window), `n`/`p`
via `tabulated-list-mode`'s parent `special-mode` conventions — bind `n`/`p` explicitly to
`next-line`/`previous-line` in the mode map, since `special-mode` alone does not. Columns:
`[("Agent" 14) ("Role" 13) ("State" 18) ("Bead" 10) ("For" 6)]`; the state glyph is the first
character of the Agent column. Faces: `success` for ●, `shadow` for ◌ and ○ text, plain default
otherwise — reuse standard faces, define none.

Auto-refresh: a buffer-local `run-with-timer 5 5` calling revert while the buffer lives; cancelled
in `kill-buffer-hook`. Refresh must preserve point's row by agent name (tabulated-list does this
with `tabulated-list-get-id` — use the agent name as the entry id).

**`tools/emacs/atlantis-fleet-test.el`** — ERT tests over the pure core (below).

**`package.json`** — one script: `"test:fleet": "emacs --batch -L tools/emacs -l
atlantis-fleet-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit"`. **Not** added to `check`: the CI runners
have no Emacs, and the gate must stay runnable everywhere. Say so in a comment right in the
script's name-adjacent docs (`tools/emacs/README.md`, three lines: what this is, how to load it,
how to run the tests).

## Increments

1. **The pure derivation.** Failing ERT tests first (`atlantis-fleet-test.el`):
   `derive/implementer-working-from-live-state-file`, `derive/implementer-idle-between-beads`,
   `derive/implementer-dead-when-pid-gone`, `derive/implementer-dead-when-file-missing`,
   `derive/implementer-external-when-not-owned`, `derive/interactive-up-from-process-args`,
   `derive/interactive-dead-when-absent`, `derive/order-interactive-first-then-roster` — each
   builds plain data (alists, a fake `pid-alive-p` lambda, args lists) and asserts on the returned
   structs. Then write `atlantis-fleet--derive`.
2. **Formatting.** Failing tests: `entry/working-implementer-shows-bead-and-elapsed` (a working
   agent since 12 minutes before NOW renders `"12m"` in the For column and the bead id in Bead),
   `entry/external-marked`, `entry/dead-has-empty-bead-column`, `elapsed/minutes-hours-days`
   (`"12m"`, `"1h03"`, `"2d"`), `elapsed/nil-since-is-empty`. Then `atlantis-fleet--entry` and
   `atlantis-fleet--elapsed`.
3. **The buffer.** Failing test: `buffer/lists-every-agent-once` — with the readers stubbed
   (`cl-letf` over the five impure functions), `(atlantis-fleet)` produces a buffer whose
   `tabulated-list-entries` carry 18 ids (3 interactive + 15 roster). Then the mode, the timer and
   the entry wiring. The timer itself is not unit-tested; the manual check covers it.
4. **Roster + docs.** Failing test: `roster/parses-lines` (feed a fixed string, expect the list —
   test the parser, not the subprocess). Then `atlantis-fleet--roster` shelling out to
   `scripts/run-implementer --roster`, the README, and the `test:fleet` script.

## The test plan

- ERT, batch mode, via `pnpm run test:fleet` — the tests in increments 1–4. Everything asserted is
  a pure function fed constructed inputs; no test starts a process or touches the real
  `.claude/implementers/`.
- `pnpm run check` must stay green untouched — this bead adds no TS/Rust and must not disturb the
  gate. (`test:fleet` is deliberately outside it; see above.)

## User-facing decisions

The navigator's, from the epic's interview (mockups were ASCII previews in the question tool —
this is a text buffer, previews are the mockup):

1. **List format — flat list** (chosen over grouped-by-kind). The agreed line shape, verbatim from
   the chosen preview:
   ```
   ● Xavier     planner       up
   ● Cerebro    orchestrator  up
   ○ Moira      feedback      dead
   ● Cyclops    implementer   working  ah-f9c  12m
   ◌ Wolverine  implementer   idle
   ● Storm      implementer   working  (external)
   ```
2. **Interactive states say `up`/`dead`** (chosen over CPU-derived working/idle, rejected because
   a Xavier waiting on the navigator's answer would read "idle" — plausible and wrong).
   Implementers say `working`/`idle`/`dead`, exact, from the launcher.
3. **Glyphs**: `●` working/up, `◌` idle, `○` dead — as in the preview legend.
4. **Keys**: special-mode convention — `n`/`p`/arrows move, `g` refreshes, `q` quits (chosen over
   follow-only-on-RET). `RET` and `s`/`k` do nothing yet; they are ah-vcf.3's.
5. **Auto-refresh every 5 seconds** (chosen over manual-only and over 15–30s), `g` still forces.
6. **External agents are shown and marked `(external)`** (chosen over ignoring them), so the list
   is the one place that knows who is up.
7. The words in the buffer are exactly the preview's: role names `planner`, `orchestrator`,
   `feedback`, `implementer`; states `up`, `working`, `idle`, `dead`; the marker `(external)`.

## Out of scope

- The detail window, vterm, launching and killing (ah-vcf.3) — `RET`, `s`, `k` unbound here.
- Cerebro's actions — flags, sweeps, counts (ah-4ao).
- Any change under `packages/`, `crates/`, `apps/`, or to the launchers beyond what ah-vcf.1
  already made. If the status file format needs anything more, that is a question for ah-vcf.1's
  seam, not a local reinterpretation.
- Sorting, filtering, or persisting anything.

## Validation

- `pnpm run test:fleet` green (needs a local Emacs 28+; not part of CI — documented in
  `tools/emacs/README.md`).
- `pnpm run check` green (untouched by this bead, run to prove it).
- By hand, the epic's manual check, list-half only: start Xavier from a terminal and one
  implementer with a `.go` flag; `M-x atlantis-fleet` shows Xavier `up (external)`, the
  implementer `working` with its bead, the rest `dead`; an implementer between beads reads `idle`;
  kill the implementer's terminal and the row turns `dead` within ~10s (its pid died; next
  refresh sees it).

## Known traps

- **Build after ah-vcf.1 has merged** — the status-file shape and `--roster` are its exports;
  `bd show ah-vcf.1` and read its plan if anything about the file surprises you.
- **The bead database cannot tell you who is working** (epic trap): do not "improve" the
  derivation with `bd list` — every claim carries the same assignee, and the display would be
  plausibly wrong. Process identity and the status file are the only truthful sources.
- **An implementer is one process per bead** (epic trap): the pid in the status file is the
  *launcher's*, stable across beads — never latch onto the inner `claude`'s pid.
- **`list-system-processes` + `process-attributes` is the portable process scan** — no `pgrep`
  subprocess; on macOS `process-attributes` may return only some keys for other users' processes,
  so match on the `args` attribute and treat nil as no-match.
- **`.claude/worktrees/` holds live agent worktrees** (epic trap) — nothing in this bead walks the
  repo tree; keep it that way. `locate-dominating-file` for `.claude/implementers` from
  `default-directory` is the whole repo discovery.
- **A timer that outlives its buffer keeps firing** — cancel in `kill-buffer-hook`, and guard the
  callback with `buffer-live-p`.
- **`json-parse-string` throws on bad JSON** — a half-written state file (the launcher writes it
  live) must read as nil, not error; wrap in `condition-case`. ah-vcf.1 writes atomically enough
  for practice, but a torn read is still a read.

title: Emacs fleet detail window: live agent sessions, started and killed from the list
description: Third child of ah-vcf (Emacs fleet view). The right window follows the selection: an Emacs-owned vterm per agent running its launcher, s to start a dead agent, k (with confirmation) to kill a live one, a placeholder for agents running outside Emacs, and process-query-on-exit kept on so quitting Emacs with agents working prompts first.
design:
## Context

Third child of epic ah-vcf (run the fleet from Emacs; P0), blocked on ah-vcf.2. This bead makes the
fleet view whole: **the right window shows the selected agent live, and agents are started and
killed from the list.** The navigator chose the "Emacs owns the terminals" attachment model —
each agent runs its launcher inside a vterm buffer Emacs owns, which is what makes the session both
visible and answerable — with the scope boundary agreed as: plain launch and kill live here;
everything Cerebro-ish (go/stop flags, sweeps, counts, releases) stays in ah-4ao.

**ah-vcf.2 is planned but may be unbuilt when you start — check it merged first.** Its
`atlantis-fleet--derive` takes an OWNED set that is always empty until this bead supplies it; that
is the seam you are filling. Read ah-vcf.2's plan (`bd show ah-vcf.2 --json`) before starting: the
struct, the derivation rules and the mode map are defined there.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

All in `tools/emacs/` (created by ah-vcf.2): extend **`atlantis-fleet.el`** and
**`atlantis-fleet-test.el`**; update **`tools/emacs/README.md`** (vterm is now a dependency for
live views).

New dependency: **vterm** (`emacs-libvterm`), chosen by the navigator in the epic. Soft-require:
`(require 'vterm nil t)`; if unavailable, the list still works and `s`/`RET` signal
`user-error "atlantis-fleet needs vterm for live sessions - install emacs-libvterm"`.

New public surface (names final; signatures the implementer follows):

