```elisp
;; Pure: what launches an agent, relative to the repo root.
(defun atlantis-fleet--launch-command (agent)
  "\"scripts/run-planner\" for Xavier, \"scripts/run-orchestrator\" for Cerebro,
\"scripts/run-user-feedback\" for Moira, (\"scripts/run-implementer\" NAME) for an implementer.")

;; Pure: the vterm buffer name for an agent: \"*fleet: Cyclops*\".
(defun atlantis-fleet--session-buffer-name (name))

;; Pure: what `s' / `k' should do, so the decision is testable without windows:
;;   s -> 'launch | 'already-up | 'external
;;   k -> 'kill | 'kill-working (confirm harder) | 'external | 'dead
(defun atlantis-fleet--start-action (agent owned))
(defun atlantis-fleet--kill-action (agent owned))

;; Pure: the placeholder text for an agent with no live view (external or dead) — exact strings
;; under \"User-facing decisions\".
(defun atlantis-fleet--placeholder (agent))

;; Impure, thin:
(defun atlantis-fleet--owned ()          ; alist name -> vterm buffer, live ones only
(defun atlantis-fleet--launch (agent)    ; create the vterm running the launcher; return buffer
(defun atlantis-fleet--show-detail (agent)  ; put the right buffer (session, or placeholder) in
                                            ; the detail window
```

Mechanics, and the decisions bound into them:

- **Layout**: `atlantis-fleet` (entry from ah-vcf.2) now splits: list window on the left,
  `fit-window-to-buffer`-capped around 45 columns, detail window right. Both remembered in
  buffer-locals; re-invoking `atlantis-fleet` re-establishes the layout rather than splitting
  again (`window-live-p` guards).
- **Follow selection**: a `post-command-hook` local to the list buffer; when
  `tabulated-list-get-id` differs from the last-shown agent, call `atlantis-fleet--show-detail`.
  Guard against running when the detail window is gone (recreate lazily).
- **Launching**: `atlantis-fleet--launch` creates the vterm with `vterm-shell` let-bound to the
  launch command run from the repo root (`default-directory` bound to it) and the buffer named by
  `--session-buffer-name`. `vterm` compiles its module on first use — nothing to do about it
  beyond the README noting it. After creating the process:
  `(set-process-query-on-exit-flag proc t)` **explicitly** — this is the navigator's quit guard
  (confirm before Emacs or a buffer kill takes a live agent down); do not rely on vterm's default,
  which is geared to killing shells silently.
- **OWNED**: derived fresh each refresh from live buffers matching the session-buffer naming
  scheme with a live process — no registry to go stale. This feeds ah-vcf.2's `--derive` (its
  OWNED parameter), which is what turns an owned interactive agent `up` and unmarks `external`.
- **Keys** (added to the ah-vcf.2 mode map): `RET` selects the detail window
  (`select-window`) so the navigator can type to the claude session; `s` runs `--start-action`:
  `launch` → launch and show; `already-up` / `external` → `message` (strings below). `k` runs
  `--kill-action`: `kill` → `y-or-n-p` then `kill-buffer` (the query flag makes even a plain kill
  confirm; the explicit prompt keeps the wording ours); `kill-working` → the harder prompt below;
  `external` / `dead` → `message`. Killing an implementer kills the **launcher loop**, not a flag
  dance — flags are ah-4ao.
- **Placeholder**: a read-only buffer `*fleet: <name> (no view)*` holding `--placeholder`'s text,
  reused across shows.

## Increments

1. **The pure decisions.** Failing ERT tests: `launch-command/each-interactive-launcher`,
   `launch-command/implementer-takes-its-name`, `session-buffer-name/shape`,
   `start-action/launches-dead`, `start-action/refuses-external`, `start-action/already-up`,
   `kill-action/plain-kill-for-idle`, `kill-action/harder-for-working`,
   `kill-action/external-and-dead-refused`, `placeholder/external-vs-dead-wording` (assert the
   exact strings). Then the five pure functions.
2. **Owned sessions feed the list.** Failing test: `derive/owned-interactive-is-up-not-external`
   (call ah-vcf.2's `--derive` with a non-empty OWNED and assert `up`, external nil) — this
   probably already passes from ah-vcf.2's implementation; if so, keep it as the seam's pin. Then
   `atlantis-fleet--owned` and wiring it into the refresh.
3. **Windows and keys.** Failing test: `show-detail/picks-session-when-owned-else-placeholder` —
   with `--owned` stubbed via `cl-letf`, assert `--show-detail` chooses the vterm buffer for an
   owned agent and a placeholder buffer otherwise (assert on the buffer chosen, not on window
   geometry). Then the layout, the follow hook, `RET`/`s`/`k`. Window geometry and vterm
   interaction are covered by the manual check, not ERT.

## The test plan

- ERT batch via `pnpm run test:fleet` (from ah-vcf.2): the tests above. vterm must **not** load in
  batch tests — the pure functions and `--show-detail` tests stub everything that would touch it,
  so `test:fleet` stays runnable on a machine without vterm.
- `pnpm run check` untouched and green.

## User-facing decisions

From the epic's interview with the navigator:

1. **Attachment: Emacs owns the terminals** — agents launched from the list into Emacs-owned vterm
   buffers. tmux-underneath and tee-to-files were rejected (tmux: dependency and naming scheme not
   wanted; tee: watch-only defeats the point for the interactive three). Consequence accepted:
   agents started outside Emacs get no live view (placeholder instead), and Emacs quitting takes
   the fleet down — hence the guard below.
2. **Scope: plain launch/kill in this bead**; flags, sweeps, counts and the Cerebro replacement
   stay in ah-4ao (navigator confirmed the boundary explicitly).
3. **External agents: shown, marked, not viewable** — placeholder rather than pretending.
4. **Quit guard: confirm on quit** — `process-query-on-exit-flag` t on every session process, so
   killing a buffer or quitting Emacs with agents up prompts first. No-guard was rejected: an
   implementer killed mid-bead strands a claim, a worktree and an open PR.
5. **Keys: `s` start, `k` kill, `RET` focus** — RET-starts-when-dead was rejected (an accidental
   RET would launch a session).
6. The exact strings (planner-proposed wording; the navigator owns layout/keys/behaviour, these
   carry no decisions beyond them):
   - dead placeholder: `Cyclops is not running. Press s to start it.`
   - external placeholder: `Xavier is running outside Emacs - no live view. Use the terminal that
     started it.`
   - `s` on a live agent: `Xavier is already up`
   - `s` on an external agent: `Xavier is running outside Emacs`
   - `k` plain confirm: `Kill Cyclops? `
   - `k` on a working implementer: `Cyclops is working on ah-f9c - killing mid-bead strands a
     claim, a worktree and an open PR. Kill anyway? `
   - `k` on external: `Xavier is running outside Emacs - stop it from its own terminal`
   - `k` on dead: `Cyclops is not running`
   - after starting an implementer: `Cyclops started - it will idle until its go flag is set`
     (flags are ah-4ao's; an s-started implementer idles by design).

## Out of scope

- Writing or clearing `.go`/`.stop` flags, sweeps, counts, releases — ah-4ao.
- tmux, tee files, or any second attachment path.
- Restarting agents automatically, or reacting to a session dying beyond the list turning the row
  dead on the next refresh.
- Any change to the launchers or to anything under `packages/`, `crates/`, `apps/`.

## Validation

- `pnpm run test:fleet` green on a machine without vterm loaded; `pnpm run check` green.
- The epic's manual check, in full (needs vterm installed): `M-x atlantis-fleet`; `s` on Xavier
  starts the planner in the right window and its row turns `up`; `s` on an implementer starts its
  loop, row `idle`; touch its `.go` flag from a shell and the row turns `working` with a bead id
  once one is claimed; moving point changes the right window; `RET` lets you type to Xavier;
  killing an agent's terminal process externally turns the row `dead` within ~10s; `k` on a
  working implementer shows the harder prompt; `C-x C-c` with agents up prompts before Emacs dies.

## Known traps

- **Build after ah-vcf.2 merged** (and transitively ah-vcf.1); the OWNED parameter and the mode
  map are its exports.
- **vterm compiles a C module on first run** and may prompt; it also cannot load in `--batch`
  CI-less test runs — keep every ERT test free of a live vterm (stub with `cl-letf`), or
  `test:fleet` breaks on machines without it.
- **`vterm-shell` is let-bound at buffer creation**, not set globally — a global set would change
  the navigator's ordinary vterm shells.
- **The query flag is the guard**: vterm's own kill behaviour is tuned for disposable shells;
  without the explicit `set-process-query-on-exit-flag` t, `kill-buffer` and Emacs exit take
  agents down silently, which is precisely what the navigator declined.
- **An implementer's vterm outlives its beads** (one launcher process, many claude children — epic
  trap): owned-ness keys on the vterm's own process, never the inner claude.
- **Do not touch `.claude/worktrees/`** (epic trap), and launch with `default-directory` at the
  repo root — a vterm inherited from a worktree directory would run the launcher against the wrong
  tree.
- **`post-command-hook` runs constantly** — the follow hook must be cheap (compare ids, return)
  and buffer-local, or every keystroke in the list pays for a window operation.

title: Implementer launcher writes its state and current bead where tools can read it
description: First child of ah-vcf (Emacs fleet view). The Emacs agent list needs to say, per implementer: working, idle or dead, on which bead, since when. The bead database cannot answer this (every claim carries the same git-config assignee) and parsing terminal scrollback is not a contract. The launcher is the one process that knows exactly when a bead run starts and ends, so it writes the answer down: a small JSON status file per implementer next to the go/stop flags, updated at every state transition, plus a --roster flag that prints the implementer roster for other tools. Groundwork for ah-vcf's list and detail children.
design:
## Context

First child of epic ah-vcf (run the fleet from Emacs; P0). The Emacs agent list (ah-vcf.2) must
show, per implementer: **working / idle / dead, the bead it is on, and since when**. Nothing can
currently answer that: the bead database stamps every claim with the same git-config assignee
(ah-vcf's "Known traps"), the `.log` file exists only under `--log`, and terminal scrollback is not
a contract. The launcher loop in `scripts/runImplementer.ts` is the one process that knows exactly
when a bead run starts and ends, and it already parses every stream-json event line — so it writes
the answer down: a JSON status file per implementer beside the go/stop flags, updated at every
transition, with the bead id extracted from the event stream. A `--roster` flag also makes the
implementer roster readable by other tools (Emacs must not hard-code a second copy of the fifteen
names).

This bead is TypeScript tooling only — nothing under `packages/`, `crates/` or `apps/`, and no
elisp yet. ah-vcf.2 (blocked on this) consumes the files.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

All in **`scripts/runImplementer.ts`** and **`scripts/runImplementer.test.ts`**.

New exports in `runImplementer.ts` (place them near `logPath`, :166-168, which is the pattern —
derive from `flagPaths`):

```ts
/** Where a named implementer's machine-readable status lives, beside its flags. */
export function statePath(repoRoot: string, name: string): string;
// -> <repo>/.claude/implementers/<name>.state.json

/** What the status file holds. `bead` is null until the stream names one. */
export type ImplementerState = {
  state: "idle" | "working";
  bead: string | null;
  /** ISO-8601, the moment this state was entered (not last write). */
  since: string;
  /** The launcher's own pid: a reader treats a file whose pid is gone as dead. */
  pid: number;
};

/**
 * The bead id a stream-json event names, or null. Recognises, in this order:
 *  - a Bash tool_use whose command matches /\bbd\s+(?:update|heartbeat)\s+(ah-[a-z0-9]+(?:\.\d+)*)/
 *  - a Bash tool_use containing a branch or worktree named for a bead:
 *    /\b(?:worktree add|checkout|switch)\b[^\n]*\b(ah-[a-z0-9]+(?:\.\d+)*)-/
 * Unparseable lines and events without a match return null (same shrug as formatEvent).
 */
export function beadFromEvent(line: string): string | null;

/** Writes the state file, swallowing fs errors: a status file must never take down a bead. */
export function writeState(path: string, state: ImplementerState): void;
```

`beadFromEvent` parses the same lines `formatEvent` (:186-223) already receives — reuse its
parse-and-shrug structure (JSON.parse in try/catch, walk `message.content`, look at
`tool_use` blocks with `name === "Bash"`, read `input.command`). The claim commands the
`implement-bead` role runs are `bd update <id> --claim` and `bd heartbeat <id>` (heartbeats recur at
every phase gate, so a missed claim is recovered a few minutes in); the branch fallback catches a
`bd ready --claim` pickup, whose command line names no bead but whose worktree branch is
`<bead-id>-<description>` by repo convention.

Loop integration, all inside `runLoop` (:342-394) and `runOneBead` (:284-339):

- `runLoop` computes `const state = statePath(repoRoot, name)` beside `paths`, and writes
  `{ state: "idle", bead: null, since: now, pid: process.pid }` before the `for (;;)` loop.
- On `action === "exit"` (:359-363): `rmSync(state, { force: true })` beside `clearStop`, so a
  finished implementer has no file and reads dead — a crash leaves a file whose `pid` is gone,
  which reads dead too.
- On `action === "idle"`: no write per poll — the idle state was written when it was entered.
- At "starting on one bead" (:370): write `{ state: "working", bead: null, since: now, pid }`.
- `runOneBead` gains an `onBead: (id: string) => void` parameter, called at most once — in the
  existing per-line loop (:321-326), if no bead has been seen yet and `beadFromEvent(line)` returns
  one, call it. The loop passes a callback that rewrites the file with the id and the *unchanged*
  `since` (the run started when it started; naming the bead is not a new state).
- After the run returns (whatever its exit), write idle again with a fresh `since`.

CLI: `--roster` handled in the `invokedDirectly` block (:399-441) **before** the name validation —
`scripts/run-implementer --roster` prints the fifteen `IMPLEMENTER_NAMES` (:61-77) one per line and
exits 0. Update the usage string (:408) to
`usage: scripts/run-implementer <name> [--log] [--repo <path>] | --roster`.

`Date.now()`/`new Date().toISOString()` are fine here — this is a Node script, not a workflow.

Nothing else changes: `scripts/run-implementer` (the bash wrapper) forwards arguments already;
flags, log, `formatEvent` and the backoff logic are untouched.

## Increments

1. **`beadFromEvent`.** Failing tests first, in `runImplementer.test.ts`, new
   `describe("beadFromEvent")` beside `describe("formatEvent")` (:157): "names the bead a claim
   command claims" (a stream-json assistant event whose Bash `input.command` is
   `bd update ah-f9c --claim && bd dolt push` → `"ah-f9c"`); "names the bead a heartbeat renews"
   (`bd heartbeat ah-vcf.1` → `"ah-vcf.1"`); "reads the bead off a worktree branch"
   (`git worktree add -b ah-t65-load-reports .claude/worktrees/ah-t65 origin/main` → `"ah-t65"`);
   "says nothing about a command with no bead in it" (`pnpm run test` → null); "survives a line
   that is not JSON at all" (→ null). Build the fixture events the way `formatEvent`'s tests do.
2. **`statePath` + `writeState`.** Failing tests: `describe("statePath")` — "puts an implementer's
   status beside its flags" (mirrors `logPath`'s test at :204-205, expecting
   `.claude/implementers/Cyclops.state.json`); `writeState` — "swallows a write into a directory
   that does not exist" (points at a path under a missing dir, expects no throw).
3. **Loop writes the file.** Failing tests in `describe("the launcher loop")`, reusing the
   `workspace()` harness (:231-249) — its stubbed `claude` body can `printf` stream-json lines to
   stdout: "records working, then the bead, then idle across one run" (stub emits a claim event
   then exits; poll the state file with the existing `until()` helper (:271-280): first
   `state:"working"`, then `bead:"ah-…"`, then `state:"idle"`); "removes the status file when told
   to finish" (touch the stop flag, wait for exit, file gone). Then wire `runLoop`/`runOneBead`.
4. **`--roster`.** Failing test: "prints the roster and exits without starting anything" — spawn
   the launcher with `--roster` and an empty-`claude` PATH, expect stdout to equal the fifteen
   names newline-joined and the invocations log to stay empty. Then the CLI change.

## The test plan

All vitest, in `scripts/runImplementer.test.ts`, run by `pnpm run test:tooling` (part of
`pnpm run test` via `scripts/runSuites.ts`). The tests named per increment above; the existing
suites in that file (nextAction, flagPaths, canonicalName, launchCommand, formatEvent, logPath, the
loop) must stay green untouched — the loop tests in particular pin that the launcher still works
with no status file expectations.

No browser tests; nothing under `packages/` moves.

## User-facing decisions

None in the shipped application — this is fleet tooling, invisible to the player. The navigator's
decisions governing the epic (Emacs owns the terminals; list format; up/dead vs working/idle
vocabulary) are recorded in ah-vcf.2's plan; this bead only supplies the data. The status-file
shape and the extraction patterns are the planner's architecture calls.

## Out of scope

- Any elisp (ah-vcf.2, ah-vcf.3).
- Status files for Xavier, Cerebro or Moira — the interactive three have no launcher loop; their
  up/dead state is derived by Emacs from the vterm process it owns (ah-vcf.2).
- Changing `--log` defaults, the flag protocol, or how a bead is run.
- Teaching `bd` who claims what.

## Validation

- `pnpm run test:tooling` green; `pnpm run check` for the full gate.
- By hand: `scripts/run-implementer --roster` prints fifteen names. Start
  `scripts/run-implementer Cyclops` with a `.go` flag in a scratch repo (or the real one with the
  queue empty): `.claude/implementers/Cyclops.state.json` appears with `state:"idle"` →
  `"working"` when a bead starts, gains the bead id within the first minutes, returns to idle after
  the run, and disappears on a `.stop` finish.

## Known traps

- **`state.json` must be git-ignored already** — `.claude/` is covered by the existing "Local agent
  scratch space" rule in `.gitignore` (which carves out only `skills`, `agents` and settings).
  Verify with `git check-ignore .claude/implementers/x.state.json` rather than assuming; if it is
  not ignored, add it to the same block, not a new one.
- **A stream chunk is not a line** (:311-319) — `beadFromEvent` must be called on the split lines
  the existing loop produces, never on raw chunks, or ids split across chunk boundaries are lost.
- **Do not write the state file from inside the `data` handler on every line** — only on the first
  bead hit. The handler runs hundreds of times a minute.
- **`bd update --claim` may fail** (another agent won the bead) and the id still gets written. That
  is acceptable staleness — the very next heartbeat of the bead actually being worked overwrites
  nothing since only the first match is taken, but a run that claimed nothing exits within
  `SHORT_RUN_MS` and the file returns to idle; do not add claim-outcome parsing to fix a
  two-minute window.
- **The fake `claude` in tests is a bash script on a bare PATH** (:242-244) — `/bin/bash` shebang,
  no `env`; emit stream-json with single-quoted `printf` formats, and remember the invocations log
  asserts on `$*`.
- **tsx runs these scripts as CJS** (:432-434) — no top-level `await` in anything you add.

title: Run the agent fleet from Emacs: an agent list beside a live view of the selected one
description:
# Summary

The fleet is run out of terminals. Every agent — Xavier, Cerebro, Moira and each implementer — is a
terminal window the navigator opened by hand, and keeping track of who is up, who is working and who
has died is a matter of tabbing between windows and reading scrollback. This bead builds an Emacs
interface over that: **one buffer listing the agents, one buffer showing the selected agent.**

Left window: the agents by name, each with its state — **working**, **idle** or **dead**. Move up and
down with the ordinary Emacs motion keys; the right window follows the selection. For an interactive
agent (Xavier, Cerebro, Moira) the right window shows its live `claude` session; for an implementer
it shows the output of its `run-implementer` run.

This is developer tooling for the navigator, not part of the shipped application. It has no bearing
on the desktop or web client and touches neither.

# Scope

- An Emacs package — elisp, in this repository — providing the two-window layout above.
- The agent list: every role that can be running, by name, with its state and enough detail to be
  useful at a glance (for an implementer, the bead it is on).
- Navigation: point moves in the list, the right window follows. Whatever the equivalent of `n`/`p`
  and the arrow keys ends up being is the planner's question for the navigator.
- The detail window: a live view, not a snapshot. An interactive agent's session is shown in
  **vterm** (chosen by the navigator — `emacs-libvterm`, which handles the full ANSI a `claude` TUI
  emits); an implementer's is its run output.
- Whatever the detail view needs to be *attachable* rather than merely readable — see the open
  question below, which is the single largest unknown in this bead.

# Out of scope

- **Replacing Cerebro with elisp and shell scripting.** Wanted, and filed as its own bead blocked on
  this one, so a working view is not held up by an open design question. The list buffer is where
  those actions would eventually be triggered from, so this bead should not make that awkward — but
  it implements none of it.
- Starting or stopping agents from Emacs. Same reason: that is the orchestrator question.
- Any change to the launcher scripts' behaviour. If one needs a flag or a status file to make this
  possible, that is in scope; changing how an agent runs is not.
- The Atlantis HUD application itself. Nothing under `packages/`, `crates/` or `apps/`.

# What the harness already offers to build on

Read before designing anything, because most of the state this needs is already written down
somewhere:

- **`scripts/runImplementer.ts`** — the roster of implementer names (a closed set, and Cerebro
  depends on it), `flagPaths()`, and the loop that gives each bead a fresh `claude` process.
- **`.claude/implementers/<name>.go` / `.stop`** — the flags Cerebro writes to put an implementer to
  work or tell it to finish. Their presence is part of "should this agent be running".
- **`.claude/implementers/<name>.log`** — every event of a run, but **only when started with
  `--log`**, which is off by default because one bead writes about a megabyte and the file is
  appended across runs.
- **`scripts/run-planner`, `run-orchestrator`, `run-user-feedback`** — the three interactive
  launchers, each `exec claude --agent <role> --name <Name>`.
- **`.claude/agents/orchestrator.md`** — how Cerebro answers "who is actually running" today:
  `pgrep -fl "runImplementer.ts"` and `ListAgents`. That is the existing answer to this bead's
  hardest question and the place to start from.

# Known traps

- **The bead database cannot tell you who is working.** Every claim in this repository carries the
  assignee `Henrik Kurelid`, because bd takes `owner`/assignee from `git config user.email` and has
  no override — so `bd list --status in_progress` says a bead is being built but not by which
  implementer. Deriving the fleet's state from beads alone will produce a plausible, wrong display.
  Process identity (`pgrep`, the launcher's own name argument) is what distinguishes them.
- **`--log` is off by default**, so a straightforward "tail the log file" detail view shows nothing
  at all for an implementer started the ordinary way. Either the view attaches to the process rather
  than a file, or something has to make logging the default — which costs a megabyte a bead and is a
  decision for the navigator.
- **An implementer is one process per bead, not one per agent.** The loop starts a fresh `claude`
  for every bead, so anything that latches onto a PID sees the agent "die" and reappear between
  beads. State must be derived from the loop, not from the session inside it.
- **A print-mode session appears in neither `claude agents` nor `ListAgents`.** Implementers run with
  `--print`; the interactive three do not. The two halves of the list will not be discoverable the
  same way, and pretending otherwise gives one half a permanently wrong state.
- **`.claude/worktrees/` holds live agent worktrees.** Anything walking the repository from Emacs
  should stay out of them, and must never check a branch out.

# The open question the planning session has to answer

**How the detail window shows a live session that is already attached to a terminal.** An interactive
agent is a `claude` process running in a terminal the navigator opened; a second viewer cannot simply
attach to it. The realistic options each cost something, and choosing between them is most of this
bead's design:

- start the agents *from* Emacs in vterm buffers, so Emacs owns the terminal — clean, but changes how
  every session is launched and means an agent started from a shell is invisible;
- run each agent under a multiplexer (`tmux`/`screen`) and have Emacs attach to the session — leaves
  the launchers usable from a shell, adds a dependency and a naming scheme;
- have the launchers tee their output somewhere Emacs can follow — read-only, so an interactive
  agent could be watched but not answered, which defeats the point for Xavier and Moira.

The planner decides this **with the navigator**, since it determines how they start their day.

# Validation

- ERT tests for everything that is a pure function — parsing the roster, deriving a state from
  flags, processes and logs, formatting a list line. The state machine is where the bugs will be, and
  it can be tested without an agent running.
- Manually, with a real fleet: start Xavier and two implementers, confirm the list shows three agents
  in the right states, that moving down the list changes the right window, that an implementer
  between beads reads as idle rather than dead, and that killing a terminal turns that agent dead
  within a few seconds.
- The Atlantis HUD suites are untouched by this and need not be run beyond the usual gate.

# Note on shape

This is bigger than one increment and will need splitting — plausible seams are the state model
first (pure, testable, no UI), then the list buffer, then the detail window, then the live-session
attachment once its question is answered. The split is the planning session's call.
design: Navigator's decisions, taken at filing: vterm is the terminal backend (emacs-libvterm, for full ANSI from the claude TUI). Replacing Cerebro with elisp/bash is a separate bead blocked on this one, so the view is not held up by that design question. Splitting this into children is the planning session's call.
acceptance_criteria: An Emacs command opens a two-window layout: a left buffer listing every agent by name with its state (working, idle or dead), and a right buffer showing the selected agent — a live vterm session for Xavier, Cerebro and Moira, and the run-implementer output for an implementer. Moving point up and down the list changes what the right window shows. An implementer between beads reads as idle rather than dead, and an agent whose terminal is killed reads as dead within a few seconds. Pure state-derivation logic is covered by ERT tests.
notes: Filed from a navigator request on 2026-08-14. Developer tooling for the fleet, not part of the shipped Atlantis HUD client.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-vcf.3, delivered in PR #229

title: An older report is stored for history, never shown
description: When a report older than the current turn is imported (own or foreign faction), it must not become the working turn. Chosen with the navigator (2026-08-14, supersedes the first reading of gh-208): the older report is parsed and committed to the game's stored turn history — so the turn-comparison feature can read it — but the workspace keeps showing the current turn, and the old confirm-and-switch dialog goes away. Reported by rmstdope in GitHub issue #208.
design:
## Context

Navigator-filed P0 (gh-208), scope settled with the navigator in planning (two questions, answers
recorded below): a report **older than the current turn must never become the working turn** — own
or foreign — but it is **still parsed and committed to the game's stored turn history**, so the
turn-comparison feature (ah-jg6.3/4) can read it. The issue's first reading ("refuse orders
imports") was wrong — an orders file carries no turn number and always applies to the current turn;
the bead was retitled during planning and its stray dependency on ah-470 removed.

Today's behaviour, all in `packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts` (pure, tested) and
`AppShell.tsx`'s `loadReport`: an older own report raises a **confirm dialog** (issue #47's
`confirmOlder`) and, confirmed, rolls the workspace back; an older foreign report raises the
foreign-report prompt with merge disabled. Both of those paths are replaced by store-without-display.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts`** — the decision, where the rules live on purpose
  (the file's own header says why):
  - `ReportLoadDecision` replaces `{ kind: "confirmOlder", ... }` with
    `{ kind: "storeOnly"; currentTurn: number; incomingTurn: number }`.
  - `decideReportLoad`: **any** incoming report with a readable turn number older than the current
    readable turn number → `storeOnly`, own and foreign alike — checked *before* the
    foreign-faction question, since age now outranks ownership. Same-turn foreign → `ask` with
    `canMerge` (unchanged); newer or same-turn own → `load` (unchanged); an unreadable turn number
    on either side keeps passing as `load` (the existing "refusing to say which of two unknowns
    came first" rule — keep its comment).
  - `shouldConfirmOlderTurnLoad` is renamed to what it now answers (e.g. `isOlderTurn`) or kept as
    the internal predicate; it is exported from `AppShell.tsx:146` — check for external users
    before renaming.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** — `loadReport`'s decision handling:
  - `storeOnly`: commit the already-parsed report to storage through **the same memory path
    `applyReport` uses** (read `gameMemory.ts` — `rememberTurn`/`commitTurn` — and reuse the exact
    call, minus every piece of shell state: no `setParsed`, no `setRawReport`, no
    `setOrdersDocument`, no selection moves, no `clearPlan`). Then one status line, the existing
    `setStatus` message shape: "turn 70 stored for history; still showing turn 71." (failed:
    false, warning: false — it is an outcome, not a problem).
  - Delete the confirmOlder pending state and its dialog rendering; the foreign-report prompt no
    longer receives older reports at all (the decision routes them away before it).
- **Reuse**: the parse already done in `loadReport` (classified when the ruleset is ready — the
  stored payload must go through the same parse the normal import uses); `gameMemory.ts`'s commit
  path; the status-line idiom.

## Increments

1. **The decision changes shape.** Opening failing test: `reportLoadDecision.test.ts` › "an older
   own report is stored, not shown" and "an older foreign report is stored, not shown" (both
   `storeOnly` with the two turn numbers); "a same-turn foreign report still asks with merge";
   "a newer own report still loads"; "an unreadable turn still loads". GREEN: the module; every
   existing case updated to the new kind.
2. **The shell stores without showing.** Opening failing test: smoke,
   `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` — rewrite the older-turn tests at :343-394 (they assert the old
   confirm dialog: "imported as turn 70"): import t71, then t70 — assert **no dialog**, the status
   line reports "stored for history", the header still shows turn 71, and the orders document is
   untouched. GREEN: the `loadReport` change.
3. **The stored turn is really there.** Extend increment 2's smoke test: open the Turn chip's
   picker (ah-jg6.3's surface, already merged) and assert turn 70 now appears in the list — the
   one observable proof the commit happened. If the picker's list is fetched on open, no reload
   is needed; follow its landed behaviour.

## The test plan

Unit (vitest): `reportLoadDecision.test.ts` as above — this file is the rules, and the house reason
it exists is that the shell cannot be unit-tested.
Smoke (Playwright, both projects): increments 2–3; the foreign-report merge tests and the
comparison-picker tests must stay green — this bead reroutes traffic just upstream of both.
Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`; full `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator, 2026-08-14 (no mockup — a dialog is removed and a status
line added in the existing idiom; no new surface):

- **Scope**: gh-208 means *reports*, not orders — an orders file has no turn to check. Chosen over
  "both kinds" and "orders only, as written".
- **Backfill**: an older report is **stored for history but never displayed** — chosen explicitly
  over refusing outright (which would have killed backfilling the comparison feature's history)
  and over keeping today's confirm dialog.

The status line's wording ("turn N stored for history; still showing turn M.") follows the
established status idiom; the navigator adjusts post-merge if it reads wrong.

## Out of scope

- Orders import (ah-470's family) — untouched; its own turn guard is unnecessary by construction.
- Merging older foreign reports into current sightings — stale data; they are stored, not merged.
- Any UI for browsing stored history beyond what ah-jg6.3 already shipped.
- Un-storing or deleting stored turns.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check   # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, post-merge is fine): with turn 71 open, import the turn-70 report — no
dialog, the status line says stored, the workspace stays on 71, and the comparison picker now
offers 70.

## Known traps

- **Store through the same parse and the same commit path the normal import uses** — a storeOnly
  commit that skips classification (or invents its own storage call) writes a payload that differs
  from what a normal import of the same file would have written, and the comparison feature will
  read both.
- **`await flush()` before nothing**: the storeOnly path must NOT flush or touch the draft writer —
  the working turn's state is exactly what it must not disturb. `loadReport` flushes at its top
  today because the *displayed* turn is about to change; under storeOnly it is not — make sure the
  flush-then-store ordering cannot clobber a draft (flushing is harmless, re-keying is not).
- **The smoke tests at :343-394 encode the old behaviour** ("imported as turn 70", the confirm
  dialog) — they are rewritten, not deleted: the scenario (a stray older file) still needs pinning,
  the pinned outcome changes.
- **Duplicate import of an already-stored turn** — the Rust side already detects a re-import
  (`diff_imported_turn`); a storeOnly of a turn already in history must surface whatever the
  normal path surfaces (an updated store or a quiet no-op), not an error.
- **`shouldConfirmOlderTurnLoad` is re-exported from `AppShell.tsx:146`** — find its consumers
  before renaming or removing.
- **ah-470 (in progress) is rewiring the same `loadReport` entry** for orders sniffing — expect a
  merge conflict in `loadReport`; whoever lands second rebases carefully around the other's sniff/
  decision ordering: orders sniff first, then report decisions, is the coherent order.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — branch from `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Attempting to import a turn older than the current turn is refused, with a clear message to the user explaining why.
- This applies regardless of which faction the imported data belongs to.
- Importing the current turn (or a newer one, if applicable) still works as expected.

title: Turn comparison shows no changes dialog on the desktop
description:
# Summary

Comparing turns does not work in the desktop app. The navigator reports that selecting another turn
to compare against produces **no changes dialog at all** — not an empty one — so the whole
turn-comparison feature is unreachable in practice.

Investigate first, then fix. The fix is likely small; what this bead buys is knowing *which* of the
several silent exits below is the one that fires.

# What is known

Reported on the **desktop** shell. Whether the web build has the same fault is unknown and part of
the investigation.

The feature is built and unit-tested (`packages/shared/src/turnDiff.ts`,
`packages/shared/src/turnCompare.ts`, `packages/shared/src/workspace/changesView.ts`,
`ChangesDialog.tsx`), so this is much more likely a wiring or state fault than a diffing one — which
also fits "no dialog" rather than "an empty dialog".

The chain from click to dialog, all in `packages/shared/src/workspace/`:

1. The turn picker calls `handleSelectComparisonTurn` (`AppShell.tsx:2070`), which loads the chosen
   turn and calls `setComparison`.
2. `comparedTurnChip` (`AppShell.tsx:2106`) derives the label from `comparison`.
3. `AppHeader.tsx:492` renders the **Changes** chip *only while `comparedTurnLabel` is truthy* — no
   comparison, no chip, and no way in.
4. The chip toggles `changesOpen`; `AppShell.tsx:2623` renders `ChangesDialog` only when
   `changesOpen && turnDiff`.

# Candidate causes, to be confirmed or ruled out

Each of these ends the chain silently, with no error shown:

- **`handleSelectComparisonTurn` returns early.** It bails without feedback when
  `parsed?.header.factionId` is missing (`AppShell.tsx:2073`) and again when
  `client.loadImportedTurn` returns `null` (`AppShell.tsx:2091`). The latter is the desktop's Tauri
  core rather than the WASM one, which is consistent with a desktop-only report.
- **The comparison is cleared as soon as it is set.** Two effects null it out — on a new working
  turn (`AppShell.tsx:796`) and on a game change (`AppShell.tsx:1445`). If selecting a turn touches
  either dependency, the comparison dies in the same render it was born in and the chip never
  appears.
- **`turnDiff` is null even with a comparison set** (`AppShell.tsx:2170`), which leaves the chip
  visible but the dialog unrenderable — clicking it would then do nothing visible. Worth telling
  apart from the case above by observation.
- **Discoverability.** If the chip is in fact appearing and the interaction is simply not findable,
  that is a UI question and goes back to the navigator rather than being decided here.

# Scope

- Reproduce on the desktop build with two imported turns of one faction, and establish which step of
  the chain above breaks.
- Check the web build for the same fault, and record the answer either way.
- Fix the cause found, with a regression test at the level the fault sits (a unit test on the shell
  wiring where possible, a smoke test where not).
- No silent dead end left behind: whatever path fails should tell the player something, even if the
  underlying cause is fixed.

# Out of scope

- Changing what the diff reports or how `ChangesDialog` presents it. If the investigation finds the
  dialog opens correctly and its *contents* are wrong, that is a second bead.
- Redesigning the comparison interaction. Any user-visible change beyond making the existing design
  work goes to the navigator first.

# Validation

- New automated coverage that fails before the fix and passes after.
- `pnpm test` and the repo's usual gate green.
- Manual on a desktop build: import two turns for the same faction, pick the older one in the turn
  picker, confirm the Turn chip shows the comparison, the **Changes** chip appears, and the dialog
  opens showing unit, region and order differences that match the two reports.
design:
## Context

Navigator-filed P0: on the desktop app, picking a comparison turn produces **no changes dialog at
all**, making the turn-comparison feature (ah-jg6.*, all merged) unreachable. The bead's own
description is the investigation brief — the click-to-dialog chain with line refs and four candidate
silent exits — and this plan structures that investigation into increments; it deliberately does
**not** pre-decide the cause, because the fix's location depends on which exit fires.

The single most important background fact, which the brief implies and the implementer must hold
onto: **the Playwright `desktop-shell` project is not the desktop backend.** Both smoke projects run
the built web bundle with the WASM core in Chrome (`vite preview`); the real desktop runs the
**Tauri core** (`command_load_imported_turn` etc.) inside a webview, exercised only by
`pnpm run test:native` (wdio) and by hand. The comparison smoke tests passing on both projects is
therefore *consistent* with a desktop-only fault in the Tauri path — it rules nothing out. That is
also why candidate 1 (the Tauri `loadImportedTurn` returning `null`) is the leading suspect for a
desktop-only report.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Unknown until the investigation lands — the candidates, from the bead:

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — `handleSelectComparisonTurn` (:2070, early
  returns at :2073 and :2091), the two comparison-clearing effects (:796, :1445), the
  `changesOpen && turnDiff` render gate (:2623).
- `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` — the Tauri adapter's `load_imported_turn` dispatch and
  wire-shape normalization (the parity tests at `index.test.ts` are the harness to extend).
- `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs` — `command_load_imported_turn` and its DTOs, if the fault is below
  the adapter.

Reuse for diagnosis: the wdio suite (`pnpm run test:native`, `wdio.conf.ts`) if it can reach the
picker; otherwise the desktop dev build with devtools. Reuse for regression: the parity-test
pattern in `index.test.ts` (hand-written snake_case/camelCase payloads through both adapters), the
Rust `command_*` tests in `core-tauri` (e.g. the imported-turn payload test), and the existing
comparison smoke tests.

## Increments

This is an investigation bead; the increments are ordered gates, not parallel features. **Write the
failing regression test at whichever level the fault turns out to sit — that test is increment 3's
deliverable and the PR's centerpiece.**

1. **Reproduce and localize.** On a desktop build (`pnpm` dev or the packaged app) with two
   imported turns of one faction: pick the older turn in the Turn picker and observe the chain —
   does the Turn chip show `71 ⇄ 70`? Does the Changes chip appear? Temporarily instrument the four
   candidate exits (the two early returns, the two clearing effects, the render gate) to log which
   fires. Record the answer in the bead's notes (`bd update ah-6l2 --append-notes`) before fixing
   anything.
2. **Check the web build the same way** and record the answer either way — the bead requires it.
   (The existing smoke tests already exercise this path on WASM; a manual confirm is enough.)
3. **Pin the fault with a failing test at its own level.**
   - Tauri adapter/core returning `null` or mis-shaped data → a parity case in
     `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` (the hand-written-payload harness) and/or a
     `core-tauri` Rust test committing a real report and loading it back by explicit turn number —
     whichever reproduces the `null`.
   - A clearing-effect race (comparison nulled in the render it was born) → a shell-level test if
     the harness allows, else a smoke test that pins the observable outcome (chip appears and
     stays) plus a unit test on the extracted decision if the fix extracts one.
   - The render gate (`turnDiff` null with a comparison set) → a unit test on the diff-input
     derivation.
4. **Fix the cause found, minimally.** No redesign of the interaction — the bead sends any
   user-visible change beyond "make the existing design work" back to the navigator.
5. **No silent dead end.** Whichever exits were NOT the cause remain silent traps; give the two
   early returns in `handleSelectComparisonTurn` a status-line message in the existing idiom
   ("could not load turn 70 for comparison") so the next fault of this kind reports itself. If the
   investigation instead finds the chip appears and the feature was merely unfindable, **stop and
   take it to the navigator** — that is a UI question and explicitly not this plan's to decide.
6. **Clean up the instrumentation** from increment 1 — nothing of it lands.

## The test plan

- The regression test from increment 3 — failing before, passing after; its level depends on the
  fault, and the plan above names the harness for each candidate.
- The status-line messages from increment 5 pinned by a unit test if shell-testable, else asserted
  in the smoke test.
- Everything existing stays green: comparison smoke tests (both projects), adapter parity suite,
  `cargo test --workspace` if the Rust side is touched.
- Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`, plus `pnpm run test:native` if the fix touches
  the Tauri path (and it likely does); full `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None taken here. Two standing instructions from the bead: any user-visible change beyond making the
existing design work goes to the navigator first; and if the investigation concludes
"discoverability" rather than "defect", the bead goes back to the navigator rather than being
decided by the implementer (park with `needs-ui-decision` + `human` per `beads-workflow`). The new
status-line failure messages follow the established idiom and are error reporting, not design.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the diff reports or how `ChangesDialog` presents it — wrong *contents* are a second
  bead, per the bead itself.
- Redesigning the comparison interaction.
- The web build, unless increment 2 finds it faulty too.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run test:native   # if the Tauri path was touched
pnpm run check
```

Human (navigator, and this one is the acceptance): on a desktop build, import two turns of one
faction, pick the older in the Turn picker — the chip shows `71 ⇄ 70`, the Changes chip appears,
and the dialog opens with differences matching the two reports.

## Known traps

- **`desktop-shell` smoke is the WASM core in Chrome, not Tauri.** Green smoke on both projects
  proves nothing about the desktop backend. Do not "reproduce" there and conclude the bug is gone;
  the native path is `pnpm run test:native` or a real desktop build.
- **The two clearing effects fire on their dependencies, not on intent** — `applyReport` clears the
  comparison on a new working turn and `enterGame` on a game switch (by design, from ah-jg6.3's
  plan); when instrumenting, distinguish "cleared by design after X" from "cleared in the same
  render it was set".
- **Instrumentation must not land.** The temporary logging from increment 1 is removed in
  increment 6; a `console.log` in `AppShell` will trip nothing automatic and live forever.
- **A `null` from `loadImportedTurn` has two different meanings** — genuinely absent row versus a
  wire-shape/argument mismatch swallowed by normalization. The parity harness with a hand-written
  snake_case payload is how to tell them apart without a desktop build in the loop.
- **`bd heartbeat` before the native suite** — wdio runs are long, and a claim's lease is five
  minutes.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — branch from `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: With two imported turns of one faction on the desktop build, picking another turn to compare against shows the comparison on the Turn chip, shows the Changes chip, and opens a dialog listing the unit, region and order differences between the two turns; the same works in the web build; a regression test covers the fault found and fails without the fix.
notes:
Investigation (increment 1-2), findings before any fix:

Ruled OUT:
- Wire-shape/casing mismatch between core-client's Tauri adapter and core-tauri's DTOs: verified
  matching exactly (rename_all = "snake_case" on the Rust #[tauri::command] args, "camelCase" on
  the DTOs, and normalizeImportedTurnRecord in core-client/src/index.ts handles both cases).
- The two comparison-clearing effects (AppShell.tsx ~836 new-working-turn, ~1533 game-change):
  both are one-shot imperative calls inside unrelated handlers (applyReport-style flow, enterGame),
  not live effects keyed on anything handleSelectComparisonTurn touches. Not reachable from the
  turn-picker click path.
- Rust/persistence layer defect: wrote and ran a throwaway Rust test in core-tauri importing two
  turns (March=2, April=3) then loading the OLDER one (2) via command_load_imported_turn while the
  "working" turn would be 3 - passed cleanly. The existing Rust test only ever loaded the
  just-committed turn, so this scenario (load a turn OTHER than the latest) was untested but is not
  broken.
- Could not run the actual native (Tauri/WebKitGTK) suite in this environment - `test:native` is
  Linux-only per wdio.conf.ts's own comment (WKWebView on macOS exposes no automation endpoint), and
  this session is on macOS. No real desktop GUI available to click through by hand either.

CONFIRMED, real code defects (both are "silent dead end" bugs per the bead's own candidate #1 and
plan increment 5, matching "no dialog at all" exactly):
1. packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx handleSelectComparisonTurn (~2145-2179): zero
   try/catch around `await client.loadImportedTurn(...)` and the subsequent `await parse(...)`, and
   its only caller does `void handleSelectComparisonTurn(turnNumber)` (~2419). Any thrown/rejected
   error - IPC failure, JSON deserialize failure, whatever - becomes an unhandled promise rejection:
   nothing shown to the user, exactly the reported symptom. The `record === null` branch (~2167-2169)
   is the same failure mode already spelled out in the bead.
2. packages/core-client/src/index.ts `loadImportedTurn` (~1818-1824) checks only `value === null`,
   NOT `undefined` - inconsistent with the very next function, `loadLatestImportedTurn`
   (~1825-1829), whose comment explains serde_wasm_bindgen can emit either for Rust's None. If the
   adapter ever returns undefined here, normalizeImportedTurnRecord(undefined) throws, which (via
   defect #1 above) vanishes silently.

Web build (increment 2): the desktop-shell Playwright project runs the built web bundle against the
WASM core in Chrome (not the Tauri path) and already has two passing smoke tests exercising this
exact flow end-to-end ("a second turn can be compared and dismissed", "the changes dialog reads a
real pair" in tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts) - web is not reproducing the bug today.

Decision: could not get a live desktop-only repro (no macOS Tauri automation, no GUI in this
environment) beyond the two confirmed defects above, which are real, present, and match "no dialog,
not even an empty one" exactly. Proceeding per plan increment 5: fix both defects (error handling +
status-line message on every silent exit in handleSelectComparisonTurn, undefined-vs-null fix in
loadImportedTurn), with regression tests pinning each. Not a "discoverability" finding, so not
escalating to the navigator.

title: Orders export on the desktop offers no save dialog
description:
# Summary

Exporting orders from the desktop app opens no save dialog. The player picks "Export orders" (or the
long-format variant), nothing is asked, and either no file appears or one appears somewhere the
player was never told about. The orders file is the one file the whole application exists to produce
— it has to be found again and mailed to the game server — so a save the player cannot locate makes
the desktop build unusable for its main purpose without going hunting in the downloads folder.

# Cause

The machinery for this already exists and the orders export simply does not use it.
`packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts` defines a `TextFileSaver` port — "a shell that can put a file
where the player asks and say where that was" — which the desktop implements with a native dialog in
`apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts` and hands to `AppShell` as the `saveTextFile` prop
(`apps/desktop/src/App.tsx:23`). Only the **map** export uses it: `exportMap` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx:1976-1987` calls `saveTextFile` when the shell offers one
and falls back to `downloadTextFile` otherwise.

`exportOrders` (`AppShell.tsx:1911`) and `exportOrdersLong` (`AppShell.tsx:1924`) call
`downloadTextFile` unconditionally — an anchor download, which is all a browser can do but which on
the desktop reports no path and lands wherever the embedded webview puts it.

The game backup at `AppShell.tsx:1594` has the same shape and is worth deciding on in passing; the
bug as reported is the orders export.

# Scope

- Route both orders exports through `saveTextFile` when the shell provides one, falling back to
  `downloadTextFile` when it does not — the same pattern `exportMap` already uses.
- The dialog is pre-filled with the existing name, `orders-turn-<n>.txt`, and the player may change
  the name and the directory.
- A cancelled dialog writes nothing and leaves the workspace exactly as it was — no error, no
  "exported" feedback.
- The web build is unchanged: it keeps the browser download.

# Out of scope

- Changing the generated orders text, the file name scheme, or the long/plain distinction.
- Remembering the last-used directory between exports.
- The game backup export, unless it falls out for free — if it is worth doing, split a child bead.

# Validation

- `pnpm test` (or the repo's usual gate) green, with new unit coverage on `AppShell` proving the
  orders export calls the injected `saveTextFile` when present and `downloadTextFile` when absent,
  and that a cancelled save (`null`) writes nothing.
- Manual on a desktop build: load a report, edit an order, export both plain and long orders — a
  native save dialog appears each time, the chosen file exists at the chosen path with the expected
  content, and cancelling leaves no file behind.
design:
## Context

Navigator-filed P0. On the desktop, "Export orders" (plain and long) opens no save dialog: both
callbacks call `downloadTextFile` unconditionally (`AppShell.tsx`, `exportOrders` and
`exportOrdersLong`, currently near :1912 and :1925), which in the embedded webview reports no path
and lands the file wherever the webview puts it. The orders file is the artifact the whole
application exists to produce, and the machinery already exists: the `TextFileSaver` port
(`packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts:21`), implemented by the desktop with a native dialog
(`apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts`, `save` + `writeTextFile`, `null` on cancel) and handed to
`AppShell` as the `saveTextFile` prop — used today by the **map export alone** (`exportMap`,
AppShell.tsx:1976-1992: saver when present, `downloadTextFile` otherwise, cancel returns quietly).

The fix is to make the orders exports take the same fork — and to extract that fork into one shared
helper so a fourth exporter cannot get it wrong again.

Verified against the code on main at planning time; all three files read as the bead describes.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/downloadFile.ts`** — the reusable fork, beside the port it uses:

  ```ts
  /** Saves through the shell's saver when there is one, else the browser download.
   *  Resolves with the path written, "" for a browser download, or null when cancelled. */
  export async function deliverTextFile(
    saver: TextFileSaver | undefined,
    fileName: string,
    text: string,
    mimeType: string,
    download: typeof downloadTextFile = downloadTextFile
  ): Promise<string | null>
  ```

  The `download` parameter exists for the tests (vitest runs without a DOM; `downloadTextFile`
  touches `document`) and defaults to the real one — callers never pass it.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** — three edits:
  - `exportOrders` and `exportOrdersLong` become async and call
    `deliverTextFile(saveTextFile, name, text, "text/plain")`. A cancelled save resolves `null` and
    nothing else happens — no error, no feedback, the workspace untouched (the bead's requirement).
    A failed native write is caught and logged (`console.error`); richer failure surfacing is out of
    scope and matches the download path, which has no failure signal either.
  - `exportMap` swaps its inline fork for the same helper — behaviour identical: `null` leaves the
    export dialog standing, a path (or `""` from the download branch) closes it. Its existing
    comment block moves to the helper.
  - The file name stays `orders-turn-<n>.txt` for both orders exports (same name on purpose — the
    doc comment at `exportOrdersLong` explains why; do not "fix" it).
- **Nothing changes in `apps/desktop/`** — `desktopTextFileSaver` already pre-fills
  `defaultPath: fileName` and lets the player change name and directory, and already returns `null`
  on cancel without writing.
- **The web build is unchanged by construction**: `saveTextFile` is `undefined` there, so
  `deliverTextFile` takes the download branch.

## Increments

1. **The fork, alone.** Opening failing test: `downloadFile.test.ts` (new) › "delivers through the
   saver when there is one" — injected saver resolves a path, injected download must not be called;
   siblings: "falls back to the download without a saver" (download called once with name, text,
   mime; resolves `""`), "a cancelled save downloads nothing" (saver resolves `null`, download not
   called, result `null`). GREEN: `deliverTextFile`.
2. **The orders exports take it.** Opening failing test: in the AppShell test suite
   (`AppShell.test.ts`, or a focused new file following its pattern) › "the orders export saves
   through the shell's saver when present" and "…downloads in a browser shell" — render the shell
   with/without a stubbed `saveTextFile` prop, trigger the export, assert which path ran and that a
   `null` (cancel) leaves no other observable effect. GREEN: the two callbacks rewritten.
3. **The map export reuses it.** No new behaviour — opening check is the existing map-export tests
   staying green after the swap, plus one assertion that a cancelled save still leaves the export
   dialog open (pin it if no existing test does).

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, `packages/shared`):
- `downloadFile.test.ts` — the three fork cases above, plus "a saver that throws rejects into the
  caller's catch" so increment 2's logging path is honest.
- The AppShell-level export tests from increment 2; every existing export/menu test stays green.

Smoke (Playwright): none new — the suite runs the web build, where behaviour is unchanged; the
existing export-menu smoke coverage is the regression net.

Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke` (unchanged, must stay green); full `pnpm run check`
before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None to ask: the dialog is the OS's own, the pre-filled name, cancel behaviour and web fallback are
all specified in the navigator's own bug report (gh-issue-shaped bead description), and no new
surface is added. The navigator ranked this P0 on 2026-08-14.

Decided in passing, as the bead invites: the **game backup export** (`AppShell.tsx:1594`, same
shape) is *not* folded in — it is split out as its own unranked bead (see Out of scope) so this fix
stays exactly the reported defect.

## Out of scope

- The game backup export — split to bead `ah-7pa`'s sibling created at P4 during planning (titled
  "Game backup export bypasses the desktop save dialog"); it will reuse `deliverTextFile` and is
  trivial once this lands.
- Changing the orders text, the name scheme, or the long/plain distinction.
- Remembering the last-used directory between exports.
- Any new failure UI for a failed disk write.
- Automating the native dialog in tests — the OS dialog cannot be driven by the suites; the manual
  check below covers it.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check   # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, on a desktop build — the part no suite can reach): load a report, export
orders plain and long — a native dialog appears each time, pre-filled `orders-turn-<n>.txt`, the
chosen file exists at the chosen path with the expected content; cancel leaves no file and no
message; the web build still plainly downloads.

## Known traps

- **`downloadTextFile` touches `document`** — a node-env vitest test that lets the real fallback
  run dies on it; the injected `download` parameter exists precisely so tests never do. Do not
  switch the suite to jsdom for this.
- **The two orders callbacks become async** — they are wired into `ExportMenu` handlers; fire-and-
  forget is fine, but an unhandled rejection is not: the catch in increment 2 is load-bearing, and
  the "saver that throws" unit test keeps it from being simplified away.
- **A cancelled map save must keep the export dialog open** (the comment in `exportMap` says why);
  when swapping in the helper, preserve the `null → return` before `setExportOpen(false)`.
- **Do not deliver the orders export through a new name** — plain and long share
  `orders-turn-<n>.txt` deliberately (`exportOrdersLong`'s doc comment).
- **The desktop bundle also runs as a plain web page** (dev server, smoke preview) —
  `desktopTextFileSaver` returns `undefined` without a Tauri runtime, so never gate on "is the
  desktop build" — gate on the saver's presence, as `exportMap` does.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree; branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: Exporting orders (plain or long) in the desktop app opens a native save dialog pre-filled with orders-turn-<n>.txt; the player can change name and directory; the file is written where they chose; cancelling writes nothing and shows no error; the web build still downloads as before.

title: Status bar wraps and faction dropdown resizes to avoid clipped content
description:
The top status bar (import/export buttons etc.) can get wider than the window, and currently just overflows/gets clipped instead of adapting. Similarly, the faction info dropdown (opened by clicking the faction name) is a fixed, short height that forces scrolling to see all faction details.

Reported by rmstdope (Henrik Kurelid) in GitHub issue #188.
design:
## Context

GitHub issue #188 (the navigator's own report) names two defects in shipped UI, and the navigator
ranked this bead P0. First: the top status bar (`AppHeader`) is a single fixed-height flex row with
`whitespace-nowrap` and no wrapping or shrinking anywhere, so on a window narrower than its content
the right-hand end — the Export button, the settings gear — is simply clipped off-screen. Second: the
faction view's scroll body is capped at `max-h-[40vh]`, so with a real faction (32 declared attitudes
in the turn-71 fixture) it always scrolls, even when the window below it is mostly empty.

The navigator chose the treatments, mockup at `docs/ui/status-bar-wrap.html` (merged via PR #190):

1. **Grouped wrap.** The header becomes two groups — game state on the left (wordmark, game
   indicator, turn, faction, merged/import-status/messages/problems/battles chips), actions on the
   right (Import, Export, settings gear). When the window is too narrow, the actions group drops to a
   second row **as one unit and stays right-aligned**; the game-state group may also wrap internally
   on very narrow windows. One row whenever everything fits, exactly as today.
2. **Popovers grow to the window.** The fixed-percentage caps go: a popover body's ceiling becomes
   the viewport height minus a small fixed allowance, so it scrolls only when genuinely out of room.
   The navigator chose to apply this to **all four capped header popovers**: FactionPanel (40vh),
   MergedFactionsPanel (40vh), ProblemsPanel (50vh), TurnMessagesPanel (60vh).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx` — the whole change to the bar lives here. Today the
  root (line ~213) is `flex h-9 flex-none items-center gap-3.5 border-b border-edge bg-panel px-3
  text-[11.5px] whitespace-nowrap` with a `<span className="flex-1" />` spacer (line ~409) splitting
  left from right. Restructure: root becomes wrapping (`flex flex-wrap`, `min-h-9` instead of `h-9`,
  keep `flex-none items-center gap-x-3.5 ... whitespace-nowrap`); the elements up to and including the
  battles chip go into a game-state group (`flex h-9 flex-wrap items-center gap-3.5 min-w-0`); the
  hidden file input, Import, Export wrapper and settings wrapper go into an actions group
  (`ml-auto flex h-9 items-center gap-3.5`). `ml-auto` replaces the `flex-1` spacer — it right-aligns
  the group on a shared row *and* after wrapping to its own row; delete the spacer. Give the actions
  group `data-testid="header-actions"`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/GameGate.tsx` (line ~46) — duplicates the header class string
  verbatim for the no-game screen. Mirror the root-class change (`h-9` → `min-h-9`, add `flex-wrap`)
  so the two headers cannot drift; it has no actions group to build.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/FactionPanel.tsx` (line ~92, `max-h-[40vh] overflow-y-auto p-2`),
  `MergedFactionsPanel.tsx` (line ~80), `ProblemsPanel.tsx` (line ~86), `TurnMessagesPanel.tsx`
  (line ~117) — replace each cap with the shared clamp described below.
- **The clamp**: add `export const POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H = "max-h-[calc(100vh-6rem)]"` to
  `packages/shared/src/workspace/primitives.tsx` (the existing shared-primitives home) and use it in
  all four panels. `6rem` = up to two 36px header rows plus the `mt-1` anchor gap plus ~20px of
  breathing room at the window's bottom edge — a pure-CSS clamp, no JS measurement. Tailwind v4 scans
  source text for class literals (`@source` in `theme.css`), so the literal must appear in the
  constant's definition (it does) — do not build the class name by string concatenation.
- **Reuse, don't invent**: the popovers' anchoring (`absolute left-0 top-full z-20 mt-1 ...`),
  dismissal effects and drag-propagation guards are all untouched. No new popover component, no
  collision arithmetic (`unitTooltip.ts` stays where it is), no breakpoint utilities.

## Increments

1. **The header wraps as two groups.** Opening failing test:
   `AppHeader.test.tsx` › "the header wraps and keeps the actions grouped right" — render via the
   existing `draw()` helper, assert the root's class contains `flex-wrap` and `min-h-9` and no longer
   contains bare `h-9` on the root, and that a `header-actions` element carrying `ml-auto` contains
   the Export menu trigger. Then restructure `AppHeader.tsx`, mirror the root class in `GameGate.tsx`
   (assert its markup too — it renders standalone, cheap to snapshot the class), run the full
   AppHeader/GameGate unit suites green.
2. **Narrow-window smoke.** Opening failing test: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` › "a narrow window
   wraps the header instead of clipping it" — `page.setViewportSize({ width: 520, height: 720 })`,
   then assert `export-menu` and `settings-indicator` have bounding boxes fully inside the viewport
   (x + width ≤ 520), and that `app-header`'s bounding-box height is greater than one row (> 40px),
   proving the wrap rather than a shrink. This should go green with increment 1's code; if it does
   not, the code is wrong, not the test.
3. **Popover bodies grow to the window.** Opening failing test: `FactionPanel.test.tsx` › "the body
   is clamped to the window, not to 40vh" — assert the rendered body class contains
   `max-h-[calc(100vh-6rem)]` and not `max-h-[40vh]`. Add the `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H` constant, apply to
   all four panels, with matching one-line class assertions in the other three panels' test files
   (create a minimal test file where one does not exist).
4. **Faction-view height smoke.** Opening failing test: `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` › "the
   faction view uses the window before it scrolls" — at the default 1280×720 viewport open the
   faction chip (the existing test at :230 shows how), and assert the panel's footnote line
   ("⌂ marks a faction…", give it a testid if it lacks one) is in the viewport via
   `toBeInViewport()` — with 32 attitudes that line sits below the old 40vh cap, so this fails
   against the old clamp and passes with the new one. Also assert the panel's bounding-box bottom
   ≤ 720, pinning "grows but never past the window".

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, SSR string assertions — the house style in these files):
- `AppHeader.test.tsx`: the new wrap/grouping test above; the two existing faction-chip tests must
  stay green (the chip markup is untouched).
- `GameGate` class-parity assertion (in its existing test file if present, else a new minimal one).
- `FactionPanel.test.tsx`: the clamp test; all 11 existing content tests stay green.
- Class assertions for `MergedFactionsPanel`, `ProblemsPanel`, `TurnMessagesPanel`.

Smoke (Playwright, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, both `web` and `desktop-shell` projects):
- The two new tests from increments 2 and 4.
- The existing faction-view tests (:230–:300) and every header-text assertion must stay green — the
  header's *content* and testids are unchanged, only its layout containers move.

Suites to run: `pnpm run test` (unit) and `pnpm run test:smoke` at minimum; full gate before PR.

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator, 2026-08-14; mockup committed at `docs/ui/status-bar-wrap.html`
(PR #190):
- Wrap treatment: **B, grouped wrap** — actions drop as one right-aligned unit — over A, free flow.
- Panel height: **grow to the window** with a small bottom margin, over merely raising the cap.
- Scope of the height fix: **all four capped header popovers**, not the faction view alone.

## Out of scope

- `ExportMenu`, `GamePicker`, `BadgeMenu` — short fixed menus with no vh cap; they don't scroll today
  and gain nothing from the clamp.
- Truncating or abbreviating long faction/game names (`truncate`/`min-w-0` ellipsis work): the chosen
  fix is wrapping, not shrinking.
- Any collision/flip logic for popovers near the window's right edge (the `w-80` panels can still
  clip horizontally on very narrow windows — a separate defect if the navigator ever reports it).
- `ShortcutHelp`, `UnitTooltip`, and the workspace dock panels — already viewport-aware or unaffected.
- Mobile breakpoints/responsive work anywhere else in the app.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run lint
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check        # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, post-merge is fine): drag the window narrow — the Import/Export/⚙ group drops
to a second right-aligned row and nothing clips; open the faction view on the turn-71 fixture — all
five attitude levels visible without scrolling on a 720px-tall window.

## Known traps

- **The `<header>` is the file drop target** (`onDragOver`/`onDrop` on the root). The new group
  wrappers must not swallow or stop those events; the popovers already `stopPropagation` deliberately
  — leave that alone.
- **Popover dismissal keys off `panelRef.current.parentElement`** (comment at AppHeader.tsx:254–259):
  each chip's own `relative` wrapper must remain its popover's *direct* parent. Wrapping a new flex
  group *around* those wrappers is safe; merging or re-parenting them breaks outside-press dismissal
  for both faction popovers.
- **`GameGate.tsx:46` duplicates the header class string.** Change it in step with AppHeader or the
  no-game screen keeps the old fixed-height bar.
- **`AppHeader.test.tsx`'s `draw()` hand-builds the full ~30-prop object**, so any new AppHeader prop
  breaks that file — this plan adds none, and none should be needed.
- **No narrow-viewport Playwright project exists** (both projects are Desktop Chrome 1280×720): the
  narrow test must call `page.setViewportSize` itself and must not assume other tests' viewport.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled** — a `test:pwa` run
  straight after a smoke run fails with worker timeouts that look real; run `pnpm run check`'s order
  or rebuild between.
- **Tailwind v4, no config file**: class literals must appear verbatim in scanned source
  (`@source` globs in `theme.css`). Keep `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H` a single literal; never assemble
  `max-h-[calc(...)]` from pieces.
acceptance_criteria:
- When the status bar's contents (import/export buttons, faction info, etc.) exceed the available window width, it wraps to a second row instead of overflowing or requiring the window to be resized.
- The faction info dropdown (opened by clicking the faction name) extends further downward to show more/all of its content before falling back to internal scrolling.
- Both behaviours verified at a few window sizes, including a narrow one that currently triggers the clipping.

title: Battles view: unscrollable side lists, empty assassinations, split routs
description:
# Summary

The battles view (`BattlesDialog`, delivered by ah-1is.2 in PR #173) has five defects that make
larger and unusual battles unreadable. Reported by the navigator from a real turn report.

# The defects

1. **The ATTACKERS and DEFENDERS lists do not scroll.** Past roughly ten entries per side the rows
   are compressed on top of each other instead of the list scrolling, and the side becomes
   unreadable. Each list needs its own scroll region with a sane minimum row height.

2. **Outcome is below the rounds.** The outcome section should come *before* the round-by-round
   detail — it is what the reader wants first, and the rounds are the supporting detail.

3. **Assassinations render almost empty.** An assassination shows no attackers and no defenders,
   and the outcome shows only the bare word "Casualties" with nothing after it. Expected:
   - Attackers: when the assassin is unknown (as it is for the victim's faction), show `?`.
   - Defenders: show the assassinated unit.
   - Outcome: the actual casualties, not a bare heading.

4. **The right-hand panel keeps its scroll position across battles.** Switching to another battle in
   the list should always start the detail panel back at the top; today it stays wherever the
   previous battle was scrolled to, so a new battle can open mid-way down.

5. **A rout is parsed as a separate battle.** When a side is routed the rout appears as its own
   entry in the battle list instead of being folded into the battle it came from. The rout belongs
   to the originating battle.

# Scope

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/BattlesDialog.tsx` — 1, 2, 3 (rendering), 4
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.ts` — 3 (assassination shape), 5 (rout grouping)
- `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` — only if the assassination/rout defects turn out to originate
  in the parser rather than in the TS layer; check before changing it.

# Out of scope

- Any redesign of the battles view beyond these five fixes.
- New battle information not already present in the report.

# Validation

- `pnpm test` (or the workspace's test task) covering `battles.test.ts` and `BattlesDialog.test.tsx`
- Manual: open a turn report containing (a) a battle with more than ten units per side,
  (b) an assassination, (c) a battle ending in a rout; confirm each renders as described above.
design:
## Context

The battles view (`BattlesDialog`, ah-1is.2, PR #173) fails on real turn reports in five ways the
navigator reported from play: side rosters compress instead of scrolling, the outcome sits below the
round-by-round detail, assassinations render as empty sections, the detail panel keeps its scroll
position when switching battles, and a rout is split off as a battle of its own. When this lands,
large battles, assassinations and routs all read correctly from the fixtures we already have.

Root causes, confirmed by reading the code and fixtures:

1. **Unscrollable rosters** — the roster `<ul>` (BattlesDialog.tsx ~line 286) is a bounded flex
   column (`flex max-h-48 ... overflow-y-auto`) and each `<li>` has `overflow-hidden`, so flexbox
   *shrinks the rows* to fit `max-h-48` instead of overflowing into the scroll. Rows need
   `shrink-0`.
2. **Outcome below rounds** — plain ordering of blocks in `BattleDetail`.
3. **Empty assassinations** — a victim-side assassination is a one-line battle,
   `L Arslan (1446) is assassinated in forest (43,79) in Utso!` (fixture
   `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f39-t17.rep` line 113; also `g7-f62-t20` line 34,
   `g3-f42-t82` line 277). `parse_headline` in `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` only knows the
   `attacks` form, so every structured field is `None` and the view renders empty ATTACKERS,
   DEFENDERS and a bare "Casualties" heading.
4. **Sticky scroll** — `BattleDetail` is one component reused across selections; its scroll
   container is never reset. Remounting it per battle (React `key`) resets scrollTop for free.
5. **Split routs** — `opens_a_battle` treats any indent-0 line ending in `!` (except
   `is destroyed!`) as a new headline. `Informator (1470) is routed!` appears mid-battle (same
   fixture, line 71), followed by `The Explorers (6363) gets a free round of attacks.`, a losses
   line, and a `Free round statistics:` block — all of which currently become a nonsense second
   battle.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/src/report/battle.rs` — the parser fixes (defects 3 and 5).
  - Reuse `split_trailing_id` and `parse_coordinate` (already imported) for the assassination
    headline; the location tail `in <terrain> (<x>,<y>) in <province>` has the same shape the
    `attacks` arm already parses — factor that tail parse out of `parse_headline` and share it.
  - Add `pub assassination: bool` to `Battle` with `#[serde(default)]`.
  - In `opens_a_battle`, exclude `is routed!` the same way `is destroyed!` is excluded.
  - In `parse_one_battle`, a body ending in `is routed!` closes the current round and opens a new
    `BattleRound { number: None, .. }` (phase `Round`) with the rout line as its first `lines`
    entry; the label `Free round statistics` switches to `Phase::RoundStatistics` (extend the
    `strip_suffix(" statistics")` arm: `"Free round"` is valid alongside `Round N`).
- `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` — mirror the new field on the `Battle` type (~line 492):
  `assassination?: boolean` (optional, because stored `parsedPayloadJson` from imports made before
  this change lacks the key). No other TS layer touches the wire shape — `crates/core-wasm`
  serializes `ParsedReport` generically via `serde_json`, so nothing there changes.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/battles.ts` — the view logic, kept DOM-free per this file's own
  doc comment:
  - `roundLabel(round, index): string` — `"Free round"` when `number` is null, else
