- **`get-buffer-window-list`'s third argument must be `t`** (all frames), as the beads-panel loop
  does — the navigator may have the fleet view on another frame.
- **Two-PR delivery**: the bead is not done when the cerebro PR merges — the fleet runs whatever
  the submodule pointer names, so without the bump PR in atlantis-hud the fix is invisible.
  Close the bead only after the bump lands.
acceptance_criteria: With an agent other than the first selected, leaving the fleet window and returning leaves that same agent selected. An automatic refresh while the window is not selected does not move the selection either.

title: Right-clicking a hex centres the map on it without selecting
description:
Bringing a distant hex to the middle of the view is a manual pan today. There is no single gesture
that says "look at this one".

**The request:** right-clicking in a hex centres the map on that hex.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- Does right-click also *select* the hex, or centre only and leave the selection alone?
- Does the map jump or animate to the new centre?
- What does right-click on the map do today, and is that being replaced or is this an addition?
- Right-click outside the map, or on a hex the map cannot centre on (an edge hex, where centring
  would scroll past the boundary) — what happens?

## Validation

Manual: right-click a hex near the edge of the view and confirm the map centres on it.
design:
## Context

Bringing a distant hex to the middle of the view is a manual pan today; there is no single gesture
for "look at this one". Right-click currently does **nothing** in the app — `onPointerDown`
(`MapCanvas.tsx:515-561`) early-returns on `event.button !== 0`, no `contextmenu` handler exists
anywhere in the repository (shared, apps/web, apps/desktop, or the Rust shell), and the browser or
WKWebView shows its native context menu. So this gesture replaces nothing; suppressing the native
menu over the map is part of the work.

Chosen behaviour (all settled with the navigator, mockup at `docs/ui/map-recentre.html`, merged in
PR #245): right-clicking a hex **instantly centres the view on it, without selecting it**;
Ctrl+click on macOS is treated as right-click; the gesture always centres — known hexes and
unexplored ground alike, even when the hex is already visible.

Almost everything needed already exists: `centreOn(...)` in `mapViewport.ts` is a pure function the
selection-follow effect already uses, and `coordinateAt(...)` already resolves an arbitrary point
on the map to a hex. The work is one event handler, a small pure helper, a guide row, and tests.

All line numbers are against `origin/main` (commit `f44e917`, and re-verified below where it
matters); the working tree can lag — verify with `git show origin/main:<path>` if a number looks
off.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapViewport.ts` — nothing to change, everything to reuse

- `centreOn(coordinate, viewport, width, height, insets = NO_INSETS): Viewport` (lines 256–271).
  Pure; keeps `viewport.step`; no bounds clamp, so an edge hex centres with fog around it —
  consistent with the keyboard cursor, and explicitly chosen by the navigator.
- `coordinateAt(x, y, viewport, level)` (lines 154–183) — point → nearest even-parity hex
  coordinate; this is how the unexplored-ground click already resolves (`MapCanvas.tsx:743-763`).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapRecentre.ts` — new, one pure decision helper

The one genuinely new decision is "which pointer events count as the gesture", and it should be
testable without a DOM:

```ts
/**
 * True when the event is the recentre gesture: the secondary button's contextmenu, or a
 * Ctrl+click on macOS (the platform synonym, which would otherwise fall through and select).
 */
export function isRecentreGesture(ev: { button: number; ctrlKey: boolean }, isMac: boolean): boolean;
```

Rules: a `contextmenu` event (any platform) → true. For the click path: `isMac && ctrlKey &&
button === 0` → true. Reuse `isMacPlatform()` from `packages/shared/src/shortcuts.ts` (line 140)
at the call site — pass its result in, keep the helper pure.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` — the handler

- Add `onContextMenu` to the root `<svg>` (line 688, next to `onPointerDown`). React attaches
  `contextmenu` normally (it is **not** in React's passive-event set, unlike `wheel` — see the
  comment at lines 436–437), so a React prop works; no manual listener needed. Handler:
  1. `event.preventDefault()` — always, over the whole map surface, so the native menu never
     appears there (this includes the fog rect and the rulers; the navigator chose the gesture, and
     a menu popping on fog but not hexes would be incoherent).
  2. Resolve the hex exactly as the fog-rect click does (lines 743–763): `const bounds =
     event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()`, then `coordinateAt(event.clientX - bounds.left,
     event.clientY - bounds.top, viewRef.current, level)`. This works uniformly for known hexes and
     unexplored ground — no per-polygon handler needed, and the polygons' own `onClick` is not
     involved because `click` does not fire for the secondary button.
  3. `commit(centreOn(coordinate, viewRef.current, size.width, size.height, readInsets()))` —
     the same call shape as the selection-follow effect (lines 413–434), **including
     `readInsets()`**: "centre" means the centre of the map area the panes leave visible, not the
     centre of the window. Unlike selection-follow, no `isOffScreen` gate — the navigator chose
     always-centre. `commit` (lines 291–302) already persists the view via `saveViewportForGame`,
     which is the established behaviour for every view change and stays.
- Ctrl+click on macOS: in the two `onClick` handlers (fog rect at 743–763, hex polygon at
  995–1004), when `isRecentreGesture({button: 0, ctrlKey: event.ctrlKey}, isMacPlatform())`,
  centre (same as step 3) **instead of** selecting, and return. Note macOS Chromium/WebKit
  usually deliver Ctrl+primary-click as a `contextmenu` event already — the click-path check is
  the belt to that suspender; both paths must behave identically, and the no-select rule is the
  point.
- Selection, `selectionEpoch`, the cursor and `mapFocused` are all untouched — centring only.
  Do not set `draggedRef`; a right-click is not a drag and must not suppress a following
  left-click's select.

### `packages/shared/src/navigationGuide.ts` — the guide row

`NAVIGATION_MOVES`, `MAP` group (constant at line 40; entries at 67–131). Insert after `mapPan`
(lines 67–73), before `mapZoom`. Agreed words, verbatim:

```ts
{
  id: "mapCentre",
  group: MAP,
  description: "Bring a hex to the middle of the view",
  mouse: "Right-click it",
  keys: null
}
```

("(or Ctrl+click)" was offered for the mouse text and declined.) `navigationGuide.test.ts:18-31`
requires non-empty description/group, one of mouse/keys non-null, unique ids — all satisfied; add
the id to the fixed id list at `navigationGuide.test.ts:43-49`, which is the idiom. The module's
header contract requires the smoke suite to perform the gesture — increment 3 does.

## Increments

1. **The gesture predicate.** Failing test first: `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapRecentre.test.ts`
   — `describe("isRecentreGesture")`: `"a contextmenu event centres on every platform"`,
   `"Ctrl+click is the gesture on macOS"`, `"Ctrl+click is not the gesture elsewhere"`,
   `"a plain left click never is"`. Then the helper.
2. **The handler.** Failing test in `MapCanvas.test.tsx` (which today has no pointer tests — this
   adds the first; render with `@testing-library/react` as the selection-ring tests there do):
   `"right-click centres the view without selecting"` — render with a spy `onSelectRegion`,
   dispatch `contextmenu` on the svg root at a known offset, assert the `map-world` group's
   `transform` changed and the spy was **not** called, and that `preventDefault` fired (dispatch a
   cancelable event and check `defaultPrevented`). Then the `onContextMenu` handler and the two
   Ctrl+click branches.
3. **Smoke + guide.** Failing browser test first, in `tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts` inside
   `"the map really answers the gestures the overlay describes"` (line 171) — the canonical home
   for gesture/guide parity. Using the file's own helpers (`hex()` bounding box, and
   `mapView(page)`-style transform reading as in `persistence.spec.ts:102-109`): read the
   `map-world` transform, `page.mouse.click(x, y, { button: "right" })` on a hex away from centre,
   poll that the transform changed; assert the previously selected hex still has
   `aria-pressed="true"` (centre-only); right-click the same spot again and assert the transform
   is now stable (already centred → idempotent). Then add the `navigationGuide.ts` row and its id
   to the test's id list.

## The test plan

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapRecentre.test.ts` — increment 1, pure.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.test.tsx` — increment 2: centres, does not select,
  suppresses the menu.
- `packages/shared/src/navigationGuide.test.ts` — the new id in the fixed list; existing
  invariants stay green.
- `tests/smoke/shortcuts.spec.ts` — increment 3, Chromium and WebKit.
- Run: `pnpm -C packages/shared test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`, `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Mockup: `docs/ui/map-recentre.html` (PR #245) — live figures; the "Decisions" paragraph in the
file records the outcome. The interview:

1. **Centre only, never select** — chosen over "centre and select" (rejected: glancing at a
   distant hex would silently swap the unit list and orders editor under the player). The white
   selection ring stays where it was.
2. **Instant jump** — chosen over a ~250ms glide (rejected: every other map movement is instant;
   the map would gain two speeds and its first transform animation).
3. **Ctrl+click on macOS is the gesture** — chosen over leaving it selecting (rejected: the
   platform synonym doing something different from right-click reads as a bug on a Mac trackpad).
4. **Always centres, including unexplored ground and already-visible hexes** — chosen over
   known-hexes-only (rejected: the keyboard cursor already walks onto fog; the gesture should not
   lag the app's own model). Edge hexes centre with fog around them — `centreOn` has no bounds
   clamp and that is deliberate.
5. **Guide row**, verbatim: description `"Bring a hex to the middle of the view"`, mouse
   `"Right-click it"`, no keyboard chord — chosen as quoted; mentioning Ctrl+click was declined.
6. Implied and stated to the navigator: the native context menu no longer appears over the map.
   No replacement menu is added.

## Out of scope

- Any context *menu* of our own — the gesture centres, nothing more.
- Animating the centring (explicitly declined), or animating any other view change.
- Changing selection-follow, `frameAll`, keyboard-cursor behaviour, or pan/zoom.
- A keyboard chord for centring (the `0`/frameAll key already exists for the whole-map version).
- Suppressing the context menu anywhere outside the map svg (panels, editor, dialogs keep the
  native menu — the orders editor's spellcheck-style menu must not be harmed).

## Validation

- `pnpm -C packages/shared test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`, `pnpm run check` — all green.
- Human check, web and desktop shells: right-click a far hex — the view jumps so the hex sits
  centred in the area between the side panes, the selection ring does not move, no browser menu
  appears; right-click bare fog — same; right-click over a pane — the native menu still appears
  (panes are outside the svg); on a Mac, Ctrl+click a hex — centres, does not select; reload —
  the centred view was remembered (existing viewport persistence); press ⌘/ — "Bring a hex to the
  middle of the view / Right-click it" listed under The map.

## Known traps

- **`click` never fires for the secondary button** — the per-hex `onClick` path cannot see a
  right-click, which is why the handler lives on the svg root's `onContextMenu` and resolves the
  hex arithmetically via `coordinateAt`, exactly as the fog rect does. Do not try to add
  `onContextMenu` to a thousand hit polygons.
- **React's passive-event trap does not apply here**: `wheel` needed a manual non-passive listener
  (comment at `MapCanvas.tsx:436-437`), but `contextmenu` is not passive — a plain React
  `onContextMenu` prop with `preventDefault()` works, in Chromium and WKWebView both.
- **macOS delivers Ctrl+click as `contextmenu`** in Chromium and WebKit, so the click-path
  Ctrl+check will rarely fire there — keep it anyway (belt and suspenders across
  browsers/webviews), and make both paths identical: centre, never select. The smoke suite runs
  Chromium and WebKit on macOS; if the Ctrl+click smoke assertion proves undrivable via
  `page.mouse` (modifier synthesis differs per driver), cover Ctrl+click in the unit test only —
  the right-button path is the one the guide advertises and the one the smoke test must witness.
- **Do not set `draggedRef` in the new handler** — it exists to stop a pan from selecting on
  release (`MapCanvas.tsx:522`, `748`, `996`); setting it from a right-click would swallow the
  player's next legitimate left-click select.
- **`commit` persists**: every centring writes `atlantis-hud-viewport-<gameId>` via
  `saveViewportForGame` (`commit`, `MapCanvas.tsx:291-302`). That is correct and chosen — but it
  means the smoke test's reload assertions interact with it; reset or re-read the view rather than
  assuming the pre-click transform survives a reload.
- **`readInsets()` matters**: centring without insets puts the hex behind the right rail at
  default widths (the selection-follow effect passes insets for exactly this reason; the keyboard
  cursor path at ~line 626-628 does not, a known inconsistency — do not copy it).
- **Line-number drift**: ah-h8z ("rails resize by a grip", planned, may merge before this builds)
  touches `AppShell.tsx`, `navigationGuide.ts` and the smoke files. Numbers here are from
  `origin/main` at `f44e917`; re-verify before relying on one, especially in
  `navigationGuide.ts` where ah-h8z inserts its own row under a different group.
acceptance_criteria: Right-clicking a hex centres the map on that hex.

title: Order text starts 6px from the editor's edge, errors marked by a slim bar
description:
# Summary

The order editor still wastes horizontal room to the left of the text, in a panel that has little to
spare. `ah-jb1` (PR #215) shrank the lint gutter from CodeMirror's stock 1.4em to 1.1em and the
navigator reports the result is not enough — issue gh-205 is still open, and this bead is the second
pass at it.

Three routes exist and they are not exclusive. **Which combination ships is a user-facing decision
and belongs to the navigator**, taken in an interactive design session with mockups — see *How this
one is planned*.

# What the margin is actually made of

Measured from the stylesheets, per line, before the first character, at the panel's 11.5px font:

| Contributor | Width | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `.cm-gutter-lint` | 1.1em ≈ 12.7px | `OrdersEditor.tsx:163` — already reduced by `ah-jb1` |
| `.cm-line` padding-left | 6px | CodeMirror's base theme; **never overridden in this repo** |
| container border | 1px | `OrdersEditor.tsx:301` |

`.cm-content` is `padding: 4px 0` and contributes nothing horizontally. So about **19.7px**, of which
`ah-jb1` only ever addressed the first row.

**The gutter is fixed-width and always present**, whether or not the unit has an error: the margin is
permanent and the dot is occasional. That is the heart of the complaint.

# The three routes

## A. Reduce further

- **`.cm-line { padding: 0 2px 0 6px }` is CodeMirror's, untouched here.** Overriding padding-left to
  2px or 0 is the largest remaining win and independent of everything else — roughly a third of what
  is left, with no effect on the marker.
- **A narrower marker shrinks the gutter with it.** 1.1em exists to hold a 1em marker; a glyph half
  that wide takes the gutter with it.
- **Or drop the lint gutter entirely.** Errors already carry a themed squiggly underline
  (`.cm-lintRange-error` → `--color-danger`), so the indication survives with no gutter at all and
  all 12.7px comes back. This is the biggest win and the biggest change in what the player sees.

## B. Move the marker to the right

Supported by CodeMirror natively: `gutter()` takes `side: "after"` and renders into a
`.cm-gutters-after` container (`insetInlineEnd: 0`). Two things the plan must account for:

- **`lintGutter()` does not expose it.** Its config is `hoverTime`/`markerFilter`/`tooltipFilter`
  only, and the marker `StateField` is not exported, so this means replacing `lintGutter()` with our
  own `gutter()`. That is feasible — `OrdersEditor` already computes the diagnostics it passes to
  `setDiagnostics` — but the hover tooltip that shows the message is internal to the package and
  would have to be rebuilt with `hoverTooltip`.
- **It reclaims no width.** `.cm-gutters` is `flexShrink: 0` in the scroller's flex row, so an
  after-gutter takes the same space from the text, on the other side. It buys a text column flush to
  the left edge, not more room. If width is the goal, this is route A; if a clean left edge is the
  goal, this is the one.

## C. Replace the symbol

Pure CSS, a few lines in the `EditorView.theme` block already at `OrdersEditor.tsx:145-181`. The dot
is `content: url("data:image/svg+xml,…")` on `.cm-lint-marker-error` — a circle, fill `#f87`, stroke
`#f43`. Any inline SVG or text glyph can replace it, and `.cm-lint-marker`'s 1em box can shrink with
it.

Worth doing whatever else is chosen: **that dot is the only hardcoded colour left in the editor's
chrome.** Everything else there already follows the theme tokens, so a replacement drawn in
`var(--color-danger)` removes an inconsistency as a side effect.

# How this one is planned

**The navigator has asked for an interactive design session with mockups.** This is not a bead to
plan from the description alone: the routes above trade width against how an error announces itself,
and that trade is the navigator's.

So the planning session builds `docs/ui`-style HTML mockups of the editor's left edge and iterates
them with the navigator, at minimum showing:

- the present state, as the baseline everything is judged against;
- text flush left with the marker moved right;
- a narrower or different symbol, at the sizes being proposed;
- no gutter at all, error shown by the underline alone;

each in **both** the error and the no-error state, since the no-error state is what the player looks
at almost all of the time and is where the permanent margin is actually felt. Mockups are linked as
`file://` URLs and iterated until the navigator has chosen — the wording of any tooltip and the shape
and colour of the symbol included.

The plan then records what was chosen **and what was rejected and why**, so an implementer meeting
the same fork does not reopen it.

# Out of scope

- The rest of the orders panel — the status line, the panel chrome, the collapsible header.
- The units table and the split between the panels (`ah-13o` covers the resizable split).
- Diagnostics themselves: what counts as an error, how they are computed, the underline's own
  styling beyond any colour change the chosen symbol implies.

# Known traps

- **A smoke test pins both the width and the marker's visibility.**
  `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:164-176` asserts `.cm-lint-marker` is visible and
  `.cm-gutter-lint` is under 14px, written deliberately so "a future shrink cannot hide the indicator
  to win the width". Routes A-drop-the-gutter and B both invalidate it. That test encodes a decision,
  so changing it is a deliberate reversal to be named in the plan, never a quiet edit to make a suite
  pass.
- **Replacing `lintGutter()` loses more than the gutter.** The hover tooltip, the marker filters and
  the gutter's own click behaviour all come with it.
- **The editor is rebuilt per unit** (`useEffect` keyed on `unitId`, `OrdersEditor.tsx:98-192`), so a
  theme change applies on the next unit selection; a manual check must switch units rather than trust
  a hot reload.
- **`theme.test.ts` scans components for hardcoded colours** and cannot see styles injected through
  `EditorView.theme`. The rule still applies in spirit: use the tokens.

# Validation

- Smoke coverage for whatever is chosen, replacing the pinned assertions above rather than deleting
  them: the error indication is present and findable, and the left edge is within the agreed budget.
- Manually, in both themes and at a narrow window: a unit with no errors, a unit with one, and a unit
  with several — confirming the margin the navigator approved and that an error is still obvious.
- `pnpm run ci` green, smoke suites included.
design:
## Context

Second pass at gh-205: after ah-jb1 (PR #215) shrank the lint gutter to 1.1em, the order editor
still spends ~19.7px before the first character — a 12.7px always-present gutter, CodeMirror's 6px
`.cm-line` padding (never overridden here), and the container's 1px border
(`OrdersEditor.tsx:301`). The navigator held the mockup session this bead demanded (2026-08-15) and
chose **Variant 2b**: the dot becomes a **3px full-height bar in the theme's danger token, filling
a 3px gutter**, line padding drops to 2px, and the whole left edge before the first character is
**exactly 6px, pinned by smoke at ≤6px**. Chosen mockup: `docs/ui/orders-editor-left-edge.html`
(PR #239); the full interview is under *User-facing decisions*.

This deliberately amends the pinned smoke test "the lint gutter hugs its marker (gh-205)"
(`tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:159-176`): its intent — a shrink must never hide the indicator
— survives (the marker stays always-visible), its numbers change. That is a named change of a
pinned decision, agreed with the navigator, not a quiet edit.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

All in `@atlantis/shared`; the editor is `packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx` and the
smoke spec is `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`. `lintGutter()` stays (imported at
`OrdersEditor.tsx:4`, installed at :119) — the whole change is CSS in the existing
`EditorView.theme({...})` block at :146-182. Nothing about diagnostics computation
(`setDiagnostics`, :238) changes.

**1. The gutter block at :163-166**, today:

```ts
".cm-gutter-lint": {
  width: "1.1em",
  "& .cm-gutterElement": { padding: "0 1px" }
},
```

becomes (px, not em — the budget is a px budget and em rounding differs per engine):

```ts
".cm-gutter-lint": {
  width: "3px",
  "& .cm-gutterElement": { padding: "0" }
},
```

**2. The marker.** CodeMirror's stock CSS puts the dot on the marker element via
`content: url("data:image/svg+xml,…")` (fill `#f87`, stroke `#f43`) — a data: URI cannot see CSS
variables, which is why this is the editor chrome's last hardcoded colour. Replace the image with
a painted element, in the same theme block:

```ts
".cm-lint-marker": {
  content: "none",            // drop the stock SVG dot
  width: "3px",
  height: "100%",
  borderRadius: "1px"
},
".cm-lint-marker-error":   { backgroundColor: "var(--color-danger)" },
".cm-lint-marker-warning": { backgroundColor: "var(--color-warn)" }
```

The exact property set may need a browser check (see Known traps for the `content` pitfall); the
requirements that must hold are: full line height, 3px wide, no image, severity colour from the
tokens — matching the underline colours already at :176-181. One line with several diagnostics
keeps CodeMirror's behaviour of one marker at the worst severity; nothing to build.

**3. The line padding.** New entry in the same theme block — CodeMirror's base theme sets
`.cm-line { padding: 0 2px 0 6px }`; override only the left:

```ts
".cm-line": { paddingLeft: "2px" }
```

**4. The smoke test at :159-176.** Rewrite in place (same test, new numbers, same spirit — do not
delete it):

- keep: `WROK` typed, `.cm-lint-marker` visible (the indicator survives the shrink — the
  assertion's whole point);
- replace `expect(box!.width).toBeLessThan(14)` on `.cm-gutter-lint` with the agreed budget on the
  whole left edge: the first `.cm-line`'s `boundingBox().x` minus the `orders-input` container's
  `boundingBox().x` is **≤ 6.5px** (6px agreed + 0.5 subpixel slack), and the gutter's own width is
  `< 4`;
- add the no-error side, which the old test never pinned and the interview centred on: with valid
  orders, `.cm-lint-marker` count is 0 and the same left-edge measurement still holds — the gutter
  is reserved but 3px, so the budget is identical with and without an error.

Rename the test title to carry the new agreement, e.g.
`"the order text starts within 6px of the editor's edge, marker still showing (gh-205)"`.

## Increments

1. **Smoke pins the agreement and fails.** Rewrite the test (file 4). RED: today's edge measures
   ~19.7px against the ≤6.5 assertion; the marker-visible half still passes.
2. **CSS lands.** Files 1–3 in one pass — they are one theme block and the budget only holds with
   all three. GREEN: the rewritten smoke test.
3. **Both severities and the no-error state.** If increment 1's no-error case was not already
   written, add it now, plus a warning-severity case if the fixture can produce a warning; verify
   the bar renders in `--color-warn` for it. (If no fixture input yields a warning, say so in the
   PR and cover error only — do not invent a diagnostics change; warnings are out of scope.)
4. **Manual pass** per Validation, then PR.

## The test plan

- **Browser (Playwright):** the rewritten `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts` test — error state
  (marker visible, edge ≤6.5px, gutter <4px) and no-error state (no marker, same edge). The other
  orders-editor smoke tests (autocomplete, snippets, diagnostics strip) must stay green untouched.
- **Unit:** none — this is CSS inside `EditorView.theme`, which `theme.test.ts`'s component scan
  cannot see (its rule, tokens-not-hex, is honoured in the change itself). No new unit test file.
- Full `pnpm run ci` before the PR, smoke suites included.

## User-facing decisions

Interview held 2026-08-15; mockup `docs/ui/orders-editor-left-edge.html` (PR #239), five variants
each shown in no-error and error states. The navigator chose, in order:

1. **Route: variant 2, the slim bar** — an always-visible at-a-glance marker retained, gutter
   shrunk to hug it. Rejected: variant 1 trim-only (4px was too little); variant 3 no-gutter
   (maximum width, but an error scrolled off-screen loses its marker — the smoke test's intent
   would be reversed); variant 4 marker-on-the-right (zero net width for a rebuild of
   lintGutter's tooltip and filters).
2. **Marker shape: the bar** — 3px, full line height, "this line is wrong". Rejected: the dot
   (needs a wider gutter) and the triangle.
3. **Budget: ≤6px** for the whole left edge. Rejected: ≤10px and keeping ≤14px.
4. **2b over 2, on a direct look**: shown both the 8px version (5px gutter, bar with breathing
   room) and the 6px version (3px gutter, bar flush to the frame), the navigator confirmed
   **2b at ≤6px** ships. The 8px variant is the recorded fallback if implementation finds 6px
   unreachable — but reach for it only via the navigator, not silently.

Colours were not asked because they follow existing agreements: the bar uses `--color-danger` /
`--color-warn`, the same tokens the wavy underlines already use (:176-181), and this removes the
editor chrome's last hardcoded colour (the stock dot's `#f87`/`#f43`) as a side effect. The wavy
underline, the hover tooltip on the text, and the diagnostics strip are all unchanged.

## Out of scope

- The rest of the orders panel: status line, chrome, collapsible header, the panel split (ah-13o).
- Diagnostics themselves — what counts as an error/warning, their wording, the strip, the
  underline styling beyond the marker.
- Replacing or reimplementing `lintGutter()`; route 4's after-gutter machinery.
- Any change to the editor's right edge or `.cm-line`'s right padding.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm exec playwright test tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts
pnpm run ci
```

Manual (and Psylocke's script): in **both themes** and at a **narrow window**, view a unit with no
errors (clean 6px edge, no marker), one error (bar + underline + strip), and several errors (a bar
per broken line); **switch units to see it** — the editor is rebuilt per unit
(`OrdersEditor.tsx:98-192` effect keyed on unit), so a hot reload does not restyle the current one.

## Known traps

- **The editor is rebuilt per unit selection** — a theme change shows on the *next* unit selected,
  not on hot reload. Every manual check switches units first.
- **`content: url(data:...)` cannot use CSS variables** — that is why the stock dot is hardcoded.
  The replacement must paint the element (`content: "none"` + background), not swap in another
  data: URI. If `content: "none"` fails to suppress the stock image in the real browser (the stock
  rule may win specificity inside the gutter), fall back to `content: '""'` or a more specific
  selector — verify in the running app, not just in the suite.
- **Px, not em, everywhere in this change.** The ≤6px budget is exact; em values rendered at the
  11.5px font differ across engines (the old test's comment says as much), and WebKit is the shell
  that always disagrees.
- **The WebKit driver returns `""` for clipped text** — if the native smoke suite touches the
  orders panel, check it stays green; do not add `overflow: hidden`/clipping to the line or gutter
  to win the last pixel.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled** — run any PWA suite
  before or in a fresh build, or its timeouts will look like this change broke the worker.
- **`theme.test.ts` cannot see `EditorView.theme` styles** — a hex literal here would pass the
  suite and still be wrong. Tokens only, as the block's own comment (:142-145) demands.
- The old assertion `gutter width < 14` must not survive anywhere — a copy left behind would pass
  forever and pin nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The order editor's left margin is reduced to whatever the navigator approved in the mockup session, and an error is still obvious without it. The plan records the chosen combination of the three routes and the ones rejected, with the mockup path. Smoke coverage replaces the pinned width/visibility assertions in tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts rather than deleting them. Verified in both themes and at a narrow window, with units having no errors, one error and several.
notes: gh-205's comment thread already carries CLAIMED/MERGED markers left by the superseded ah-jb1 attempt. Ignore those when checking this issue's posted state — a fresh CREATED-style note was posted 2026-08-14 to avoid confusing the reporter, and future PLANNED/CLAIMED/MERGED/RELEASED updates for ah-gth must still be posted even though those state markers already exist in the thread from the earlier bead.

title: Drive the implementer fleet from the Emacs agent list instead of from Cerebro
description:
# Summary

Cerebro is a `claude` session on Fable that does almost nothing a script could not: it touches
`.claude/implementers/<name>.go` to put an implementer to work, removes it or writes `<name>.stop` to
take one down, sweeps worktrees with `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`, checks claims and epics, and
counts what has shipped. That is a model reasoning about `touch`, `pgrep` and a handful of `bd`
queries — and it costs a terminal, a model and the navigator's attention to drive.

Once the Emacs agent view exists (`ah-vcf`), the natural home for those actions is the list buffer
itself: put the point on an implementer and press a key to start it, stop it, or sweep after it.
**This bead explores how much of Cerebro can become elisp and shell, and what genuinely needs a
model.**

# Scope

An exploration first, then whatever it justifies building:

- **Sort Cerebro's jobs into three piles** — mechanical (a flag written, a script run, a count
  displayed), mechanical-but-needs-a-decision (which implementer to start, whether a stale claim is
  really dead), and genuinely requiring judgement (reading a log to work out why an implementer is
  stuck, cutting a release).
- **Build the first pile into the agent list** as commands on the selected agent: start, finish,
  sweep, and the counts Cerebro reports on startup.
- **Say plainly what is left**, and whether the remainder is worth a session at all or is better as
  something the navigator invokes when they want it.

The three sweeps are described in `.claude/agents/orchestrator.md` and are the concrete inventory to
work from: worktrees, claims, epics.

# Out of scope

- The agent list and detail view themselves — that is `ah-vcf`, which this is blocked on.
- Removing `.claude/agents/orchestrator.md` or the `run-orchestrator` launcher. Whether Cerebro
  retires is decided *after* this exploration reports, by the navigator, and probably in a bead of
  its own. Nothing here deletes a working role on its author's own judgement.
- Replacing Xavier, Moira or the implementers. They plan, converse and build; none of that is
  scriptable, and this bead is about the one role that mostly is not.

# Known traps

- **A safety rule that lives in a prompt does not survive being scripted.** Cerebro's sweeps are
  hedged in ways that matter: `bd reclaim` is `--id` only and never a sweep, a live claim is never
  taken without the navigator, `prune-worktrees.sh` removes a worktree only when clean, merged and
  half an hour idle. A key binding that runs the dangerous version of any of those is worse than the
  session it replaced. Each rule that survives must survive **in code**, not in a docstring.
- **Flags are read between beads, never during one.** Taking an implementer down means telling it to
  finish, so a "stop" command must write the flag and then show that the implementer is still
  working — not report success and leave the navigator thinking it has stopped.
- **Cerebro is the one who knows the roster is closed.** Anything that starts an implementer must
  pick from `IMPLEMENTER_NAMES` in `scripts/runImplementer.ts`; an off-roster name starts a real
  agent that nothing accounts for.

# Validation

- A written recommendation the navigator can act on: what became a key binding, what stayed, and why.
- ERT tests for every command that writes a flag or invokes a script, proving the guard conditions
  hold — most importantly that no path reaches a destructive `bd` or `git worktree` invocation
  without the conditions Cerebro's instructions require.
- Manually: put an implementer to work from the list, watch it take a bead, tell it to finish, and
  confirm it completes the bead it is on rather than stopping mid-flight.
design:
## Context

Cerebro the session does four kinds of work: writing stop flags, running three sweeps (worktrees,
claims, epics), reporting counts, and judgement calls (release cutting, reading a stuck log). The
Emacs fleet view (`.claude/cerebro/emacs/cerebro.el`) has since taken over starting sessions (`s`,
`cerebro-start`, cerebro.el:670), killing them (`k`, :702), and supervising implementers from their
state files (`cerebro--supervise-action`, :215, on the 5s `cerebro--tick`, :633). This bead moves
the remaining *mechanical* jobs into the fleet view and writes the recommendation the navigator
asked for on what stays with a session.

Three of the bead's own premises have expired and are corrected here rather than built:

- The `.go` flag is retired (cerebro commit `95092af`); starting from the list already shipped
  (ah-vcf.3, PR #229). Nothing here re-implements starting.
- `scripts/runImplementer.ts` and `IMPLEMENTER_NAMES` are deleted (atlantis-hud `8049f17`); the
  closed roster now lives in `.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer:36-40` (`ROSTER`, 14 names)
  and the elisp already inherits it via `run-implementer --roster` (`cerebro--roster`, :336).
- The counts panel is already built in **cerebro PR #6** (branch `bead-panel`, unmerged): a beads
  panel with Claimed / Planned / Unplanned / Merged sections, `cerebro--bd-json`,
  `cerebro--partition-beads`, `cerebro--gather-beads`, a 30s `cerebro--beads-timer`, and priority
  editing. **The navigator decided (2026-08-15) that this plan assumes #6 merges first** and builds
  on its seams; if #6 is still open when implementation starts, wait for it or ask the navigator —
  do not re-implement the panel.

The navigator's design rulings (2026-08-15): one bead, no split; **sweeps run regularly on their
own** (no keypress to detect), surface what they found, and **every destructive action asks y/n
per item** — `bd close`, `bd reclaim`, epic close; **worktree pruning stays fully automatic** as
today, since its guards only ever remove a clean, merged, half-hour-idle tree.

Related in-flight work: **ah-rnz (P0)** changes the same launchers to export `BEADS_ACTOR`, after
which claim assignees read as roster names. It will almost certainly merge first — rebase on it,
and note the claims sweep gets *simpler* then (assignee names line up with state-file names).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything except the final cleanup lives in the **cerebro submodule** (`rmstdope/cerebro`); see
Known traps for the two-repo flow. The elisp keeps the file's own law: pure decision functions
tested by ERT, impure readers/executors thin and at the bottom (cerebro/CLAUDE.md, "pure core").

**1. `emacs/cerebro.el` — the finish command.** The elisp reads `<name>.stop`
(`cerebro--stop-flag-path`, :537; `cerebro--stop-flag-p`, :541) but nothing writes it; that is
Cerebro's last routinely-needed job. Add:

```elisp
(defun cerebro--finish-action (agent flag-set)
  "Pure: what `f' should do for AGENT given FLAG-SET.
One of `write' (implementer, no flag yet), `offer-clear' (flag already
set - ask before removing it), or `not-implementer'." ...)

(defun cerebro-finish ()
  "Tell the implementer at point to finish: write its stop flag.
The session completes the bead it is on; the flag is read at `done'.
If the flag is already set, offers to clear it instead."
  (interactive) ...)
```

Bind `f` to `cerebro-finish` in `cerebro-mode-map` (keymap at :736-751; `f` is free — taken keys
are `s`, `k`, `RET`, `TAB`, `n`, `p`, plus PR #6's `0`–`4`, `+`, `-`, `u`). On `write`: create the
flag file, then `(message "told %s to finish — it completes its current bead first")`. On
`offer-clear`: `y-or-n-p` "Stop flag already set for %s — clear it?". The list entry for a working
implementer with a flag set shows ` finishing` after its state, so the navigator sees the flag took
effect while the bead is still in flight (render where `cerebro--entry` builds the line; the flag
state reaches it as plain data the same way `cerebro--stop-flag-p` feeds `cerebro--supervise`).

**2. `scripts/sweep-claims.sh` and `scripts/sweep-epics.sh` — read-only fact gatherers.** New,
alongside `prune-worktrees.sh` (reuse its superproject-root resolution, prune-worktrees.sh:62-76).
Each prints JSON to stdout and **never mutates anything** — no `bd close`, no `bd reclaim`, no
`git` writes; keeping them read-only is what makes "guards in code" checkable at a glance.

- `sweep-claims.sh --json`: for every bead from `bd list --status in_progress --json`, emit
  `{id, assignee, title, verification_failed, on_main, commit_age_min, docs_only}` where `on_main`
  uses Cerebro's own matching rules (orchestrator.md:262-331): `git log origin/main
  --grep "(<id>):" --oneline` — colon and parens required (:271) — after a `git fetch`, with
  `docs(<id>): mockup` commits discounted (:273-277), `verification_failed` from the bead's labels
  (:279), and `commit_age_min` from `git log -1 --grep ... --format='%cr'` parsed to minutes. A
  fetch failure prints `{"error": ...}` and exits non-zero rather than guessing, exactly as
  prune-worktrees.sh:105-108 does.
- `sweep-epics.sh --json`: from `bd epic status --eligible-only --json`, emit
  `{id, title, minutes_since_last_child_closed}` (via `bd children`), per orchestrator.md:364-411.

**3. `emacs/cerebro.el` — sweep detection, display, and confirmed execution.**

- A slow timer alongside PR #6's fast one: `(defvar cerebro-sweep-refresh-seconds 600 ...)` — ten
  minutes, Cerebro's own cadence — driving `cerebro--gather-sweeps`, an impure reader that runs the
  two scripts and parses their JSON (reuse the subprocess/JSON plumbing `cerebro--bd-json` from
  PR #6 establishes).
- Pure decisions, one per sweep, mirroring orchestrator.md's guard tables:

```elisp
(defun cerebro--claim-finding (candidate live-names now)
  "Pure. CANDIDATE is the parsed sweep-claims JSON for one bead.
Returns nil (leave it alone), or (close ID REASON) when on_main,
commit_age_min > 10, assignee not in LIVE-NAMES, and not
verification_failed - or (reclaim ID) when not on_main and the
assignee's session is dead." ...)

(defun cerebro--epic-finding (candidate)
  "Pure. nil, or (epic-close ID) when eligible and
minutes_since_last_child_closed > 10." ...)

(defun cerebro--finding-command (finding repo-root)
  "Pure. The exact argv for FINDING:
(close ID R)   -> (\"bd\" \"close\" ID \"--reason\" R)
(reclaim ID)   -> (\"bd\" \"reclaim\" \"--id\" ID \"--older-than\" \"10m\")
(epic-close I) -> (\"bd\" \"close\" I)
nil            -> nil. Never anything else: this function is the
complete list of destructive commands the fleet view can run." ...)
```

  `live-names` comes from the state files the view already gathers (`cerebro--gather-states`,
  :360) — the fact Cerebro had to approximate with `pgrep`, the view has natively.
- Display: a **Sweeps** section appended to the beads panel via PR #6's `cerebro--bead-section`,
  one finding per line ("close ah-xyz — delivered by Cyclops, on main 25m"), empty section hidden.
- Execution: `cerebro-sweep-act`, bound to `x` in the beads-panel buffer's mode map (PR #6's
  `cerebro-bead-mode-map` area), acting on the finding at point. It builds the command with
  `cerebro--finding-command`, shows it verbatim in a `y-or-n-p` prompt ("run: bd close ah-xyz
  --reason …? "), runs it only on yes, then `bd dolt push` (also behind the same yes), and
  refreshes. **`y-or-n-p` sits in `cerebro-sweep-act` itself and nowhere else; no timer path may
  reach `cerebro--finding-command`'s output.** `bd reclaim` findings additionally follow the
  crashed-implementer rule: the prompt names the worktree that may need cleaning, per
  beads-workflow.
- Reclaim never sweeps: one finding, one id, `--id` always — the pure function makes any other
  shape unrepresentable.

**4. `emacs/cerebro.el` — the prune watcher.** Cerebro starts `prune-worktrees.sh --watch` on its
startup (orchestrator.md:224-247); move that to the view: on `M-x cerebro`, if no live process
named `cerebro-prune` exists, `make-process` running `prune-worktrees.sh --watch` with output to a
buffer `" *cerebro-prune*"`, killed when the cerebro buffer is killed. Pure decision
`cerebro--prune-action (process-live)` → `start`/`already-running`. The script's own guards are the
safety story (prune-worktrees.sh:100-166); the view adds nothing and must not add `--force`.

**5. `docs/cerebro-jobs.md`** (cerebro repo) — **the written recommendation**, the bead's primary
acceptance artifact. Three piles, each job placed with a sentence of why, written for the navigator:

- *Now in the fleet view*: start (`s`, shipped ah-vcf.3), finish (`f`, this bead), counts (PR #6),
  worktree pruning (watcher, this bead), claims and epics sweep detection with confirmed execution
  (`x`, this bead).
- *Stays with a session, started when wanted*: release cutting (orchestrator.md:542-635 — judgement
  plus a long `gh run watch`), diagnosing a stuck implementer (reading a transcript is a model's
  job), and anything `bd update --force`-shaped.
- *Retired with the sessionless design*: the keepalive loop (orchestrator.md:413-459) — a timer in
  Emacs needs no subagent holding a `sleep`.

End with the open question the navigator owns and this bead must not answer: whether Cerebro the
session is still started by default, or only on demand. Recommend on-demand; decide nothing.

**6. `agents/orchestrator.md`** — align prose with what moved: the stale
`pgrep -fl "runImplementer.ts"` at :437 and :467 (that file no longer exists — point at the state
files and `claude agents --json` instead), and a paragraph at the top of each sweep section saying
the fleet view now detects candidates and the session's role is the judgement cases. Do not delete
the sweep instructions — they are the specification the elisp guards were written from, and
Cerebro-on-demand still uses them.

**7. Consumer cleanup (atlantis-hud, in the submodule-bump PR):** delete the dead pre-move copy
`tools/emacs/atlantis-fleet.el`, `tools/emacs/atlantis-fleet-test.el`, `tools/emacs/README.md`, and
remove `package.json`'s `"test:fleet"` script (line 18) which runs that dead copy. No CI references
either (verified: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has no fleet/emacs mention).

## Increments

ERT harness: `emacs/cerebro-test.el`, run as
`emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` (cerebro CLAUDE.md). All
new logic goes in pure functions so the tests pass plain data; follow the existing
`cerebro-test/…` naming.

1. **Finish.** RED: `cerebro-test/finish-action-writes-for-unflagged-implementer`,
   `…/finish-action-offers-clear-when-flagged`, `…/finish-action-refuses-interactive-roles`, and a
   rendering case `…/entry-shows-finishing-when-flag-set`. GREEN: `cerebro--finish-action`,
   `cerebro-finish`, the ` finishing` marker, the `f` binding.
2. **Fact gatherers.** `sweep-claims.sh` and `sweep-epics.sh`. Their correctness rides on bd and
   git, so the automated pinning is at the elisp layer (they feed pure functions); validate the
   scripts by running each against the live consumer repo and eyeballing the JSON (they are
   read-only, so this is safe). Assert in `tests/launchers.sh`-style only that `--json` produces
   parseable JSON and a bad flag exits 2, if ah-rnz's `tests/launchers.sh` exists by then.
3. **Sweep decisions.** RED: ERT cases per guard, each one a candidate that fails exactly one
   guard — `…/claim-finding-leaves-verification-failed`, `…/claim-finding-leaves-live-implementer`,
   `…/claim-finding-leaves-fresh-commit`, `…/claim-finding-closes-delivered-dead-and-old`,
   `…/claim-finding-reclaims-dead-not-on-main`, `…/epic-finding-waits-ten-minutes`, and the
   command mapping `…/finding-command-covers-only-the-three-shapes` (asserts nil → nil and that an
   unknown shape errors rather than producing argv). GREEN: the three pure functions.
4. **Display + confirmed execution.** RED: `…/sweep-section-renders-findings`,
   `…/sweep-section-hidden-when-empty` (reuse PR #6's `cerebro-test--with-panel` macro), and
   `…/sweep-act-runs-nothing-without-confirmation` — bind `y-or-n-p` to a recording stub returning
   nil and assert the process-runner stub was never called. GREEN: the section, the timer,
   `cerebro-sweep-act`, the `x` binding.
5. **Prune watcher.** RED: `…/prune-action-starts-when-absent`,
   `…/prune-action-leaves-running-process`. GREEN: `cerebro--prune-action` and the `make-process`
   wiring.
6. **Prose.** `docs/cerebro-jobs.md` and the `orchestrator.md` edits. No tests; the check is the
   acceptance criterion — a recommendation the navigator can act on.
7. **PRs.** Cerebro PR (say in the body: ERT suite output, both sweeps' JSON verified against the
   live consumer). After merge: atlantis-hud bump PR carrying the submodule pointer plus item 7's
   deletions, through normal CI and review.

## The test plan

- ERT (`emacs/cerebro-test.el`): the ~14 new cases named above; the existing 63+ must stay green.
  This is where the bead's acceptance line "no path reaches a destructive bd or git worktree call
  without the guards" is proven: `cerebro--finding-command` is the only argv source, its tests
  enumerate its total output range, and `…/sweep-act-runs-nothing-without-confirmation` pins the
  confirmation gate.
- Shell: run both sweep scripts read-only against the live repo; JSON parses, facts spot-checked
  against `bd list --status in_progress` and `bd epic status`.
- Manual (also the bead's own validation): from the list, `s` an implementer, watch it claim; `f`
  it, confirm the list shows ` finishing` and the session completes its bead before ending; force a
  sweep refresh and confirm a finding line appears and `x` prompts with the exact command.

## User-facing decisions

The player sees none of this; the *navigator* is the user here, and their rulings (2026-08-15):

1. **Scope**: one bead — sweeps + counts + recommendation; no split. (Rejected: recommendation
   first with child beads; splitting now.)
2. **PR #6**: assumed merged first; build on the bead panel, never duplicate it. (Rejected:
   planning the counts independently.)
3. **Sweep model**, in the navigator's words: "Sweeps should be done regularly, but confirmation is
   needed before any destructive-ish action" — confirmed reading: detection on a timer with no
   keypress; y/n per item before `bd close` / `bd reclaim` / epic close; worktree pruning stays
   automatic because its guards only remove a clean, merged, half-hour-idle tree. (Rejected:
   keypress-triggered detection; fully automatic execution; confirming worktree prunes too.)
4. **Keybindings** were left to the planner within that policy: `f` finish, `x` execute the
   sweep finding at point. If either reads wrongly at the keyboard, renaming a binding is a
   one-line change and needs no plan revision.

## Out of scope

- Retiring Cerebro, or changing when it is started — the recommendation informs that decision; the
  navigator takes it, later, probably in a bead of its own.
- Xavier, Moira, Psylocke, the implementers, and everything in their prompts and skills.
- Release cutting from Emacs.
- Re-implementing anything PR #6 contains, or reworking its layout/priority-editing behaviour.
- bd changes; ah-rnz owns actor identity.
- CI for the cerebro repo.

## Validation

```bash
# cerebro clone
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
scripts/sweep-claims.sh --json | jq .    # from the consumer root, read-only
scripts/sweep-epics.sh --json | jq .
```

plus the manual walk under *The test plan*, and atlantis-hud's normal gates on the bump PR. Human
check: the navigator drives one full `f` cycle and one confirmed `x` on a real finding.

## Known traps

- **Submodule bead: never branch in `.claude/cerebro`** — it is shared by every session like the
  main checkout. Clone `rmstdope/cerebro` to a scratch path outside `.claude/worktrees/` (the prune
  sweep walks that directory), branch there, PR there; bump the pointer in atlantis-hud afterwards
  from a normal worktree. Same flow ah-rnz's plan spells out — and **rebase on ah-rnz's merged
  launchers before starting**, since both beads touch the same repo.
- **PR #6 is the floor.** If it is unmerged when work starts, stop and ask the navigator rather
  than building the panel twice. Its test macros (`cerebro-test--with-panel`,
  `cerebro-test--with-bd`) are the harness increments 3–4 reuse — they exist only after it merges.
- **A safety rule that lives in a prompt does not survive being scripted** (the bead's own words).
  The concrete keeps: reclaim is `--id` only, ever; close needs on-main AND >10min AND no live
  session AND not `verification:failed`; epic close is one at a time and never
  `bd epic close-eligible`; prune never gets `--force`. Each lives in a pure function or the
  script, and each has the ERT case that fails if it is loosened.
- **`cerebro--derive-implementer` maps unknown states to `idle`** (cerebro.el:103-113) — reading as
  "fine" rather than as an error. Do not invent new state-file vocabulary for ` finishing`; the
  flag is a separate fact the view already reads, not a new state.
- **The 5s tick and the new timers are separate.** Sweep detection on the 5s `cerebro--tick` would
  hammer bd and git; keep it on its own 600s timer, and kill all timers with the buffer as PR #6
  does with `cerebro--beads-timer`.
- **Flags are read between beads, never during one.** The `f` command's message and the
  ` finishing` marker exist so the navigator is never told a stop "succeeded" while the implementer
  is still mid-bead.
- **Emacs backup files (`*.el~`) are committed in the cerebro repo** — ignore them, never edit or
  delete them in these PRs.
acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation naming which of Cerebro's jobs became commands in the Emacs agent list, which stayed with a session, and why. The mechanical ones are implemented as commands on the selected agent — putting an implementer to work, telling it to finish, running the sweeps, showing the counts — each with ERT coverage proving no path reaches a destructive bd or git worktree call without the guards Cerebro's instructions require.

title: Reduce left margin in the order editor
description:
The order editor currently reserves more left-margin space than it needs for the error indicator, leaving less room for order text than necessary.

Reported by rmstdope (Henrik Kurelid) in GitHub issue #205, with a screenshot attached to the issue showing the current spacing.
design:
## Context

Navigator-filed (gh-205, screenshot attached there), ranked P2. The order editor
(`packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx`) is CodeMirror with `lintGutter()` (:119); the
left margin the issue shows is the lint gutter at CodeMirror's default width plus padding — wider
than the error/warning marker it exists to hold, so order text loses room in an already narrow
panel. The fix is a theme rule: the editor already carries an `EditorView.theme({...})` block
(:146-176) styling `.cm-gutters`; the gutter width belongs beside it.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx` — extend the existing theme block: size
  `.cm-gutter-lint` to hug the marker (width in the marker's own `em` terms plus minimal padding,
  e.g. width ~`1em` with `2px` horizontal padding — tune against the running editor, not on paper)
  and keep the marker itself untouched so error/warning glyphs render as today. Nothing else — no
  new extension, no gutter removal (`lintGutter()` stays; the indicator is the feature, the excess
  is the defect).
- Reuse: the theme block's own conventions — tokens not literals, comments saying why (the block's
  header comment explains the rule).

## Increments

1. **Pin the width.** Opening failing test: smoke, in the suite that already exercises the orders
   editor — "the lint gutter hugs its marker": select a unit, locate `.cm-gutter-lint` in the
   editor, assert its bounding-box width is below a threshold that fails today and passes with the
   fix (measure the current width first, then set the threshold between current and target; keep
   the assertion loose enough to survive font rendering differences — a ceiling, not an exact px).
   GREEN: the theme rule.
2. **Nothing else moved.** The existing editor smoke tests (typing, diagnostics underlines, the
   gutter marker appearing on a broken line) all stay green — the marker must still show at the
   reduced width; if no existing test pins "a broken order shows a gutter marker", add that
   assertion to increment 1's test so the shrink cannot quietly hide the indicator.

## The test plan

Smoke (Playwright, both projects): the width ceiling + marker-still-visible test above; every
existing orders-editor test stays green.
Unit: none new — SSR string tests cannot see injected CodeMirror layout, and pinning the CSS text
itself would test the spelling, not the outcome.
Suites: `pnpm run test` (unchanged, green), `pnpm run test:smoke`; `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None to ask: the goal — reduce the reserved space to what the indicator needs — is the navigator's
own issue, screenshot included. The exact value is tuning toward that stated goal; the human check
below is where the navigator confirms it reads right.

## Out of scope

- Removing or redesigning the lint gutter or its markers.
- Line numbers, folding, or any other gutter.
- The editor panel's own width or the dock layout.
- Any other editor styling.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check
```

Human check (navigator, post-merge is fine): open the order editor beside gh-205's screenshot — the
text starts close to the left edge, and a broken order line still shows its marker clearly.

## Known traps

- **Do not hide the marker to win the width.** The gutter exists for the error indicator; the smoke
  assertion that a broken line still shows its marker is the guard.
- **CodeMirror class names are the API here** (`.cm-gutter-lint`, `.cm-gutters`) — they are stable
  across the pinned CodeMirror version but check the rendered DOM rather than guessing; the theme
  block's existing selectors show the working spelling.
- **Smoke measures rendered pixels** — assert a ceiling, not equality; WebKit/Chromium font metrics
  differ and the suite runs Chromium only, but the desktop shell project shares the assertion.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — branch from `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria:
- The order editor's left margin is reduced, giving more horizontal room to the order text.
- Space for the per-line error indicator is preserved so errors are still clearly shown.
- Verified visually against the screenshot attached to GitHub issue #205.

title: The diff view: read what changed between two turns
description:
## Summary

The surface of ah-jg6. Given a chosen pair of turns and the computed differences, show the player what changed: units added, removed and changed; region changes; and how the orders drafts differ.

## Scope

- The view itself, wherever the navigator puts it, showing all three kinds of change.
- Say plainly when nothing changed in a category, rather than showing an empty list.
- A change must be traceable back to the thing that changed — a unit named in the diff is a way back to that unit.

## Why this is its own bead

Its shape is a navigator decision and needs mockups, and it is the only piece of ah-jg6 that cannot start until the other three have landed.

## Out of scope

- Computing the differences (ah-jg6.2) and holding the pair (ah-jg6.3).
- Editing anything from the diff view. Reading only.
- Diffing more than two turns, or across games.
design:
## Context

The surface of the diff epic, and the only bead of `ah-jg6` that stands on all three others. At
planning time **none of its blockers had merged** — ah-jg6.1 was in progress, ah-jg6.2 and ah-jg6.3
freshly planned — so every reference below to their surfaces is to what their plans commit to, and
the first act of implementation is to read the landed code and prefer it over this sketch:

- From **ah-jg6.3**: `comparison: { key: { factionId, turnNumber }, parsed: ParsedReport } | null`
  held in `AppShell` beside `parsed`, signalled in the Turn chip as `71 ⇄ 70`.
- From **ah-jg6.2**: `diffTurns(older, newer): TurnDiff` (`units.added/removed/changed` with
  preformatted `ValueChange`s and `movedFrom/movedTo`; `regions.changed/onlyInNewer/onlyInOlder`)
  and `diffOrders(olderText, newerText): OrdersDiff` — all in `packages/shared/src/turnDiff.ts`.

The navigator chose the shape (mockup: `docs/ui/turn-diff-view.html`, PR #199): a **centred dialog**
in the battles-view frame, its categories behind **Units / Regions / Orders tabs** with counts in
the tab labels — tabs chosen explicitly over stacked sections — opened from a **Changes chip** that
appears in the header only while a comparison is on, and **clicking a unit or region named in the
diff selects it on the map and closes the dialog**. An empty category states "nothing changed"
plainly inside its tab.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/changesView.ts`** (new) — the pure view-model, so the dialog
  stays declarative:
  - `changesTabs(diff: TurnDiff, orders: OrdersDiff | null)` → the three tab descriptors
    `{ key: "units" | "regions" | "orders", label: string /* "Units · 5" */, count: number }`.
  - Row builders that flatten the diff into renderable rows (glyph `+`/`−`/`±`/`→`, the clickable
    target's `unitId`/`regionId`, the preformatted change text) — using `hexLabelOf` from
    `hexMapModel.ts` for region names; never hand-format coordinates.
  - The empty-state line per category ("No unit changed between these turns." etc.) — exact wording
    is in the mockup's idiom; keep it one sentence.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/ChangesDialog.tsx`** (new) — copied structurally from
  `BattlesDialog.tsx`: the `fixed inset-0 z-30 ... bg-black/50` backdrop (`:49`) dismissing on a
  backdrop press, `role="dialog"`, `useEscapeToDismiss(onDismiss)` from `./dismissLayer` (`:3,:37`
  — use the shared layer, not a hand-rolled `keydown`), a pinned header row with the pair label
  ("turn 70 → 71") and a close button. Tabs follow the `GamePicker` tab pattern
  (`game-picker-tab-*`). Testids: `changes-backdrop`, `changes-dialog`, `changes-close`,
  `changes-tab-units|regions|orders`, rows `changes-unit-<unitId>`, `changes-region-<regionId>`,
  `changes-order-<unitId>`. Props: the two diffs, the pair label, `onSelectUnit(unitId, regionId)`,
  `onSelectRegion(regionId)`, `onDismiss` — the dialog computes nothing.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx`** — a `Changes` chip beside the Turn chip,
  rendered only when comparing, exactly the conditional pattern of `problems-chip` (rendered only
  when `problemCount > 0`). Testid `changes-chip`; like `battles-chip` it needs **no `relative`
  wrapper** — its surface is a centred dialog, not an anchored popover (the prop doc around the
  battles chip says why). New props: `onChangesOpen` and whatever ah-jg6.3 landed for "a comparison
  is on" (reuse its prop rather than adding a parallel one).
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** — the wiring:
  - `const [changesOpen, setChangesOpen] = useState(false)` — transient, like `battlesOpen`;
    cleared wherever ah-jg6.3 clears the comparison (game switch, new working turn, comparison
    dismissed — an open dialog over a vanished comparison must close).
  - `const turnDiff = useMemo(...)` over `[parsed, comparison]`: orient **by turn number** — the
    lower-numbered turn is `older` whichever side is the working one, and the pair label reads
    "turn <lower> → <higher>".
  - Orders texts: the working side is the **live `ordersDocument` text** (what the player sees is
    the truth, not the stored copy); the compared side is
    `client.loadOrderDraft(databasePath, gameId, factionId, turnNumber)` — already on `CoreClient`
    (`core-client/src/index.ts:1101`) — falling back to the compared parse's `ordersTemplate.text`,
    and to `null` if neither exists (the Orders tab then shows its empty line "No orders known for
    turn 70."). Loaded when the dialog opens, not eagerly.
  - Traceability: `onSelectRegion` → the shell's existing `selectRegion(regionId)`;
    `onSelectUnit` → `selectRegion` + `selectUnit` (both exist — the restore effect at
    `AppShell.tsx:1284` uses them); then `setChangesOpen(false)`. `BattlesDialog`'s
    `battles-show-on-map` (`:206`) is the wired precedent to read.
- **Reuse**: `BattlesDialog.tsx` as the frame; `changesView` consumes ah-jg6.2's preformatted
  strings — no item/skill arithmetic in the view; `hexLabelOf` for region display names.

## Increments

1. **The view-model.** Opening failing test: `changesView.test.ts` › "tabs carry their counts and an
   empty category says so" — a diff with five unit changes, no region changes and a null orders diff
   yields `Units · 5`, `Regions · 0` with the empty line, `Orders · 0` with "no orders known".
   GREEN: `changesView.ts`.
2. **The dialog renders.** Opening failing test: `ChangesDialog.test.tsx` › "the units tab lists
   rows with glyphs and the region tab is reachable" — SSR string assertions on `changes-tab-units`,
   a `changes-unit-<id>` row containing the preformatted change text, and the pair label. Plus
   "an empty regions tab states nothing changed". GREEN: the component.
3. **The chip appears only while comparing.** Opening failing test: `AppHeader.test.tsx` › "the
   changes chip appears with a comparison and not without" — `draw()` with and without the
   comparison prop. The `draw()` helper hand-builds the full prop object; extend it once. GREEN:
   the AppHeader change.
4. **The shell wires it.** Opening failing test: smoke, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` › "the
   changes dialog reads a real pair" — import `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t70.rep` then `-t71.rep`
   (both already imported by the suite), start the comparison via ah-jg6.3's picker, click
   `changes-chip`, assert the dialog opens with the pair label "turn 70 → 71" and that the Units
   tab label carries a non-zero count (the two fixtures genuinely differ). GREEN: the AppShell
   wiring.
5. **A change leads back to its thing.** Opening failing test: smoke › "clicking a changed unit
   selects it and closes the dialog" — click a `changes-unit-*` row, assert the dialog is gone and
   the unit's region/unit panels show the target. Escape and backdrop dismissal asserted in the
   same test, following the battles dialog's smoke shape.

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, SSR string assertions, `packages/shared`):
- `changesView.test.ts` — counts, empty lines, row flattening (a moved unit renders `→` with both
  region labels; an added unit names its region).
- `ChangesDialog.test.tsx` — tabs, rows, pair label, empty states.
- `AppHeader.test.tsx` — the conditional chip; existing tests stay green.

Smoke (Playwright, both projects): increments 4 and 5; the battles-dialog and comparison-picker
smoke tests must stay green.

Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`; full `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator, 2026-08-14; mockup at `docs/ui/turn-diff-view.html` (PR #199):
- Container: **dialog** in the battles-view frame. Rejected: a dock panel.
- Layout: **tabs** — Units / Regions / Orders with counts in the labels. The navigator chose tabs
  over the recommended stacked sections; do not "simplify" back to sections.
- Opening: a **Changes chip** in the header, present only while a comparison is on. Rejected:
  overloading the ⇄ half of the Turn chip; auto-opening on pick.
- Traceability: **select and close** — clicking a named unit or region selects it on the map and
  dismisses the dialog.

Taken here as architecture: the diff is oriented lower turn → higher turn regardless of which side
is the working turn; the orders comparison uses the live document on the working side and stored
draft (falling back to template text) on the compared side.

## Out of scope

- Computing differences (ah-jg6.2) and holding/picking the pair (ah-jg6.3).
- Editing anything from the view — no order edits, no writes of any kind.
- Filtering, searching or sorting inside the tabs; per-battle-style expanders. First version reads
  top to bottom.
- Diffing battles, events or turn messages.
- More than two turns, or cross-game pairs.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check   # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, post-merge is fine): with turns 70 and 71 imported, compare, open Changes;
the counts ring true against the two reports, an empty category says so in words, and clicking a
changed unit lands you on it with the dialog gone.

## Known traps

- **This plan is written against three unlanded beads.** Before writing any code, read what
  ah-jg6.1/2/3 actually merged — prop names, the comparison state's shape, `TurnDiff`'s exact
  fields — and follow the landed code where it differs from the sketches here. If any of the three
  has *not* landed when this bead is picked up, it is blocked in fact: hand it back rather than
  building a blocker's feature inside it.
- **The compared side's orders may not exist.** `loadOrderDraft` returns `null` for a turn never
  drafted, and a fixture imported fresh has no stored draft — the Orders tab must render its empty
  line, not crash and not show the template as if the player wrote it (label the fallback "orders
  template" if shown).
- **Close the dialog when the comparison dies.** Game switch, a new working turn, or the ✕ in the
  Turn chip all clear the comparison; an open dialog reading freed state is a blank or a crash.
  One effect keyed on the comparison handles it.
- **Use `useEscapeToDismiss`/the dismiss stack**, as `BattlesDialog` does — a hand-rolled `keydown`
  fights the layered popovers (the picker may be open under the dialog's chip).
- **`AppHeader.test.tsx`'s `draw()` breaks on any new prop** — extend it once, in increment 3.
- **The dialog must not become a drop target** — the header is; the battles dialog's backdrop
  already stops what needs stopping. Copy, don't reinvent.
- **Both sides must be parsed the same way** (ah-jg6.2's rule): the comparison's `parsed` and the
  working `parsed` both come through the shell's normal parse path, so this holds by construction —
  do not re-parse one side differently inside this bead.
- **`z-30` backdrop vs `z-20` popovers**: the dialog sits above the header popovers by design;
  keep the battles dialog's z values rather than inventing new ones.

title: Hold a second turn alongside the working one, and pick the pair
description:
## Summary

The app holds exactly one parsed report in memory (`parsed` in `AppShell`). To compare two turns it has to hold two, and the player has to be able to say which two.

## Scope

- Load a second, chosen turn alongside the current one without disturbing the working turn — selection, orders drafts and the map must all still refer to the turn being played.
- A way to pick the pair from the turns ah-jg6.1 enumerates.
- Make clear at all times which turn is the working one and which is being compared against, so the second turn can never be mistaken for the current one.

## Why this is its own bead

The picker is a surface the player sees and the navigator decides, and holding a second report touches the shell's central state. Doing that in the same bead as the diff rendering would put two risky changes in one PR.

## Out of scope

- The diff computation (ah-jg6.2) and the diff view (ah-jg6.4).
- Editing orders in the compared turn. It is read-only.
- Holding more than two turns.
design:
## Context

Middle bead of the diff epic `ah-jg6`. The shell holds exactly one parsed turn (`parsed`,
`AppShell.tsx:259`); this bead lets it hold one chosen second turn, read-only, so the diff view
(ah-jg6.4) has something to diff. It stands on **ah-jg6.1** (`listImportedTurns`), which is planned
but **not yet built** — at planning time its implementer's lease had expired with no commits, so
treat every `listImportedTurns` reference below as the seam its plan commits to, not as code to read:
`listImportedTurns(databasePath, gameId)` on `CoreClient` returning summaries
`{ key: { factionId, turnNumber }, season: string | null, importedAt, updatedAt }`, ordered by turn
number ascending, **all factions' turns included** — the caller filters. If ah-jg6.1 has landed by
implementation time, read its actual signatures first and prefer them over this sketch.

The navigator chose the interaction (mockup: `docs/ui/turn-compare-picker.html`, PR #197): the Turn
chip — today the only non-interactive chip in the header — opens a popover listing the stored turns;
the working turn is always one side of the pair and **clicking another turn compares against it**,
one click on, one click off; the chip itself carries the state as `71 ⇄ 70` (compared half in brass)
with an inline ✕ to stop. No banner, no second surface.

When this lands: a comparison turn is held in shell state beside `parsed`, visibly and dismissably,
and ah-jg6.4 can consume it.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/turnCompare.ts`** (new) — the pure logic, so the shell stays thin:
  - `type ComparisonTurn = { key: { factionId: string; turnNumber: number }, parsed: ParsedReport }`.
  - `toggleComparison(current: number | null, clicked: number, working: number): number | null` —
    clicking the working turn → `null` (no-op close), clicking the current comparison → `null`
    (off), anything else → `clicked`.
  - `comparisonChipLabel(workingTurn: number, comparedTurn: number | null)` — the `71 ⇄ 70` text
    split into parts the header can style.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/TurnPicker.tsx`** (new) — the popover, copied structurally from
  `GamePicker.tsx` (its dismissal effect at :46-71 — Escape `keydown` plus `pointerdown` tested
  against `panelRef.current.parentElement`, *not* the panel alone; its root pattern at :94-105 —
  `role="dialog"`, `onDragOver={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` because the header is the report drop
  target, and the popover class string `absolute left-0 top-full z-20 mt-1 ... whitespace-normal
  shadow-lg`). Use `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H` from `primitives.tsx` for the scroll body — ah-cp8 (merged)
  established it. Testids: `turn-picker`, rows `turn-row-<turnNumber>`; rows show turn number and
  season (from the summary; season may be null — show the number alone), the working turn marked `●`
  and labelled `playing`, the compared turn marked `⇄` and labelled `compare`, plus the hint line
  from the mockup.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx`** — the Turn chip (lines ~238-242) becomes a
  button in **its own `relative` wrapper** (the comment at :254-259 explains why sharing one breaks
  dismissal), `data-testid="turn-chip"`, `aria-expanded`, hosting a `turnPicker?: ReactNode` prop —
  the "header owns the button, shell owns the panel" split every sibling chip uses. When a
  comparison is on, the chip renders working number, `⇄ <compared>` in brass
  (`text-brass-bright`), and an inline ✕ (`aria-label="stop comparing"`) wired to a new
  `onStopComparing` prop. New props: `onTurnToggle`, `turnPickerOpen`, `comparedTurnLabel`,
  `onStopComparing`, `turnPicker` — keep them nullable so `GameGate`'s header is untouched.
- **`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`** — the state and the load:
  - `const [comparison, setComparison] = useState<ComparisonTurn | null>(null)` and
    `const [turnsOpen, setTurnsOpen] = useState(false)` — plain `useState`, per the shell's own
    comment at :332-333 ("a panel that is open for a moment, not a preference"); nothing persisted.
  - Turn summaries fetched when the picker opens (not eagerly), via `client.listImportedTurns`,
    filtered to the working faction (`parsed.header.factionId`) — a merged game legitimately holds
    other factions' turns and comparing across factions is not this feature.
  - Selecting a turn: `client.loadImportedTurn(game.databasePath, gameId, factionId, turnNumber)`
    (which has **no production caller today** — `restoreLatestTurn` in `gameMemory.ts:283` uses only
    the latest-turn path; follow its shape: re-parse `stored.rawReport` with the same injected parse
    the restore effect builds), then `setComparison({ key, parsed })`.
  - Clear `comparison` and `turnsOpen` in `enterGame` (:1389, beside the other resets) **and** in
    `applyReport` (:744) — a new working turn redefines the pair, and a stale comparison against a
    replaced turn is exactly the confusion this bead exists to prevent.
- **Reuse**: `GamePicker` as the popover template; `factionLabelOf`/`turnLabel` derivation at
  :1998-2002 for labels; the merged-reports pattern (`mergedReports` beside `parsed`) as the
  precedent for a second dataset held alongside the working turn.

## Increments

1. **The pure toggle.** Opening failing test: `turnCompare.test.ts` › "clicking the compared turn
   again turns the comparison off" (plus siblings: clicking the working turn is null, clicking a
   third turn switches). GREEN: `turnCompare.ts`.
2. **The picker renders.** Opening failing test: `TurnPicker.test.tsx` › "lists the turns in turn
   order and marks the playing and compared turns" — SSR string assertions on `turn-row-71` with
   `●`/`playing`, `turn-row-70` with `⇄`/`compare`, and a null-season row showing the bare number.
   GREEN: the component.
3. **The chip carries the state.** Opening failing test: `AppHeader.test.tsx` › "the turn chip shows
   the comparison and offers the way out" — with `comparedTurnLabel`, markup contains `⇄`, the
   compared number, and a control labelled `stop comparing`; without it, the plain label and `▾`.
   GREEN: the AppHeader changes. The `draw()` helper hand-builds the full prop object, so this
   increment updates it once with the new props.
4. **The shell holds the pair.** Opening failing test: smoke,
   `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` › "a second turn can be compared and dismissed" — import
   `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t70.rep` then `-t71.rep` (the suite already imports both — see
   `OWN_OLDER_REPORT` at :42 and the older-turn tests at :343-394), open `turn-chip`, click
   `turn-row-70`, assert the chip shows `⇄ 70`, then click the ✕ and assert it reverts — and
   throughout, assert the header still shows turn 71 as working and (the invariant) the orders and
   selection surfaces are undisturbed. GREEN: the AppShell wiring.
5. **The working draft is untouchable.** Opening failing test: smoke › "comparing does not disturb
   the working turn's orders" — type an order line for a unit of turn 71, start a comparison, clear
   it, reload the page, assert the typed order survived (the existing persistence patterns in
   `persistence.spec.ts` show the reload shape). This pins the draft-key invariant below.

## The test plan

Unit (vitest, SSR string assertions in `packages/shared`):
- `turnCompare.test.ts` — the toggle truth table and the chip-label split.
- `TurnPicker.test.tsx` — ordering, marks, null season, empty list (a game with one turn renders
  only the playing row and the hint).
- `AppHeader.test.tsx` — chip states; existing tests stay green.

Smoke (Playwright, both `web` and `desktop-shell` projects):
- The two new tests from increments 4 and 5.
- Existing older-turn import tests (:343-394) must stay green — this bead sits right beside them.

Suites: `pnpm run test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`; full `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator, 2026-08-14; mockup at `docs/ui/turn-compare-picker.html`
(PR #197):
- Picker: **A** — the Turn chip opens the turn list; a click compares that turn **against the
  working turn**; click again (or the working row) to stop. Rejected: free pick of any two turns.
- Signal: **A** — the chip itself becomes `71 ⇄ 70`, compared half in brass, inline ✕ to stop.
  Rejected: a banner row under the header.

Taken here as architecture (not player-visible surface, recorded so it is not re-opened): the
comparison is transient (never persisted), is cleared by a game switch or a new working turn, and
the picker lists only the working faction's turns.

## Out of scope

- The diff computation (ah-jg6.2) and the diff view (ah-jg6.4) — nothing here renders the compared
  turn's content beyond the chip.
- Editing orders in, or exporting from, the compared turn. It is read-only by construction: no
  surface of it is wired to any writer.
- Comparing turns of different factions, or across games.
- Holding more than two turns.
- Persisting the comparison across reloads.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check        # the full gate, before the PR
```
