title: Commit a second turn so multi-step routes can be proved on real data
description:
## Summary

Commit a second real turn for one faction, so that routes longer than one step can be proved against
real data rather than only against synthetic corridors.

## Problem

Issue #8 built a map that accumulates across turns, and it works: the core merges remembered regions
with the current report, the current turn wins where they disagree, and both platforms store and
read back region sightings. All of that is unit-tested.

None of it can be demonstrated end to end, because the repository holds exactly one report per
faction: neworigins-3.0.0-f73-t2.rep for faction 73 and neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep for faction 95.

A single report cannot support a route longer than one step. It describes the hexes the faction
stood in and names their neighbours, but a named hex describes no exits of its own, so the graph
stops at the fringe. With the committed fixtures, every route the planner produces is one step.

Multi-step, multi-month, road and flight behaviour is therefore covered only against small synthetic
reports built in the tests. Those are honest tests, but they are our own fixtures rather than the
game's output, and they cannot catch a disagreement between what we think a report says and what one
actually says.

Fabricating a second turn was deliberately avoided during #8: inventing game data and committing it
as a fixture would make every test built on it worthless as evidence.

## Scope

- Commit a genuine second turn for faction 95, ideally adjacent in time to turn 71
- Add an acceptance test that imports both turns and plans a route crossing ground the later report
  does not describe
- Extend the smoke suite so the multi-step case is exercised in a browser, not only in the core

## Acceptance criteria

- Two turns of one faction are committed under tests/fixtures/reports
- A test plans a route of more than one step over the accumulated map, with a cost read from the
  reports by hand
- The stale map state is exercised, since it becomes reachable only once a hex is remembered from an
  earlier turn than the current one

## Validation

    cargo test --workspace
    pnpm run check

## Dependencies / Links

- Main issue: #1
- Follows: #8

## Note

This one needs a human: the report has to come from a real game.
design:
## Context

Issue #8 built a map that accumulates across turns: `MapKnowledge::from_remembered`
(`crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs:248`) merges regions remembered from earlier turns with the
current report, the current turn wins where they disagree, and both platforms store and read the
sightings back. All of it is unit-tested against small synthetic reports. None of it was ever proved
against the game's own output, because the repository held one report per faction.

**The first half of this bead is already done, by someone else.** ah-dyi imported 25 real fixtures,
among them three consecutive turns of faction 42 in game 3 (t40, t41, t42), three of faction 21 in
game 5 (t23-t25), and three of faction 95 in game 7 (t70-t72, plus t74). So nothing needs capturing
or committing here. What is left is the evidence: an acceptance test in the core that plans a real
multi-step route only the accumulated map can find, and a browser walk that does the same through
IndexedDB and the planner panel.

Two findings from probing the fixtures with the real planner shape this plan, and both contradict
the bead's own description - read them before writing a test against faction 95:

1. **Faction 95 cannot show this at all.** t70 describes a single region, and f95's land holdings
   across t71/t72/t74 are scattered islands separated by ocean. Planning every own unit in t72 (and
   in t74) to every hex of the accumulated map yields *no* route longer than one step, remembered
   or not. The turn-71 fixture the existing tests are built on is a naval faction's turn.
2. **A single report is no longer a one-step map.** The premise in
   `crates/core/tests/movement_plan.rs:3-7` - "no route in this report is longer than one step" -
   held for f95 t71 with eleven regions. It does not hold for the bigger fixtures: f42's t42 alone
   supports twelve-step routes, because its visited regions are contiguous and each brings its own
   exits. What memory adds is therefore *not* "longer than one step" in general; it is **reaching
   ground the current report does not describe**, where the current report knows the destination
   only by name and so has no way there at all.

That second point is what the test must pin, and faction 42 has an exact, small case for it - see
Increments.

When this lands, the accumulation path is backed by the game's own output end to end, the stale map
state is exercised on a hex that is genuinely two turns old, and the stale doc comments above are
corrected.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- `crates/core/tests/movement_plan.rs` - the acceptance suite for planning. Add the new cases here
  rather than in a new file; reuse its `at`, `ruleset`, and the shape of `plan`, and add a sibling
  helper that builds the accumulated map. **Correct the module doc comment at lines 3-7**, which
  states the one-step limitation as a standing fact.
- `crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs` - nothing to change. Use `MapKnowledge::from_remembered`
  (line 248) and `RememberedRegion { region, last_seen_turn }` (line 178). `MapKnowledge::hex`
  (line 352) gives `last_seen_turn` back, which is how the test names the stale hex.
- `crates/core/src/report/sighting.rs` - `region_sightings(&report, turn)` is what both platforms
  store. Building the `RememberedRegion` list straight from `report.regions` is simpler for a test
  and is what `crates/core/src/movement/request.rs:427` already does; either is fine, but do not
  invent a third way.
- `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` - the browser walk. Reuse `loadReport`/`choose` (lines 90-120),
  `selectHex` (line 84), `selectUnit`, `enableMovementPlanner`, and the planner walk at lines
  1172-1204 (`planner-arm`, `planner-route`, `planner-order`, `planner-problem`). The batch-import
  walk at lines 248-280 shows how several reports go in through one `setInputFiles`, and its
  assertions on `import-summary` are the model for this one. **Correct the doc comment at lines
  1140-1148**, which says accumulation cannot be shown because the repository holds one report per
  faction.
- `tests/fixtures/reports/README.md` - the "good for" column of the three f42 rows should say they
  are the multi-step accumulated-route fixture, so the next importer does not treat them as
  interchangeable with the other consecutive runs.
- Nothing in `crates/`, `packages/` production code changes. This bead is evidence, not behaviour.
  If a test fails for a real reason, that is a finding: stop and escalate rather than adjusting the
  assertion to match.

## The case, read out of the reports by hand

Game 3, faction 42 ("The Disinherited Knights"). Current report **t42**; remembered **t40 and t41**.

- `tundra (41,3) in Huykash` is a region **t40 visited** (`...-g3-f42-t40.rep:929`), and neither
  t41 nor t42 describes it. In t42 it is known only as an exit - `Southeast : tundra (41,3)` in
  `forest (40,2)`'s exit list - so t42 alone knows its terrain and nothing else, exits included.
- `tundra (42,2) in Huykash` the faction has **never visited**. t40's (41,3) names it
  (`Northeast : tundra (42,2) in Huykash.`), and t42 names it once, as `Southwest : tundra (42,2)`
  from `tundra (43,1)` - a hex reachable only across ocean.
- So from any land unit near (40,2), t42 alone gives `RouteProblem::NoKnownRoute` to (42,2): the
  one hex that joins them up is known by name only, and a named hex has no exits. With t40
  remembered, (41,3) brings its exits back and the route exists.

Units in `forest (40,2)`, from t42 (region block at `...-g3-f42-t42.rep:968`):

| unit | weight/capacity | mode | route to (42,2) | cost | months |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Woodsmen (10293)` | 360, `0/420/420/0` | ride, 4 points | SE (41,3) tundra 2, NE (42,2) tundra 2 | 4 | 1 |
| `Lookout (12195)` | 10, `0/0/15/0` | walk, 2 points | same two steps | 4 | 2 |

And a three-step, three-month case from `tundra (40,0)` (region at line 703), `Scout (1512)`,
weight 20, capacity `0/0/29/0`, a walker: S into `forest (40,2)` 2, SE into `tundra (41,3)` 2, NE
into `tundra (42,2)` 2 - total 6 over three months. Its middle hex is the remembered one and its
first hex is described by the current turn, so one route crosses both kinds of ground.

Every step above is real, not estimated (`RouteStep::estimated == false`): the destination is a hex
t42 names, so the planner never guesses. These numbers came from running the committed planner and
the committed `config/public/ruleset.json` over the committed fixtures - tundra and forest are in
`terrainCosts.doubled`, so each step is 2 for a walker or a rider - but the implementer should
still read them out of the report text rather than trusting this table.

## Increments

Each opens with a failing test. Run `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test movement_plan` between
them.

1. **A route the current report alone cannot find.** New test in `movement_plan.rs`, e.g.
   `a_remembered_turn_opens_a_route_the_current_report_cannot_find`: build `MapKnowledge::from_report`
   over t42 and assert `plan_route` for `Woodsmen (10293)` to `at(42, 2)` is
   `Err(RouteProblem::NoKnownRoute)`; then build `MapKnowledge::from_remembered(&t42, &[t40, t41])`
   and assert `Ok` with `steps.len() == 2`, both steps `tundra`, `cost == 2` each,
   `total_cost == 4`, `months.len() == 1`, and no step `estimated`. RED first: write the
   remembered half before the helper exists.
2. **The stale hex.** Assert, in the same suite, that
   `map.hex(at(41, 3)).unwrap().last_seen_turn == Some(40)` while
   `map.hex(at(40, 2)).unwrap().last_seen_turn == Some(42)`, and that the (41,3) hex is `visited`
   in the accumulated map but not in the t42-only map. This is the state the bead calls stale, and
   it exists only because a hex is remembered from an earlier turn than the current one.
3. **Multi-month over accumulated ground.** `Lookout (12195)` over the same two steps:
   `total_cost == 4`, `months.len() == 2`, and the first month ends at `at(41, 3)` - unspent points
   carry, which is the rule `plan.rs:26-31` describes and which no real-data test has exercised.
4. **Three steps across both kinds of ground.** `Scout (1512)` from `at(40, 0)` to `at(42, 2)`:
   three steps, `total_cost == 6`, `months.len() == 3`, middle step into the remembered hex.
5. **The doc comments.** Correct `movement_plan.rs:3-7` and `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:1140-1148`
   to say what is now true: a small report stops at its fringe, a large one does not, and what
   memory adds is ground the current turn does not describe. No test change - this increment is the
   record.
6. **The browser walk.** New test in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, e.g.
   `"a route crosses ground only an earlier turn described"`: create a game, `setInputFiles` the
   three f42 reports in one action (out of turn order, as the existing batch walk does), close the
   import summary, `selectHex(page, "1:40,2")`, `selectUnit(page, "10293")`,
   `enableMovementPlanner`, `planner-arm`, `selectHex(page, "1:42,2")`, and expect `planner-route`
   to be visible with "4 movement points" and `planner-order` to read `MOVE SE NE`. Confirm the
   exact order text against `crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs` before asserting it.
7. **The stale banner in the browser.** In the same walk, `selectHex(page, "1:41,3")` and expect
   `panel-region` to contain "Last seen turn 40" and "2 turns ago"
   (`packages/shared/src/workspace/primitives.tsx:57-68`). This is the stale state on screen, on
   real data, which is the half the core test cannot show.
8. **The fixtures README.** Update the "good for" cells for the three f42 rows.

## The test plan

**Core, `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test movement_plan`** - four new tests, named above:
the memory-only route (pins that t42 alone answers `NoKnownRoute` and the accumulated map answers a
two-step route costing 4), the stale hex's `last_seen_turn`, the walker's two months with the first
ending at (41,3), and the scout's three steps costing 6 over three months. Together they pin that
`from_remembered` merges real reports into a graph a route can cross, that the current turn's
description is kept for the hexes it covers, and that a remembered hex keeps the turn it was seen
in.

**Browser, `pnpm run test:smoke`** - one new walk in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` covering the
batch import of three real turns, the planned route across the remembered hex, and the stale banner
on that hex. It is the only test that puts storage, the wasm core and the planner panel on the same
path with real accumulated data.

No new component tests: nothing about the components changes, and the browser walk is where the
integration risk is.

Suites that must run: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`. The native and
PWA suites run the same specs, so `pnpm run check` covers them and must be green before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None. This bead adds tests and corrects comments; nothing a player sees changes, and no new surface
is introduced. The one thing the browser walk asserts on screen - the stale banner's wording - is
already built and already chosen.

## Out of scope

- Committing any further fixture. ah-dyi already committed what this needs; adding another report is
  a new bead against that README's selection rule.
- Faction 95. Its fixtures cannot show a multi-step route, and forcing one out of them would mean
  synthetic data, which is the thing this bead exists to avoid.
- Any change to the planner, the map merge, or the storage layer. If a real defect surfaces, raise a
  bead for it rather than fixing it here.
- Sea routes and SAIL, which are ah-2vy.2's.
- Performance of the accumulated map on a large memory. Worth its own bead if it bites.

## Validation

```
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test movement_plan
cargo test --workspace
pnpm test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check
```

Nothing here needs a human check: every number asserted is readable in the committed report text,
and the smoke walk asserts what it renders.

## Known traps

- **Do not reach for faction 95.** Every existing planner test uses it, so it is the obvious
  fixture to extend, and it cannot show this - see Context. If a plan for one of its units comes
  back multi-step, something else has changed and is worth understanding before continuing.
- **A faction id repeats between games.** Faction 42 exists in game 2 and game 3 with entirely
  different turns. The fixtures wanted here are all `-g3-f42-`; `neworigins-3.0.0-g2-f42-t0.rep` is
  a different faction's first turn.
- **The remembered turn matters, not just "an earlier turn".** (41,3) appears in t40 only. Remember
  t41 alone and there is no route; remember both and `last_seen_turn` is 40, because
  `from_remembered` sorts oldest first and lets the newer sighting win.
- **Every coordinate is `z: 1`.** f95's Barrens hexes sit on another level, which is why probing
  them by `(x, y)` alone finds nothing; `at()` in the test helper already fixes `z` to 1.
- **The smoke suite's serial origin.** Start the new walk with `clearGames` and `createGame` like
  every other walk, or an earlier walk's game is still loaded.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped**, so an assertion that passes in
  Chromium can hide a broken native shell. Assert on `toContainText` against panels that are
  visible without scrolling, and if the stale banner assertion is flaky in one browser, that is
  this trap rather than a race.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled.** A `pnpm run
  test:pwa` straight after `pnpm run test:smoke` fails with timeouts that look like a broken
  worker; `pnpm run check` orders them correctly (`build:web` between the two), so run it rather
  than the suites by hand.
- **Assert `estimated` is false.** The planner will happily cross fog and mark the steps as
  guesses. A test that forgets to check this would still pass if memory stopped working and the
  route were guessed instead - which is exactly the regression this bead is meant to catch.
notes: Planning (2026-08-13): the 'commit a second turn' half is already done - ah-dyi committed three consecutive turns for three factions. What remains is the evidence, and it cannot use faction 95: probing the committed planner over every own unit in f95 t72/t74 against the accumulated map finds no route longer than one step, because that faction's land holdings are ocean-separated. The design uses game 3 faction 42 (t40+t41 remembered, t42 current) instead. The title still says 'commit a second turn'; read the design for what the work actually is.

title: Attach a self-contained web deployment tarball to each release
description:
# Summary

A release publishes three desktop bundles and republishes `atlantis-hud.kurelid.se`, and that is
all. Anyone who wants to run the client on a web server of their own has to clone the repository and
reproduce a Rust/wasm-pack/pnpm toolchain to get a static site out of it. The release should also
attach a **tarball of the complete web deployment**, so that hosting the client is unpacking one
file into a served directory.

# Scope

Add a tarball to the release, built from the same commit as everything else in the run:

- `atlantis-hud-web-v<version>.tar.gz`, attached to the GitHub release alongside the `.dmg`,
  `.AppImage` and `.exe`.
- Contents: the built site (everything `pnpm run build:web` puts in `apps/web/dist/`, PWA service
  worker, manifest, icons and `ruleset.json` included) under a single top-level directory, plus:
  - a **deployment README** — where to unpack it, that it is a static site with no server side, and
    the requirements that are not obvious: HTTPS (the service worker will not register without it),
    the correct `application/wasm` MIME type, and that it must be served from a domain or
    subdomain **root**;
  - **server configuration samples** for nginx and Apache — the WASM MIME type, and cache headers
    that treat Vite's content-hashed assets as immutable while keeping `index.html`,
    `manifest.webmanifest` and the service worker uncached.
- The version must match the tag, as the desktop bundles already do.

**Root path only**, decided with the navigator. `apps/web/vite.config.ts` leaves Vite's `base` at
`/` and pins the PWA manifest's `start_url` and `scope` to `/`, so the built site only works at a
root. That is a deliberate limit here, not an oversight: the tarball ships the same bytes the live
site is built from, and the README says root-only rather than the build learning a second layout.

# Out of scope

- Serving from a subdirectory (`https://example.com/atlantis/`). If someone asks for it, that is a
  separate bead — it means a configurable `base`, a manifest scope that follows it, and PWA coverage
  for the sub-path case.
- Docker images, an installer, or any packaging beyond the tarball.
- Changing how `atlantis-hud.kurelid.se` is published. The tarball is an addition to the release, not
  a change to `deploy.yml`'s SFTP publish.

# Notes on how it fits the existing pipeline

`.github/workflows/release.yml` has three build jobs and a `publish` job that downloads their
artifacts and calls `softprops/action-gh-release`; the `web` job runs after `publish` and calls
`deploy.yml`, which builds the site and uploads it by SFTP without producing any artifact.

So the site is built during a release, but not in a form the release can attach. The implementer
picks the shape — most likely a small `web-tarball` job building `pnpm run build:web` and uploading
an artifact that `publish` includes in its `files:` list, which keeps `publish` as the single place
that attaches things. Reusing `deploy.yml`'s build is the alternative, and it changes a workflow
whose job is the live site; prefer not to unless it turns out to be clean.

Whatever shape it takes, the tarball must be built from the tag, and the release must not publish if
building it fails — the existing jobs are all-or-nothing for the same reason.

# Validation

- Tag a pre-release (or run the workflow on a test tag) and confirm the release page carries
  `atlantis-hud-web-v<version>.tar.gz` beside the three desktop downloads.
- Unpack the tarball into a local static server's root, serve it over HTTPS, and confirm: the
  application loads, `ruleset.json` is fetched, the WASM core parses a report, and the service
  worker registers and the app is installable.
- Confirm the nginx and Apache samples in the tarball actually serve it correctly, rather than being
  written from memory.
- `pnpm run ci` (or the repo's usual gate) green, and the release workflow's version check still
  covers the tarball's name.
design:
## Context

A tagged release publishes three desktop bundles and republishes `atlantis-hud.kurelid.se`; anyone
else who wants to host the web client must reproduce the Rust/wasm-pack/pnpm toolchain. This bead
attaches `atlantis-hud-web-v<version>.tar.gz` to each GitHub release: the complete built site plus
a deployment README and nginx/Apache samples, so self-hosting is unpacking one file. Root-path-only
is already decided (the built site pins `start_url`/`scope` to `/`); the tarball ships the same
bytes the live site is built from and the README says so.

The release must not publish without the tarball — all-or-nothing, like the existing jobs.

Pipeline facts this plan stands on (verified 2026-08-15): `release.yml` has jobs `macos`, `linux`,
`windows`, `publish` (needs all three; `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` at lines 276-315 with a
`files:` list of the three globs and a literal `body:` at 284-315), and `web` (317-333), which
calls `deploy.yml` after `publish`. `deploy.yml` builds the site and uploads by SFTP, **producing
no artifact**. The tag-vs-version check lives only in the `macos` job (lines 38-47). Desktop
artifact names come from Tauri; nothing in the repo constructs a versioned artifact name today.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**1. `.github/workflows/release.yml` — a new `web-tarball` job**, modelled on `deploy.yml`'s build
half (checkout; `actions/setup-node@v4` with `.nvmrc`; `pnpm/action-setup@v4` version `9.12.0`;
`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with `targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`
`shared-key: wasm`; `taiki-e/install-action@v2` `tool: wasm-pack`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`;
the Playwright Chromium cache/install steps — copy `deploy.yml:84-126` faithfully). Then:

- the same tag check as `macos` (copy of release.yml:38-47) — the tarball's name embeds the tag,
  so this job must fail on a mismatch too rather than shipping a mislabelled file;
- `pnpm run build:web` (root script → `@atlantis/web` build; SW and manifest are emitted because
  nothing sets `ATLANTIS_PWA_DISABLE` here);
- `pnpm run test:pwa` against those exact bytes, as `deploy.yml:133-134` does — the release must
  not attach an untested build. (Yes, deploy repeats this later on an identical build; the
  duplication is accepted because deploy runs *after* publish, too late to stop a broken asset.)
- stage and pack:

  ```bash
  stage="atlantis-hud-web-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
  mkdir -p "$stage/site" "$stage/server-samples"
  cp -R apps/web/dist/. "$stage/site/"
  cp docs/self-hosting/README.md "$stage/README.md"
  cp docs/self-hosting/nginx.conf "$stage/server-samples/nginx.conf"
  cp docs/self-hosting/apache.conf "$stage/server-samples/apache.conf"
  tar -czf "${stage}.tar.gz" "$stage"
  ```

- sanity-check the archive before uploading: `tar -tzf` output must contain
  `$stage/site/index.html`, `$stage/site/sw.js`, `$stage/site/manifest.webmanifest`,
  `$stage/site/ruleset.json` and `$stage/README.md`, else fail. (`sw.js` and
  `manifest.webmanifest` are the canaries for a build accidentally run with the PWA disabled — a
  local `check` build omits them.)
- `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, `name: web-tarball`, `path: atlantis-hud-web-*.tar.gz`,
  `if-no-files-found: error`, exactly as the bundle jobs do (release.yml:138-143).

**2. `release.yml` `publish` job**: `needs: [macos, linux, windows, web-tarball]`; a fourth
`actions/download-artifact@v4` step into `release-artifacts/web` (following the split-path pattern
at 258-274); `files:` gains `release-artifacts/web/*.tar.gz`; and the literal `body:` block gains,
after the `**Windows**` section, verbatim (navigator-approved wording, 2026-08-15):

```
**Self-hosting the web client**
Download atlantis-hud-web-v<version>.tar.gz, unpack it, and serve the site/ directory from the
root of an HTTPS domain. The included README covers server requirements; nginx and Apache samples
are inside.
```

(The literal string `v<version>` stays as-is in the body — the body is static text and the
adjacent desktop sections already describe their files generically.)

`deploy.yml` is untouched, per the bead.

**3. `docs/self-hosting/README.md`** — new, the copy that lands in the tarball root. Required
content, in this order; wording is the implementer's except where quoted:

- What this is: the complete built Atlantis HUD web client, a static site with **no server side**.
- Where to put it: serve the `site/` directory (its *contents* at the document root) from the
  **root of a domain or subdomain** — `https://hud.example.com/`, never
  `https://example.com/hud/`. The build pins the PWA `start_url` and `scope` to `/`; a
  subdirectory deployment will not work and is deliberately unsupported.
- **HTTPS is required** — the service worker (offline support, installability) will not register
  over plain HTTP; `http://localhost` is the one exception, usable for a quick look.
- **The `application/wasm` MIME type is required** for `site/assets/atlantis_core_bg-*.wasm`; the
  README names the symptom of getting it wrong (the app loads but cannot parse a report).
- Caching: everything under `site/assets/` is content-hashed and safe to cache forever;
  `index.html`, `sw.js`, `registerSW.js` and `manifest.webmanifest` must be revalidated, or
  updates will not reach the player. Point at the two samples rather than repeating directives.
- SPA fallback: unknown paths should serve `index.html` (the samples do this).
- Which version this is (the directory name carries it) and where releases live (the GitHub
  releases URL).

**4. `docs/self-hosting/nginx.conf`** — new. The directive core, exactly this, wrapped in a
minimal complete `server` block the implementer writes around it (listen 443 ssl, root pointing at
the unpacked `site/`, a comment where cert paths go):

```nginx
# Vite emits .wasm; some distros' mime.types predate it.
types { application/wasm wasm; }

# Content-hashed bundles: immutable.
location /assets/ {
  add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
}

# The entry points the browser must revalidate, or updates never arrive.
location ~ ^/(index\.html|sw\.js|registerSW\.js|manifest\.webmanifest)$ {
  add_header Cache-Control "no-cache";
}

# Single-page app: unknown paths fall back to the shell.
location / {
  try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
}
```

**5. `docs/self-hosting/apache.conf`** — new, the same four concerns for Apache 2.4: `AddType
application/wasm .wasm`, `<LocationMatch "^/assets/">` with the immutable `Header set
Cache-Control`, the no-cache `<LocationMatch>` for the four entry files, and `FallbackResource
/index.html`. Note in a comment that `mod_headers` and `mod_mime` must be enabled.

**6. `scripts/ciDocsGate.ts`** — extend the tooling gate (run by `pnpm run test:tooling`;
currently asserts `ci.yml` structure only: `REQUIRED_JOBS` at line 13, `GATE_JOB` at 16) with
release-workflow assertions: `release.yml` contains a `web-tarball` job, `publish` `needs:`
includes it, and the `files:` list contains `release-artifacts/web/*.tar.gz`. This is the one part
of a workflow change that can be test-driven, and it stops a later edit from quietly dropping the
tarball from the release.

**7. `docs/issue-10-release-contracts.md`** — add a row to the "What publishes what" table (lines
117-121): the release tarball, built by `release.yml`'s `web-tarball` job, attached by `publish`.

## Increments

1. **The gate demands the tarball job and fails.** RED: the new assertions in
   `scripts/ciDocsGate.ts` (increment names its own test run: `pnpm run test:tooling`). GREEN
   comes only at increment 3 — this RED spans the workflow edit, which is normal for a gate test.
2. **The self-hosting docs exist.** `docs/self-hosting/{README.md,nginx.conf,apache.conf}` per
   files 3–5. Verify the nginx sample against a real container before committing:
   `docker run --rm -v <unpacked>/site:/usr/share/nginx/html -v <sample>:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf -p 8080:80 nginx`
   (HTTP is fine for the MIME/caching/fallback checks; the HTTPS requirement is asserted
   separately in validation) — `curl -I` the wasm file for `application/wasm`, an asset for
   `immutable`, `index.html` for `no-cache`, and a nonsense path for a 200 shell. If Docker is
   unavailable on the machine, say so in the PR and mark the sample as verified only by reading —
   do not silently skip.
3. **The workflow.** Files 1, 2 and 7. `pnpm run test:tooling` goes green. Workflow YAML cannot be
   executed pre-merge for a tag push — the real proof is increment 4.
4. **A test tag.** After merge, run the release on a pre-release tag (coordinate with the
   navigator on the version — `scripts/release.ts` owns bumping, and a throwaway tag must not
   collide with the next real version). Confirm the release page carries the tarball beside the
   three bundles; download it, unpack, and run the Validation checks. This increment is the
   bead's acceptance test and cannot be skipped.

## The test plan

- `pnpm run test:tooling` — the extended `ciDocsGate` assertions (increment 1).
- `pnpm run check` — the repo's full gate. (The bead's validation text says `pnpm run ci`; **no
  such script exists** — `check` at package.json:19 is the gate meant.)
- The container check of the nginx sample (increment 2) and the live tag run (increment 4).

## User-facing decisions

Root-path-only was decided with the navigator before this bead was filed and is restated in the
bead; not re-opened. Taken in this planning session (2026-08-15):

1. **Tarball layout**: `atlantis-hud-web-v<version>/` containing `README.md`, `server-samples/`,
   and the site under `site/` — chosen so the docs never end up web-served by accident. Rejected:
   the flat layout with the dist files and README side by side.
2. **Release-notes wording**: the three-sentence "Self-hosting the web client" block quoted in
   file 2, verbatim. Rejected: the one-line variant.

The README/sample *content requirements* are specified in files 3–5; their connective prose is the
implementer's, which the navigator accepted by approving this structure.

## Out of scope

- Subdirectory serving (configurable `base`, manifest scope, sub-path PWA coverage) — a future
  bead if anyone asks.
- Docker images or any packaging beyond the tarball.
- Any change to `deploy.yml` or how `atlantis-hud.kurelid.se` publishes.
- Caddy or other servers beyond the two samples.
- A `ci.yml` job for the tarball — the tarball is a release artifact; PR CI already builds the
  web bundle via `check`'s `build:web`.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test:tooling
pnpm run check
```

Then the tag run (increment 4), and on the unpacked tarball served over HTTPS at a root: the app
loads, `ruleset.json` fetches, the WASM core parses a fixture report, the service worker registers
and the app is installable. Human check (Psylocke): the release page shows four downloads and the
self-hosting section; the unpacked site works per the above.

## Known traps

- **A local `pnpm run check` build ships no service worker** — `check` runs smoke with
  `ATLANTIS_PWA_DISABLE=1`, so a `dist/` left by it lacks `sw.js`/`manifest.webmanifest`. The
  tarball job must do its own fresh `build:web`, and the `tar -tzf` sanity check exists precisely
  to catch a stale or PWA-disabled dist. Never build the tarball from a dist you did not just
  produce.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the SW disabled** (same mechanism) — running
  `test:pwa` after `test:smoke` without rebuilding fails with worker timeouts. In the workflow the
  order is build → test:pwa with nothing between, as `deploy.yml` already does.
- **`ciDocsGate.ts`'s `REQUIRED_JOBS` is about `ci.yml`** — do not add `web-tarball` to that list;
  the release assertions are a separate concern in the same file (or a sibling gate file, either
  is fine so long as `test:tooling` runs it).
- **`GITHUB_REF_NAME` on a tag push is the tag** (`v0.6.0`), so
  `atlantis-hud-web-${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.tar.gz` yields the agreed `-v<version>` name with no string
  surgery; do not strip and re-add the `v`.
- **`softprops/action-gh-release` `files:` globs that match nothing succeed silently** — the
  `if-no-files-found: error` on the upload-artifact step and the download step are the real
  guards; keep both.
- **`scripts/release.ts`'s local gate never runs the browser suites or builds the tarball** — a
  broken `web-tarball` job is discovered only on the tag. That is why increment 4's test tag is
  mandatory, not optional polish.
- **`config/public` is the Vite `publicDir`** (`apps/web/vite.config.ts:22`): `ruleset.json`,
  icons and biomes arrive in `dist/` through it. Do not add copy steps for them; if `ruleset.json`
  is missing from the tarball, the build is wrong, not the packing.
acceptance_criteria: Tagging a release attaches atlantis-hud-web-v<version>.tar.gz to the GitHub release beside the desktop bundles; it contains the full built web application plus a deployment README and nginx/Apache configuration samples; unpacking it into an HTTPS static server's document root gives a working, installable client with no build toolchain; the release fails rather than publishing without it.

title: Compute the diff between two parsed turns
description:
## Summary

The reading half of ah-jg6's comparison: pure functions that take two parsed reports and say what changed. No UI, no storage, no adapters.

## Why this is its own bead

It depends on nothing — it is a function of two `ParsedReport` values, both of which the app can already produce — so it can be built in parallel with ah-jg6.1 and proved entirely against the committed fixtures. It also carries the hard part: deciding what "changed" means for a unit that moved, for a region seen in one turn and not the other, and for an order draft that was reflowed but not altered.

## Scope

- Units: added, removed, and changed between the pair, with the changed fields named rather than a bare "changed".
- Regions: what differs between the two turns' knowledge of a hex, and the distinction between "this region changed" and "this region was not seen in one of the turns", which are not the same thing and must not be reported as the same thing.
- Order drafts: how the two turns' drafts differ.
- Every comparison is a pure module under `packages/shared`, unit-tested against real fixtures — there are consecutive-turn reports for several factions in `tests/fixtures/reports/`.

## Out of scope

- Rendering anything. The view is a sibling.
- Enumerating or loading turns — ah-jg6.1 and ah-jg6.2.
- Diffing more than two turns, or across games.
- Any change to parsing or order validation.
design:
## Context

The reading half of the diff epic `ah-jg6`: pure functions from two `ParsedReport` values (and two
orders texts) to a statement of what changed. No UI (ah-jg6.4), no storage or enumeration (ah-jg6.1,
ah-jg6.3). It depends on nothing unbuilt — `parseReportFull` already produces `ParsedReport` — so it
can be built now and proved against the committed consecutive-turn fixtures
(`tests/fixtures/reports/README.md` lists the pairs; `g5-f21` t23→t24→t25 is committed explicitly
for "turn-over-turn comparison").

The hard part is semantic, and this plan decides it rather than leaving it to the implementer:

- **A unit that moved is moved, not removed-here-and-added-there.** `unitId` is stable within a game.
- **A region unseen in one turn is "not seen", never "changed".** The report describes what the
  faction saw; absence is missing knowledge, not a change in the world. This is the same distinction
  `hexMapModel.ts` already draws (`HexKnowledge` current/stale) — reuse the vocabulary.
- **Foreign units are only compared inside regions seen in both turns.** A foreign unit "missing"
  from a region the faction never visited that turn is not gone, it is unobserved. Own units are
  always visible, so their added/removed is global and real.
- **A reflowed draft is not a change.** Normalize with `commandsOnly` before comparing.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/shared/src/turnDiff.ts`** (new) — the whole module. Public surface:

  ```ts
  export type ValueChange = { field: string; before: string; after: string };
  export type UnitChange = { unitId: string; name: string; changes: ValueChange[];
                            movedFrom: string | null; movedTo: string | null };
  export type UnitsDiff = { added: ReportUnit[]; removed: ReportUnit[]; changed: UnitChange[] };
  export type RegionChange = { regionId: string; changes: ValueChange[] };
  export type RegionsDiff = { onlyInNewer: string[]; onlyInOlder: string[];
                              changed: RegionChange[] };   // regionIds; "not seen" ≠ "changed"
  export type TurnDiff = { units: UnitsDiff; regions: RegionsDiff };
  export function diffTurns(older: ParsedReport, newer: ParsedReport): TurnDiff;
  export type UnitOrdersChange = { unitId: string; before: string[]; after: string[] };
  export type OrdersDiff = { changed: UnitOrdersChange[];
                             onlyInNewer: string[]; onlyInOlder: string[] };  // unitIds
  export function diffOrders(olderText: string, newerText: string): OrdersDiff;
  ```

  Decisions bound into that surface:
  - `ValueChange` carries **preformatted strings** on both sides (mirroring the core's
    `FieldChange { field, original }` at `core-client/src/index.ts:322`, extended with the after
    side) — the view renders them without knowing item arithmetic. Small local formatters:
    `ItemAmount[]` as `"3 swords, 2 horses"` (sorted by tag), `SkillInfo[]` as
    `"combat 2 (90)"`-style, scalars via `String()` with `null` as `"—"`.
  - Unit fields compared, by name: `name`, `factionId`, `own`, `onGuard`, `flags`, `items`,
    `skills`, `men`, `structureId`. `items`/`skills`/`flags` compared as multisets keyed by
    tag/name, order-insensitively. `regionId` difference becomes `movedFrom`/`movedTo`, not a
    `ValueChange`. `weight`/`capacity` are **not** compared — derived from items, they would
    duplicate every cargo change. `menByRace`/`menEstimated` are not compared (see traps).
  - Region fields compared: `terrain`, `province`, `settlement`, `population`, `race`, `taxBase`,
    `wages`, `maxWages`, `entertainment`, `products`, `wanted`, `forSale`, `structures` (multiset
    by `structureId`+`name`), and the unit-bearing changes fall out of the units diff, not here.
    `exits` are not compared — geography does not change, and phantom exit diffs from partial
    sightings would be noise.
  - `diffOrders` is text-in, text-out on purpose: drafts come from `loadOrderDraft` as plain
    strings, and the template lives in `OrdersTemplate.text` — which of those ah-jg6.4 feeds in is
    its decision, not this module's.

- **Reuse from `packages/shared`** (all existing):
  - `ordersDocument.ts` — `findUnitBlocks`, `readUnitOrders`, `commandsOnly` (:232) for the
    normalize-then-compare; do not write a new block parser.
  - `hexMapModel.ts` — `regionIdOf`/`parseRegionId` (:94/:115) for keys; never reformat
    coordinates by hand (`regionId` is `"z:x,y"`, z from 1 at the surface).
  - Test factories: copy the `report()`/`region()` factory shape from `hexMapModel.test.ts:97` and
    the `unit(overrides)` factory from `unitComposition.test.ts:1-25`.
- **`packages/browser-core/src/turnDiff.fixtures.test.ts`** (new) — the fixture-backed proof lives
  here, **not** in `packages/shared`: shared depends only on `@atlantis/core-client` types and
  cannot parse a `.rep`; `parseReportFull.test.ts:14-26` in browser-core already boots the real
  wasm against fixture files and is the pattern to copy.

## Increments

Each is RED first in `packages/shared/src/turnDiff.test.ts` unless said otherwise.

1. **Nothing changes against itself.** "diffing a report against itself reports nothing" — empty
   added/removed/changed/onlyIn* across units and regions. GREEN: the skeleton.
2. **Own units come and go.** "an own unit present only in the newer turn is added" and its mirror;
   plus the symmetry pin "swapping the arguments swaps added and removed".
3. **A moved unit is moved.** "an own unit in a different region is one moved unit, not an add and
   a remove" — `movedFrom`/`movedTo` carry the two regionIds; no entry in added/removed.
4. **Changes are named.** "a unit's men change names the field with both values"; "an item gained
   names items with before and after lists"; "reordered items are not a change" (multiset).
5. **Foreign units only where both turns looked.** "a foreign unit in a region unseen in the other
   turn is not reported"; "a foreign unit gone from a region seen in both turns is removed".
6. **Regions: not seen is not changed.** "a region seen only in the newer turn is onlyInNewer and
   has no field changes"; "a region seen in both turns with a population change is changed with the
   field named".
7. **Market and structures.** "a price change in forSale names the market field"; "a structure
   present only in the newer turn's region is a structures change" (multiset by id+name).
8. **Orders diff, reflow-blind.** "a draft reflowed with blank lines and comments is not a change"
   (via `commandsOnly`); "a changed order line reports the unit with before and after commands";
   "a unit with orders in only one draft is onlyIn*".
9. **The fixtures agree.** In `packages/browser-core/src/turnDiff.fixtures.test.ts`: parse
   `neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep` and `-t24.rep` with `parseReportFull` (both through the same
   path), run `diffTurns`, and assert a handful of differences the implementer verifies by reading
   the two reports (at least: one own-unit change, one region change, one moved or added unit), plus
   the invariants "no unit appears in more than one of added/removed/changed" and "self-diff of t24
   is empty". Repeat the self-diff on `g7-f95-t71` for scale.

## The test plan

- `packages/shared/src/turnDiff.test.ts` — increments 1–8, hand-built factories, house style: a
  `describe` per domain (units/regions/orders), a comment on each case saying why it matters.
- `packages/browser-core/src/turnDiff.fixtures.test.ts` — increment 9, real wasm, real reports.
- Suites: `pnpm run test` runs both packages (`pnpm -r run test` via `scripts/runSuites.ts`). No
  smoke tests — nothing here renders.

## User-facing decisions

None. This bead is a pure module; every choice above is semantics of computation, and the one place
taste enters (how a change is worded on screen) belongs to ah-jg6.4, which receives structured
`ValueChange`s precisely so it can decide.

## Out of scope

- Rendering anything (ah-jg6.4), enumerating or loading turns (ah-jg6.1, ah-jg6.3).
- Diffing battles or turn events/messages — they are per-turn narrative, not state to diff.
- Diffing more than two turns, or across games (`unitId` is only unique within a game).
- Any change to parsing, `ordersDocument.ts`, or order validation.
- Movement inference beyond "the unit's region differs" — no pathing, no cause.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test
pnpm run check   # full gate before the PR
```

No human check: the module has no surface. The fixture test in increment 9 is the acceptance.

## Known traps

- **Parse both sides the same way.** `men`/`menEstimated`/`menByRace` differ between
  `parseReportFull` and `parseReportClassified` output for the same report; diffing one of each
  produces phantom men changes. The module therefore never compares `menEstimated`/`menByRace`, and
  the fixture test parses both fixtures through `parseReportFull`. State the requirement in the
  module's doc comment.
- **`packages/shared` cannot parse a report.** It has no dependency on `@atlantis/browser-core` and
  must not gain one for this — the fixture-backed test lives in browser-core, the pure tests in
  shared with factories.
- **`commandsOnly` keeps `@;` lines** (repeating orders are orders) because they start with `@`,
  while plain `;` comments are dropped — rely on it, do not "improve" it, and pin the `@;` case in
  increment 8's reflow test.
- **A unit formed this turn has no id until the next report** — it appears in drafts as a `FORM`
  block. `diffOrders` keys by `findUnitBlocks`' unitIds, so new-unit blocks fall outside the
  per-unit diff; that is accepted and noted in the doc comment, not silently wrong.
- **`regionId` is `"z:x,y"` with z counted from 1** and the lattice invariant `(x+y) % 2 === 0` —
  always go through `regionIdOf`/`parseRegionId`.
- **Nullable scalars everywhere** (`population`, `wages`, `taxBase`, header fields): `null` on one
  side is a real change and must format as `"—"`, not crash and not compare equal to `0`.
- **`ImportedTurnRecord` carries the flat `ReportParseResult`, not `ParsedReport`** — whoever wires
  this to stored turns (ah-jg6.4) re-parses `rawReport`; this module must not grow a dependency on
  the record type.

title: Plan sea routes for units aboard a fleet, emitting SAIL
description:
## Summary

The planning half of ah-2vy: a Sail movement mode, sea routes, and SAIL orders instead of MOVE.

## Why this is its own bead

ah-2vy.1 adds the ship's sailing requirement to the ruleset; this bead is everything that then uses
it. Splitting keeps the ruleset change small and reviewable on its own, and keeps this bead's plan
from being written against a schema that is about to change.

## Scope

Carried from the parent, unchanged:

- A Sail movement mode, with speed taken from the ship rather than from the unit.
- Flat terrain cost at sea: "For a fleet to enter any region only costs one movement point", so the
  terrain premium that applies to riding and walking does not apply.
- Recognising that a unit is aboard a fleet it can actually sail, skill requirement included.
- Emitting SAIL rather than MOVE.
- Refusing a sea route with a named reason when the crew cannot sail the ship.

Two loose ends from #8 belong here. `MovementMode` has no `Sail` variant, deliberately. And
`crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs` has a `can_swim` that nothing outside its own test calls — this
ruleset's water rule exempts only flight from needing a ship, so swimming currently decides nothing;
it should either be used here or deleted.

Guards behave differently at sea: a fleet enters a guarded region and is then stopped, where a land
unit is prevented from entering at all.

## Out of scope

- Combat at sea; building or repairing ships.
- Whether the planner's surface needs anything new. The mode is inferred from the unit's situation
  rather than chosen by the player, so this is expected to need no UI decision — confirm that when
  planning, and take it to the navigator if it turns out otherwise.

## Depends on

ah-2vy.1, for the sailing requirement.
design:
## Context

The planning half of `ah-2vy`: a Sail movement mode, sea routes, and SAIL orders instead of MOVE.
Its blocker ah-2vy.1 is **merged** (commit `d09a573`, PR #165): every ship item in
`config/public/ruleset.json` now carries `sailingSkill`, `cargoCapacity` and `moves` (per-hull speed
in hexes/month), read through `ItemEntry` in `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:145-161`, and the
skill catalogue has `SAIL`. Crew skills are already parsed onto `ReportUnit.skills`.

What exists and what is missing, measured against the code on main:

- `MovementMode` (`rules.rs:20-26`) deliberately has no `Sail` — its doc comment and
  `docs/ruleset-contract.md:148-152` both promise that, and this bead is the bead that revokes the
  promise. Both texts must be updated.
- The planner (`plan.rs`) is Dijkstra over `MapKnowledge`; water blocks every non-flying mode via
  one function, `blocks(ruleset, mode, terrain)` (`plan.rs:208-210`).
- **The planner cannot see a fleet today**: `KnownHex` (`graph.rs:138-153`) carries no structures —
  they are only harvested for roads (`graph.rs:200-204`). A unit aboard one is known only by
  `ReportUnit.structure_id`.
- The mode is **inferred, never chosen** (`mobility(unit)`, `mode.rs:66-88`); no adapter signature
  carries a mode anywhere. Sail keeps that: aboard a sailable fleet → sail. **No new UI control**,
  which the bead asked to confirm — confirmed, and the navigator was consulted only on the one new
  player-visible sentence (below).
- MOVE text is emitted in TS (`routeAsOrder`, `PlannerPanel.tsx:132-136`) and stripped/replaced by
  `applyRoute` (`AppShell.tsx:1813-1833`, regex `^\s*@?\s*(move|advance)\b`); Rust reads orders for
  the trace via `last_top_level_move` (`request.rs:197`), MOVE/ADVANCE only.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**Ruleset (scrape → data → model):**
- `packages/ruleset/src/rules.ts` — scrape the fleet movement rule the way `OceanRule` was scraped
  (rules.ts:173-178, provenance sentence kept verbatim): the flat entry cost, from the rules' own
  sentence "For a fleet to enter any region only costs one movement point", and the fleet-entry
  constraint from the SAIL section of the rules (fleets sail ocean hexes and may enter coastal land
  regions — read the actual sentence at https://atlantis-pbem.com/rules and scrape what it states;
  keep its text as provenance). New block in `config/public/ruleset.json` beside `ocean`, e.g.
  `"sailing": { "flatCost": 1, "landNeedsCoast": true, "terrain": "ocean", "provenance": ... }`.
- `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` — a `SailingRule` struct mirroring that block, accessors
  beside `water_needs_a_ship()`; `validate` refuses a zero flat cost. `MovementMode` gains `Sail`
  (serde camelCase, so `"sail"`); `movement_points(Sail)` must not invent a number — see the
  refactor below.
- `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts` — scraper coverage in the ah-2vy.1 style.

**Movement core:**
- `crates/core/src/movement/graph.rs` — `KnownHex` gains `structures: Vec<Structure>` (populated in
  `from_report` and `from_remembered`; roads keep their existing harvest). This is the general fix
  for "the planner cannot see a fleet".
- `crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs` — new fleet questions beside `mobility`:
  - `fleet_of<'a>(unit, hex) -> Option<&'a Structure>` — the structure `unit.structure_id` names,
    when its kind names a hull or a fleet.
  - `parse_fleet_kind(kind: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String /*hull name*/, u32 /*count*/)>>` — both
    report wordings: a bare hull (`"Longship"`) and the newer `"Fleet, 8 Corsairs"` /
    `"Fleet, 2 Galleons"` (singular/plural hull names must map to the ruleset item by name).
  - `sailing_requirement(fleet, ruleset) -> Option<i64>` and `fleet_speed(fleet, ruleset) ->
    Option<u32>` — **prefer the server's own words in `description`** (`"Sailors: 4/4"` states
    have/need; `"MaxSpeed: 4"` states speed — see `g3-f42-t40.rep:1120`), fall back to ruleset
    arithmetic: requirement = Σ hulls' `sailingSkill`, speed = min of hulls' `moves`.
  - `crew_sailing_levels(units_in_hex, structure_id) -> i64` — Σ of `SAIL` skill levels over **own**
    units aboard the same structure.
  - **Delete `can_swim`** (`mode.rs:104-113`) and its test. The bead names it as use-or-delete;
    sail does not consult swim capacity (this ruleset's water rule exempts only flight), so it is
    dead code with no prospective caller left.
- `crates/core/src/movement/plan.rs` — the inference and the search:
  - In `plan_route`, before `mobility()`: if `fleet_of(unit, origin_hex)` is Some, the mode is
    `Sail`; crew check first — insufficient levels → new
    `RouteProblem::CrewCannotSail { required: i64, available: i64 }`; an unknown hull (no ruleset
    item and no server-stated Sailors/MaxSpeed) → fall back to the existing land planning as if not
    aboard (never guess a ship's numbers).
  - `blocks()` learns Sail: water never blocks; a land hex blocks unless the sailing rule allows a
    coastal entry — coastal meaning the hex has at least one known water neighbour (through
    `MapKnowledge`, estimated hexes counting as unknown, in keeping with the fog rules).
  - `step_cost` for Sail: the flat cost for every enterable hex; roads and `doubled_for` do not
    apply (the flat-cost sentence is the rule).
  - Speed: refactor the two callers of `ruleset.movement_points(mode)` (`plan.rs`,
    `split_into_months`) to take a resolved `points_per_month: u32`, computed once: land modes from
    `MovementPoints`, Sail from `fleet_speed`. `movement_points(Sail)` becomes unreachable —
    `unreachable!` with a sentence, or restructure so the match never sees it.
  - The pre-check that names a water origin (`plan.rs:143-156`) must not fire for a sail plan — a
    fleet's origin *is* water; amend the order of checks.
- `crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs` — `render_move` gains a sail twin or a parameter (the order
  word is the only difference); `parse_move` learns the `SAIL` keyword; `request.rs`'s
  `last_top_level_move` (:197) recognises SAIL lines so a written SAIL order traces.
- `crates/core/src/movement/trace.rs` — traces a sail order with the sail legality (`blocks` already
  shared); mode inference for the trace comes from the unit's fleet exactly as planning does.
- `crates/core/src/movement/risk.rs` — guards stay advisory (nothing in the planner blocks on them
  today, for any mode); for a sail route the sentence changes to the sea behaviour: guards stop a
  fleet after it enters rather than barring entry. One wording branch in the existing prose.

**Boundary and TS surface (no adapter signature changes — the mode travels in the existing
`RoutePlan.mode` field):**
- `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` — `RoutePlan.mode` union gains `"sail"` (:194), `TracedPath`
  likewise (:310); `RouteProblem` union gains the crew refusal (:207-214).
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/PlannerPanel.tsx` — `routeAsOrder` emits `SAIL ...` when
  `plan.mode === "sail"`; `describeProblem` gains the navigator's sentence (below). The existing
  test "a sentence for every RouteProblem kind" (`plannerPanel.test.ts`) forces this.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — `applyRoute`'s stripping regex becomes
  `^\s*@?\s*(move|advance|sail)\b` so applying a route replaces an old SAIL line too.

## Increments

House style throughout: integration tests in `crates/core/tests/movement_*.rs` against committed
reports, each test's doc comment quoting the exact report line it stands on; inline `mod tests` for
the pure pieces.

1. **The sailing rule reaches the ruleset.** RED: `movement_ruleset.rs` (or `rules.rs` inline) —
   `reads_the_fleet_movement_rule_from_the_committed_ruleset`. GREEN: scraper + json + `SailingRule`.
2. **The planner can see the fleet.** RED: `movement_graph.rs` — a `KnownHex` built from
   `g3-f42-t40.rep` carries `+ Ship [329] : Longship; Load: 110/150; Sailors: 4/4; MaxSpeed: 4.`
   GREEN: `KnownHex.structures`.
3. **Fleet arithmetic.** RED (inline `mode.rs` tests): `parse_fleet_kind` on `"Longship"` and
   `"Fleet, 2 Galleons"` (fixture `g3-f42-t82.rep:5885`); requirement/speed preferring the stated
   `Sailors: 4/4` / `MaxSpeed: 4` and falling back to ruleset numbers; crew levels summed from the
   two `Sailors` units at `SAIL 2` each. Delete `can_swim` in this increment (its test goes with it).
4. **A sea route is planned and refused rightly.** RED: `movement_plan.rs` —
   `a_crewed_longship_is_planned_a_sea_route` (Ship [329]: 2×SAIL-2 crew = exactly the 4 levels a
   Longship needs — the boundary case the fixture hands us; assert `mode: Sail`, flat step costs,
   months split by MaxSpeed 4); `an_uncrewed_fleet_names_the_missing_skill` (assert
   `CrewCannotSail { required, available }`); amend `a_unit_standing_at_sea_cannot_walk_ashore`
   (`movement_plan.rs:112-125`) — its unit still gets that refusal only if it is *not* aboard a
   sailable fleet; read the fixture and pin whichever is true. Land destination must be coastal;
   an inland destination refuses with the existing no-route/ocean problems.
5. **SAIL in and out of text.** RED: `movement_orders.rs` — `render` emits `SAIL N NE`, `parse_move`
   reads it back; `movement_trace.rs` — a written SAIL order traces over water with `blocked_from`
   set where it enters an illegal hex; `request.rs`'s reader finds a SAIL line.
6. **The TS surface.** RED: `plannerPanel.test.ts` — the every-problem-has-a-sentence test fails on
   the new variant; `routeAsOrder` emits `SAIL` for a sail plan. Plus the `applyRoute` regex change
   pinned by an `AppShell`-level test if one exists for MOVE-stripping (follow the existing test's
   shape; add one if not). GREEN: the three TS files.
7. **Boundary parity.** RED: `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` — a `RoutePlanResponse` with
   `mode: "sail"` and a `CrewCannotSail` problem round-trips identically through the wasm and Tauri
   adapters (the existing parity-test pattern).

## The test plan

Rust: `cargo test --workspace` — increments 1–5 as named above, in the movement test files' style
(real reports, quoted lines, no synthetic maps).
TS: `pnpm run test` — `plannerPanel.test.ts`, `index.test.ts` parity, ruleset scraper tests.
No smoke tests: the movement planner is behind the `movementPlanner` feature flag and has no smoke
coverage today; do not add flag-flipping smoke in this bead.

## User-facing decisions

Asked and decided with the navigator, 2026-08-14. One decision, no mockup (a sentence in the
existing planner panel, no new surface):

- The crew refusal reads **skill-focused**: "The crew cannot sail this fleet: it needs {required}
  levels of sailing, and the units aboard have {available}." Rejected: an action-suffixed variant
  and a terse variant.

Confirmed with the code, as the bead asked: the mode is inferred from the unit's situation (aboard a
sailable fleet → sail), shown read-only in the existing `Travel` field as `sail` — **no new control,
no UI decision beyond the sentence above**.

## Out of scope

- Combat at sea; building or repairing ships (the bead says so).
- Any new planner UI; choosing a mode by hand.
- Moving the fleet's *other* passengers' orders, cargo/`cargoCapacity` load checks, or overloading
  a ship — this bead plans the route and writes the order for the selected unit.
- The map drawing of fleets (`isShip` in `mapThemes/hexView.ts:184-187` does not recognise
  `"Fleet, N Corsairs"` and draws it as a building — a real defect, but its own bead; create it at
  P4 if it bothers anyone before then).
- Smoke coverage for the flagged-off planner.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm run test
pnpm run check   # the full gate, before the PR
```

Human check (navigator, post-merge is fine): flag the planner on, select a unit aboard the crewed
Longship in the g3 fixture game, plan across water — the panel says `Travel: sail`, the order
applied is `SAIL ...`, and planning from an uncrewed fleet names the missing levels.

## Known traps

- **`movement_points(Sail)` must never answer.** Sail speed comes from the fleet, not from
  `MovementPoints`; route the resolved points-per-month through the callers instead. A default of 0
  would silently plan zero-length months; a panic in a reachable path would take the wasm down.
- **Prefer the server's stated numbers.** `Sailors: 4/4` and `MaxSpeed: 4` in a structure's
  description are the engine's own arithmetic; ruleset sums are the fallback for the newer report
  wording that omits them. Getting this backwards produces refusals the game would not make.
- **The fleet-kind wording varies**: `"Longship"`, `"Fleet, 8 Corsairs"`, `"Fleet, 2 Galleons"`,
  and the structure *name* is arbitrary (`"Ship"`, `"Bradr"`, `"Red Squadron"`). Match on kind,
  never on name; map plural hull names to singular ruleset entries.
- **An unknown hull falls back to land planning, not to a guess.** No ruleset entry and no stated
  numbers means the planner does not know the ship; refusing to sail is honest, inventing a speed is
  not.
- **The water-origin pre-check** (`plan.rs:143-156`) fires today for exactly the unit this bead
  serves (aboard a fleet, standing at sea). Reorder the checks or sail plans are refused before
  inference runs — the amended test in increment 4 pins this.
- **`step_into`'s fog comment** (`plan.rs:463-464`) warns that a route already at sea would guess
  itself further out to sea — re-read it when touching the fog branch for sail; estimated hexes at
  sea remain estimated.
- **Both promise-documents must be updated**: the `MovementMode` doc comment (`rules.rs:10-19`) and
  `docs/ruleset-contract.md:148-152` say Sail does not exist. Leaving either contradicting the code
  fails the next reader.
- **`rules.rs::validate` refuses a water terrain in `doubled`** — the sailing rule's flat cost must
  not be modelled by adding ocean to the doubled list; it is its own rule.
- **The scraper is ship-only on purpose** (ah-2vy.1 kept Summon Wind's "up to N sailing skill
  points" from matching); keep any new scraping equally anchored to its exact sentence, provenance
  string included.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree; branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: A unit aboard a fleet can be given a sea route with a cost and a month breakdown; the route emits SAIL rather than MOVE; a crew without the sailing skill the ship requires is refused with that as the named reason; sea movement costs one point per region regardless of terrain; land units are unaffected; can_swim is either used or deleted

title: Scrape the sailing skill a ship requires into the ruleset
description:
## Summary

The data page states, for every ship, how much sailing skill its crew needs between them:

    Longship [LONG]. This is a ship with a capacity of 150 and a speed of
      4 hexes per month. This ship requires a total of 4 levels of sailing
      skill to sail.

The scraper reads the capacity (`cargoCapacity`) and the speed (`moves`) and drops the skill
requirement. Sail planning cannot refuse "the crew cannot sail this ship" without it, which is one
of ah-2vy's acceptance criteria.

## Why this is its own bead

It is a self-contained addition to the ruleset scraper and its Rust mirror, with no planner
involvement, and ah-2vy.2 would otherwise be planned against a ruleset schema this bead changes.

## Scope

- Read `requires a total of <n> levels of sailing skill to sail` in
  `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`, beside the existing `moves` and `cargoCapacity` reads.
- Mirror it on the Rust `ItemEntry` (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:154`) as an optional field,
  so an older committed ruleset still deserialises.
- Assert it on the committed ruleset, as `data.test.ts:126` already does for cargo capacity: every
  ship has one.

## Out of scope

- Anything about planning, routing or SAIL orders. That is ah-2vy.2.
- Summon Wind and the wind-related items, which add movement points to ships requiring up to so many
  sailing points. Noted here because the same wording appears on those entries and must not be
  mistaken for a ship's own requirement.
design:
## Context

The data page states three numbers for every ship. The scraper reads two of them:

    Longship [LONG]. This is a ship with a capacity of 150 and a speed of
      4 hexes per month. This ship requires a total of 4 levels of sailing
      skill to sail.

`cargoCapacity` comes from `with a capacity of 150` and `moves` from `a speed of 4 hexes per month`
(`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:185-192`, `:239-241`). The sailing requirement is dropped. Sail
planning cannot refuse "the crew cannot sail this ship" — an acceptance criterion of the parent
ah-2vy — without it, and ah-2vy.2 is blocked on this bead for exactly that reason.

Checked against the committed data page: **all nine ships state a requirement**, so the field is
present everywhere it should be and the test can say so.

| tag | ship | moves | cargo | sailing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LONG | Longship | 4 | 150 | 4 |
| RAFT | Raft | 2 | 450 | 2 |
| COG | Cog | 4 | 750 | 6 |
| GALL | Galleon | 4 | 2700 | 15 |
| GLLY | Galley | 4 | 1200 | 12 |
| CORS | Corsair | 5 | 1500 | 15 |
| BALL | Balloon | 4 | 100 | 3 |
| AIRS | Airship | 4 | 800 | 10 |
| CLOU | Cloudship | 4 | 1500 | 15 |

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`** — a `sailingOf(kind, paragraph)` beside `cargoOf` (`:185`),
  built the same way and spread into the entry the same way (`:237`). Ship-only, like `cargoOf`, and
  reading `requires a total of (\d+) levels of sailing skill` through the existing `readNumber`
  helper. Add the field to `ItemEntry` (`:64`, beside `cargoCapacity`), optional, with a doc comment
  saying what it is for — this package documents every field it keeps and why.
- **`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`** — `ItemEntry` at `:154` gains
  `#[serde(default)] pub sailing_skill: Option<i64>` beside `cargo_capacity` (`:164`). The struct is
  `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, so it reads `sailingSkill` with no extra attribute.
  `#[serde(default)]` is what lets an older committed ruleset still deserialise — the field must not
  be required.
- **`config/public/ruleset.json`** — regenerated and committed, from the committed fixtures rather
  than the network:

  ```bash
  pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- \
    --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html \
    --data  tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html
  ```

  The CLI takes a local file wherever it takes a URL, which is how the fixtures are re-read without
  touching the network (`packages/ruleset/src/cli.ts:8`).
- **`packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`** — the ship assertions at `:126` and `:175-179` are the
  pattern; the new ones go beside them.
- **`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`** tests — the committed ruleset is `include_str!`ed at
  `:541`, which is where the Rust side proves it can read what the scraper wrote.

## Increments

1. **The Rust field first**, so the two sides cannot land out of step in the wrong order. RED: a test
   in `rules.rs` asserting the committed ruleset gives `LONG` a `sailing_skill` of 4 — it fails
   because the JSON has no such field yet. GREEN: the field, still failing until increment 3.
   (If a red test that stays red across two increments is uncomfortable, do 2 and 3 first and let
   this one go green immediately; the ordering above is the one that proves the `serde(default)`
   works, since between 1 and 3 the crate is deserialising a ruleset that lacks the field.)
2. **The scrape.** RED: `reads the sailing skill a ship requires` in `data.test.ts`, over the
   committed data page fixture. GREEN: `sailingOf` and the `ItemEntry` field.
3. **The regenerated ruleset.** Run the scrape command above, commit `config/public/ruleset.json`,
   and increment 1's test goes green.

## The test plan

Suites: `pnpm -r run test` (the ruleset package's own vitest) and `cargo test -p atlantis-core`.
`pnpm run check` before the PR.

`packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`:
- `reads the sailing skill a ship requires` — `LONG` is 4 and `RAFT` is 2, named values from the
  page, in the style of the existing `BALL`/`LONG` cargo assertions at `:175-179`.
- `every ship states the sailing skill it needs` — all nine, mirroring the `cargoCapacity` sweep at
  `:126`. The table above is why this can be asserted as an absolute rather than hedged.
- `does not read a sailing requirement onto something that is not a ship` — the summon-wind skill
  and the wind-related items talk about "ships requiring up to 12 sailing skill points" and
  "up to 24 sailing skill points". Different wording, different entry kind, and both guards should
  hold; this test is what proves they do.

`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`:
- `reads the sailing skill from the committed ruleset` — `LONG` is 4.
- `a ruleset written before this field still loads` — deserialise a small JSON item entry with no
  `sailingSkill` and get `None`. This is the `serde(default)` contract, and it is the one that
  breaks a running installation if it is wrong.

Nothing else. The planner does not read this field until ah-2vy.2.

## User-facing decisions

None. This is scraper data and a serde field; nothing is displayed, and the parent's only UI
question — whether the planner's surface needs anything new for sailing — belongs to ah-2vy.2, which
expects the answer to be no because the mode is inferred from the unit's situation rather than
chosen by the player.

## Out of scope

- Everything about planning, routing, `MovementMode::Sail` and SAIL orders. That is ah-2vy.2, which
  this bead blocks.
- Summon Wind, wind items, and anything that *adds* movement points to a ship. They are noted here
  only because their wording is close enough to be caught by a careless regex.
- Any other unscraped ship property. If one is wanted later it is a one-line addition on the same
  pattern.
- Re-scraping from the live site. The committed fixtures are the source for this change.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test
cargo test -p atlantis-core
pnpm run check
```

And read the regenerated `config/public/ruleset.json` diff by eye before committing: it should add
exactly nine `sailingSkill` lines and change nothing else. A diff that touches anything more means
the scrape picked up something other than this change, and the ruleset is the file every route is
costed against.

## Known traps

- **A tag appears on the page more than once.** `Cloudship [CLOU]` occurs both in its own entry and
  inside the Summon Wind spell text — a whole-page regex for `CLOU` finds the spell first and
  concludes the Cloudship has no sailing requirement, which is wrong; it needs 15. Read from the
  entry paragraph the scraper already isolates (`entryParagraphs`), exactly as `cargoOf` does, and
  never from the whole document.
- **The requirement wraps across physical lines** — `requires a total of 4 levels of sailing` /
  `  skill to sail`. Whatever `cargoOf` and the `moves` reads already do about that is what to do
  here; do not write a regex that assumes one line.
- **`#[serde(default)]` is not optional.** Without it, a shell holding a ruleset written before this
  change fails to deserialise the whole file — every route, every cost, everything — rather than
  losing one field. The second Rust test exists for that reason and must not be dropped as
  redundant.
- **A flying "ship" is still a ship.** The Balloon, Airship and Cloudship are `kind: "ship"` and each
  states a sailing requirement, so a `kind !== "ship"` guard is right and a "not a flying one"
  refinement is wrong.
- **Regenerating from the network would change unrelated numbers.** The site moves; the committed
  fixtures do not. Pass the local paths.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. Branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.
acceptance_criteria: packages/ruleset/src/data.ts records the sailing skill a ship requires; the Rust ItemEntry carries it as an optional field so an older ruleset still deserialises; a test over the committed ruleset asserts every ship has one; the regenerated ruleset is committed

title: Record beads CLI traps in the beads-workflow skill
description:
Three beads behaviours bit during the #126 migration and are not obvious from the CLI help. Record them in the beads-workflow skill so the next session does not rediscover them.

- The pre-commit auto-export can write a stale snapshot: a commit picked up a JSONL still containing a throwaway bead that had already been deleted.
- `bd config set` accepts unknown keys silently, so a mistyped key reads as success; probing also rewrote a commented-out default in `.beads/config.yaml` and stripped its trailing newline.
- The `owner` field is taken from `git config user.email` at creation and has no override; `--actor` sets `created_by` only, and `--assignee` is a separate field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.claude/skills/beads-workflow/SKILL.md` carries a section covering all three behaviours.
- The export trap names the verification command that catches it.

title: Plan sea movement for fleets
description:
## Summary

Plan sea movement: routes for units aboard a fleet, emitting SAIL rather than MOVE.

## Problem

The planner handles land movement only. A unit standing in an ocean hex - which is what a unit
aboard a fleet looks like in a report - is refused with "the sea is in the way", and so is any
destination across water. That is correct for what #8 built, and useless for a faction that sails.

The rules make sailing a second system rather than a variation:

- A fleet has its own speed, stated per ship on the data page: a Longship moves 4 hexes per month, a
  Raft 2, a Galleon 4
- "For a fleet to enter any region only costs one movement point", so the terrain premium that
  applies to riding and walking units does not apply at sea
- Sailing needs a total of N levels of sailing skill among the crew, stated per ship
- A fleet has a cargo capacity, which the scraper already records as cargoCapacity
- Guards behave differently: a fleet enters a guarded region and is then stopped, where a land unit
  is prevented from entering at all

## Scope

- A Sail movement mode, with speed taken from the ship rather than from the unit
- Flat terrain cost at sea, per the quoted rule
- Recognising that a unit is aboard a fleet it can actually sail, including the skill requirement
- Emitting SAIL orders rather than MOVE
- Refusing a sea route with a named reason when the crew cannot sail the ship

## Out of scope

- Combat at sea
- Building or repairing ships

## Acceptance criteria

- A unit aboard a fleet can be given a sea route with a cost and a month breakdown
- A crew without the sailing skill the ship requires is refused with that as the reason
- Land units are unaffected

## Notes

Two loose ends from #8 belong here. MovementMode has no Sail variant, deliberately. And
crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs has a can_swim function that nothing outside its own test calls -
this ruleset's water rule exempts only flight from needing a ship, so swimming currently decides
nothing; it should either be used here or deleted.

## Dependencies / Links

- Main issue: #1
- Out of scope of: #8
