title: Import lots of reports
description:
There are plenty of old Borg reports that could be imported to the code base to potentially be used for testing. This issue should cover importing them into the code base in a structured way and they should be used by later issues.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Borg reports are committed under a documented location in the repository.
- File naming encodes game, faction and turn so a test can select a report without opening it.
- A short document records where the reports came from and what they may be used for.
design:
## Context

Four real reports are committed under `tests/fixtures/reports/` and 43 references across 30 source
files depend on them. They are the reason this parser is tested against real text at all — but they
are all one ruleset, two factions and three turns, so a whole class of shapes has no fixture: a
fresh faction's first turn, a report with no orders template, two factions of the same game in the
same turn, a late-game report twice the size of anything committed.

The archive exists. Surveyed at `~/Documents/Atlantis`: **209 reports, ~20 MB**, in eight
game/faction runs.

| game | faction | files | turns | size | longest run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 42 | 1 | 0 | — | 1 |
| 3 | 42 | 82 | 1–82 | 12.7 MB | 82 |
| 4 | 17 | 2 | 0–1 | — | 2 |
| 4 | 35 | 1 | 0 | — | 1 |
| 5 | 21 | 38 | 0–39 | 2.9 MB | 22 |
| 7 | 39 | 2 | 17–18 | 0.2 MB | 2 |
| 7 | 62 | 30 | 0–22 | 1.0 MB | 23 |
| 7 | 95 | 52 | 23–74 | 3.9 MB | 38 |

Two findings that shape everything below.

**`v2`…`v7` in the source filenames is the game, not the ruleset.** Every report in the archive
says `NewOrigins, Version: 3.0.0 (beta)` inside; what differs between them is the *engine* version
(5.2.4 and 5.2.5) and the game. So the committed name `neworigins-3.0.0-f95-t71.rep` encodes a
constant and omits the thing that actually varies — and the omission is not academic: faction **42
appears in both game 2 and game 3**.

**201 of the 209 carry an `#atlantis` line with a real faction password**, and this repository is
public.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

- **`tests/fixtures/reports/`** — the documented home already; it stays.
- **Naming: `neworigins-3.0.0-g<game>-f<faction>-t<turn>.rep`.** One `-g<n>` inserted into the
  existing scheme, so a test still selects by ruleset, game, faction and turn without opening a file,
  and the game/faction ambiguity above cannot arise. The four committed files are renamed:
  `…-f95-t70` and `…-f95-t71` become `g7`; `…-f73-t2` and `…-f73-t71` become `g8`.
- **43 references in 30 files** — `crates/core/tests/*.rs`, `crates/core/src/lib.rs:454`,
  `crates/core/src/cache.rs:152`, `crates/core/src/movement/request.rs:275,432`,
  `packages/browser-core/src/parseReportFull.test.ts:14`, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:27-42`.
  Find them with `grep -rn "neworigins-3.0.0"`, excluding `node_modules` and the fixture directory.
- **`tests/fixtures/reports/README.md`** — new; the short document the bead asks for. Provenance,
  the redaction rule, the selection rule, and a table of one row per fixture: game, faction, turn,
  engine version, size, and what it is good for. That last column is the point — it is what stops
  the next person adding a twelfth near-duplicate of turn 71.
- **`scripts/reportFixtures.test.ts`** — new, under `test:tooling`. The repository already tests its
  own configuration this way (`scripts/cargoTargetDir.test.ts` over `.cargo/config.toml`); these are
  the two invariants that matter, and one of them is a secret.
- **Redaction** is one substitution: the quoted value on the `#atlantis <id> "…"` line becomes
  `<password>`, exactly as the four existing fixtures already have it. Everything else stays
  verbatim — faction names, allies and units are already public to everyone in that game, and
  scrubbing them would destroy what the fixtures are for. Confirmed with the navigator.

## The curated set

~23 new files, about 1.5 MB, chosen so that every row earns its place. The rule, which goes in the
README, is: *a fixture is added only for a shape no committed fixture has.*

**A fresh faction's first turn** — no history, small report, the shape every "empty state" path
meets: `g2 f42 t0`, `g3 f42 t1`, `g4 f17 t0`, `g5 f21 t0`, `g7 f62 t0`, and `g8 f73 t1` (in
`~/Downloads/report-neworigins-v8-73-1.rep`, the sibling of a fixture already committed).

**Three consecutive turns** — for anything comparing a turn against the one before, which nothing
committed can currently test: `g3 f42 t40–t42`, `g5 f21 t20–t22`, and `g7 f95 t72` completing the
run with the two already committed.

**A late, large turn** — the stress case, and the one most likely to expose a quadratic:
`g3 f42 t82`, `g5 f21 t39`, `g7 f95 t74`.

**Two factions of one game in the same turn** — `g7 f39 t17, t18` with `g7 f62 t17, t18`. This is
the merge case done properly: `crates/core/tests/merge_reports.rs` currently merges f95 with f73,
which are different games entirely. Note f62 (turns 0–22) and f95 (turns 23–74) never overlap, so
f39/f62 is the only genuine same-game pair the archive offers.

**A report with no orders template** — `g7 f62 t20`, the `noorders` variant, which pins
`ordersTemplate: null` against real text rather than a hand-cut file.

## Increments

1. **The naming rule, before any import.** RED: `every fixture names its game` in
   `scripts/reportFixtures.test.ts` — it fails on all four committed files. GREEN: `git mv` the four
   and update the 43 references. Keep this as its own commit: a pure rename is trivial to rebase,
   and two other planned beads touch `parse_real_reports.rs`.
2. **The secret guard.** RED: `no fixture carries a password` — passes immediately on the four
   redacted files, and that is fine; it is written now so it is watching before anything new lands.
   Say so in the commit rather than manufacturing a failure.
3. **The import.** Copy, redact and rename the curated set. The guard from increment 2 is what
   proves the redaction actually happened, on every file, every run.
4. **The document.** `tests/fixtures/reports/README.md`, with the table and the selection rule.

## The test plan

Suites: `pnpm run test:tooling` for the new guards, then `cargo test --workspace` and
`pnpm -r run test` because increment 1 touches 30 files that read fixtures, and
`pnpm run test:smoke` because `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:27-42` names four of them.

`scripts/reportFixtures.test.ts`:
- `every fixture names its ruleset, game, faction and turn` — every `*.rep` in the directory matches
  `neworigins-<version>-g<n>-f<n>-t<n>.rep`. This is the acceptance criterion, stated as a test.
- `no fixture carries a password` — for every `#atlantis <id> "…"` line in every fixture, the quoted
  value is exactly `<password>`. **The failure message names the file and nothing else** — a test
  that helpfully prints the offending line writes the secret into CI logs, which is the accident it
  exists to prevent.
- `every fixture is listed in the README` — one row per file, so the table cannot drift from the
  directory. Match on the filename appearing in `README.md`; do not try to parse the table.
- `no fixture is a duplicate` — same game, faction and turn twice, which is what an import run
  repeated by mistake produces.

`crates/core/tests/parse_real_reports.rs` — one assertion per newly interesting shape, so a fixture
that is committed and never read is caught by review rather than sitting there for a year:
- the first-turn report parses with a faction, a turn number and at least one region;
- the `noorders` report parses with `orders_template` empty and everything else intact;
- the late `g3 f42 t82` report parses, as the largest thing the parser has ever been handed.

Nothing else needs a test in this bead. It is fixtures; the beads that use them bring their own.

## User-facing decisions

**Asked**, because neither answer was mine to assume:

- *How much of the archive to commit.* The navigator chose **a curated set of roughly 20–30 files**,
  over committing all 209 (~20 MB, paid by every clone and every CI checkout, permanently, since git
  keeps it even if pruned later) and over moving the archive to git-lfs or a second repository.
- *What to redact.* **The password only**, exactly as the four existing fixtures do. Faction names,
  allies and unit names stay verbatim.

No mockup: nothing here is drawn, and the application does not change.

## Out of scope

- Any use of the new fixtures. Later beads do that; this one only makes them available. The three
  parse assertions in the test plan are the minimum to prove the files are readable, not a coverage
  push.
- The 180-odd reports not selected. They stay where they are; the README says where, and the
  selection rule says what would earn one a place later.
- Any change to the parser. If a newly imported report does not parse, that is a finding to raise as
  its own bug bead — do not fix the parser here and do not quietly drop the file that exposed it.
- Reports from other rulesets. The whole archive is NewOrigins 3.0.0.
- A fixture-generation script. Copying 23 files once does not earn a tool.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run test:tooling
cargo test --workspace
pnpm -r run test
pnpm run test:smoke
pnpm run check
```

And the size, stated in the PR, because it is the cost the navigator agreed to:

```bash
du -sh tests/fixtures/reports
git count-objects -vH        # before and after
```

If the added weight comes out much above 3 MB, drop the largest fixtures whose shape is already
covered rather than merging over the number.

Human-only: read the README table against the directory once, by eye. A row that says a file is good
for something it is not is worse than no row.

## Known traps

- **The passwords are real, and the repository is public.** Redact before `git add`, never after —
  a password committed and then removed is still in the history for ever, and the only remedy is
  rewriting a published branch. Check `git diff --cached` for `#atlantis` before the first commit of
  increment 3. Do not paste a report's `#atlantis` line into a commit message, a PR body, a bead, or
  a test failure.
- **Faction 42 exists in two different games.** Any scheme without the game in it is ambiguous
  today, not hypothetically — which is the whole reason for increment 1.
- **`v7` is the game, `3.0.0` is the ruleset.** Reading the source filename as a version and copying
  it into the new name would encode the same constant twice and still omit the game.
- **The rename touches 30 files, two of which other planned beads are also editing** —
  `parse_real_reports.rs` is edited by ah-vp3.1 and ah-1is.1. Land increment 1 as its own commit and
  get this bead merged promptly; a pure rename rebases cleanly, a rename tangled up with an import
  does not.
- **Some source names carry spaces and duplicate markers** — `report-neworigins-v7-95-40 (1).rep`,
  `report-neworigins-v7-62-21 - noorders.rep`. Quote paths, and check which of a `(1)` pair is
  actually wanted rather than trusting the suffix.
- **There is no `.gitattributes`.** The archive and the committed fixtures are all LF today, so
  nothing needs doing — but if a future report arrives with CRLF, `text=auto` normalisation would
  silently rewrite bytes that tests assert on. If one turns up, convert it deliberately and say so
  in the README rather than letting git decide.
- **Do not `git checkout main`** — another agent usually holds it in a worktree. Branch from
  `origin/main` after `git fetch origin main`.

title: Turn-to-turn diffs for units, regions, and orders
description:
## Summary

Compare two imported turns of a game and see what changed: units gained/lost/moved, region changes, and how the orders differ.

## Problem

The app keeps every imported turn in storage, but the player can only ever look at the latest one. Between turns the real questions are "what changed since last month?" and "what did I order last time?" — today that means opening two report text files side by side.

## Scope

- An API to enumerate the imported turns of a game (`listImportedTurns` through core-persistence, the WASM and Tauri adapters, and the shared `CoreClient`), since today only "a known turn number" or "latest" can be loaded.
- Loading a second turn alongside the current one for comparison (the app currently holds exactly one parsed report in memory).
- A diff view for a chosen turn pair surfacing adds/removes/changes for units, regions, and orders.

## Out of scope

- Diffing more than two turns at once, or cross-game comparison.
- Changes to report parsing or order validation.

## Acceptance criteria

- The user can pick two imported turns of the current game.
- The diff view lists units added, removed, and changed between the pair.
- The diff view lists region changes between the pair.
- The diff view shows how the orders drafts differ between the pair.

## Validation

- Import two consecutive turn reports with known differences; open the diff view and verify each known difference is surfaced and nothing is falsely reported.
- Vitest coverage for the diff computation modules; a Playwright smoke walk of the diff view on both web and desktop-shell projects.

## Dependencies / Links

- Broken out of issue 9 (Productivity UX), where it was originally a scope bullet; deferred to its own deliverable.
- Storage substrate already exists: `imported_turns` table keyed by game/faction/turn in `crates/core-persistence`.
